courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, BUSI 408 and BUSI 585.

courses.title: People Analytics
courses.description: This course introduces students to major topics in People Analytics and how using a data-driven human capital strategy can improve organizational performance (e.g., revenue, stock price, customer satisfaction, retention, etc.) and sustain competitive advantage. In this course students will exercise critical thinking skills by analyzing how managers apply human capital strategies in practice. Development of skills in problem solving, creative thinking, written and oral communication, are the main objectives of this course.

courses.title: Strategic Innovation
courses.description: This course is designed for undergraduate business students interested in innovation and entrepreneurship inside established firms. It focuses on the art of bringing novel ideas and products to market while working inside a company. This course will help you understand the barriers to innovation inside existing firms, learn the tools and techniques for overcoming these, and develop an entrepreneurial mindset.

courses.title: Consulting Skills and Frameworks
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. The course is dedicated to teaching the core skills for success in consulting and business in general: teamwork, analysis, and presentations. Honors version available.

courses.title: Groups and Teams in Organizations
courses.description: Examines the design, management, and leadership of teams in organizational settings. Focus is on the interpersonal processes and structural characteristics that influence the effectiveness of teams, individual behavior in face-to-face interactions, and the dynamics of interpersonal relationships.

courses.title: Thinking Creatively: Cognitive Tools for Individuals and Teams
courses.description: This course blends insights from cognitive and organizational psychology to nurture creativity as a process and develop applied skills. Students will learn to recognize the need for creativity, change their own thinking, and foster creativity in teams and organizations. It operates on the assumptions that creative thinking is essential across professions, creativity is a learnable skill, and it complements domain expertise and analytical skills. The course emphasizes experiential learning through exercises, simulations, and discussions.

courses.title: Digital Marketing
courses.description: The main concepts of marketing are identifying market opportunity (3C analysis), setting the target strategy (STP analysis) and implementation via 4P strategies. This course will discuss online consumer behavior; internet marketing strategy; online and digital advertising; social media. It will focus on strategic perspective, rather than on technical details.

courses.title: Product Management
courses.description: Product managers oversee innovation, development, and profit generation. Their roles, previously dispersed, now integrate various functions for better coordination. This course equips you with analytical and creative skills essential for modern product management. Professors with research expertise cover topics including customer insights, product-market fit, and growth strategies. Emphasis is on practical frameworks.

courses.title: Consumer Behavior
courses.description: A business's success relies on fulfilling its consumers' wants and needs, but how does a business effectively do this? This course blends theory with practice to explore how consumers' information processing, decision making, and purchase decisions are influenced by such factors as their values, psychological motivations, and social and cultural forces. In doing so, a deeper understanding of how to target and reach consumers, as well as how to influence their behavior is learned.

courses.title: Retail and E-tail Marketing
courses.description: Retail is ever-evolving as consumer finances, preferences, and tastes shift. Retailers innovate to attract and retain customers, while management competence influences success. This course explores how retailers drive foot traffic, convert shoppers into customers, and enhance competitiveness. We examine the retailer's role as the link between the channel and consumers, analyze internal and external environments, and assess key management practices, including finances, inventory, location, and personnel. Through these topics, students will gain insights into effective retail strategies and operations in a dynamic market.

courses.title: Design Thinking and Product Development
courses.description: Traditional marketing research (focus groups, surveys) is being complemented by design thinking and Web 2.0 approaches. This course will introduce several tools and techniques that are used in the design thinking process (empathy, define, ideate, prototype, test). A sampling of topics includes: creativity and brainstorming, empathy maps, personas, journey mapping, mind mapping, prototyping, storyboarding, intellectual property basics, and open innovation (crowdsourcing/crowdfunding). Key concepts will be learned via several in and out of class hands-on exercises.

courses.title: Marketing Research Design and Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to research methodology with emphasis on the compilation, analysis, and interpretation of data used in the planning and control of marketing operations.

courses.title: Marketing Strategy: Sustainable Competitive Advantage in Dynamic Environments
courses.description: This course addresses all aspects of a firm's overall strategy, from market selection to prioritization to marketing tactics. The flow of the course mirrors the strategic and tactical development processes that are used in practice with companies today: Choice of Markets; Choice of Customers and Discovery of Deep-Seated Customer Needs; and, on the Ground Strategic Execution. Course material will be reinforced through a course-long group project that requires integration and application of course principles.

courses.title: Customer Journeys
courses.description: This course covers state-of-art tactics, concepts, and tools of customer lifecycle marketing, which is the business process of (1) selecting customers that a firm can most profitably serve, and (2) shaping interactions between a company and these customers. This customer journeys framework consists of the design, implementation, and analysis of strategic initiatives including identifying and undertaking profitable customer acquisition; understanding the drivers of attrition and retention; and data-driven attribution of marketing actions and product decisions.

courses.title: Customer Insights and Analytics
courses.description: Over the last 20-30 years, the way information and data have been collected and analyzed has undergone a substantial transformation. Firms have adopted marketing methods that are grounded in economic theory and utilize detailed data on customer transactions to generate insights into how customers behave. This course will provide students with a basic understanding of how to use data to understand customer behavior, and how these insights can be used to make managerially relevant decisions.

courses.title: Strategic Cost Analysis and Performance Management
courses.description: The objective of the course is to develop an understanding of the powerful role of strategic cost analysis and performance measurement in supporting decision-making, performance management and incentive alignment in a timely, efficient and effective manner. The course is intended as an introduction for individuals who will make business decisions, evaluate business units, and evaluate others through the use of cost and performance measurement systems.

courses.title: Taxes and Business Strategy
courses.description: This course covers high-level topics related to tax planning that are relevant to future CEOs, CFOs, investment bankers, equity analysts, and marketing consultants. In this course, students will understand how taxes interact with other fields such as finance, accounting, law, marketing, human resources and compensation, operation management, risk management, etc.

courses.title: Financial Statement Analysis and Valuation
courses.description: This course teaches students how to analyze financial statements so they will better understand firms' business decisions and strategies, sensibly forecast firms' financial statements, and sensibly value firms' equity. Using practical and interactive cases, plus mini-lectures, the goals are to teach students to: appreciate accruals and deferrals in accrual accounting vs. cash accounting; analyze earnings management, firm financial performance, revenues, expenses, assets, liabilities and equity.

courses.title: Applied Impact Investing
courses.description: Applied Impact Investing introduces students to early-stage venture capital and angel investing with a focus on generating both financial returns and measurable social or environmental impact. The course covers core investment processes - sourcing, screening, valuation, due diligence, deal execution, and exit strategies - while integrating impact frameworks such as the UN SDGs and Global Impact Investing Network standards. Students will learn to evaluate startups for commercial viability and impact outcomes, apply sustainability metrics, and make real-world investment decisions alongside a syndicate of investors, gaining practical experience in impact-driven venture capital.

courses.title: Projects for Investment Management Experiential-Learning
courses.description: This course offers experiential learning in investment management through action-based projects with partner firms and weekly seminars. It focuses on preparing students for summer internships and full-time opportunities, tailored to individual career goals. Students will engage in peer learning, project discussions, and interact with guest speakers to connect theory with practice. The instructor will mentor students in both group and individual sessions, offering career guidance and connecting them with field experts. The course structure will evolve with student input, ensuring relevant and personalized content. Application required.

courses.title: Investments
courses.description: A survey of investment principles and practices. Emphasis is given to the problems of security analysis and portfolio management with special attention to the investment problems of the individual investor. Honors version available.

courses.title: Financial Modeling for Leveraged Buyout Transactions
courses.description: This course teaches students how to weave their forecasts into coherent spreadsheet-based, pro-forma financials. The main goal of this course is to illustrate how a practitioner would analyze a leveraged buyout. Students will construct their own LBO model in Excel and, by the end of the course, should feel comfortable assessing a company and determining if it is a viable LBO candidate.

courses.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
courses.description: Through lectures, case studies, and guest speakers, this course will cover all aspects of mergers and acquisitions from strategy to post-merger integration with an emphasis on valuation. Related activities such as hostile takeovers, private equity deals, and international acquisitions will also be discussed. Honors version available.

courses.title: Applied Investment Management
courses.description: Permission of the department. Year-long course. A live, student-managed investment fund with real dollars and fiduciary responsibility to the UNC Foundation. Emphasis is on the decisions that must be made by and/or for the ultimate investor and the analytic tools and empirical evidence that can help inform such decisions. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Financial Modeling
courses.description: Skill development in constructing financial models for analyzing problems with decisions faced by financial professionals. Analyzing historical performance, forecasting free cash flows, estimating discount rates, determining terminal value, identifying other sources of value, and interpreting results in a dynamic setting.

courses.title: Introduction to Real Estate
courses.description: An overview of residential and commercial real estate. This survey course examines 1) buying a house and constructing a portfolio of single-family rental houses, 2) commercial real estate product types, 3) amortization, cash flows, capital expenditures, cap rates, debt and equity, hurdle rates and taxes, 4) investment analysis, 5) acquisition, development, operation, and disposition, 6) real estate and contract law, and 7) the partnership negotiation process.

courses.title: Personal Finance
courses.description: Introduces and broadens the concept of personal finance and increases understanding of the process of accumulating and protecting personal wealth. Students learn to identify and analyze risk and return relationships, understand investment alternatives and how strategies develop as life situations mature, and gain understanding of retirement planning and effectively transferring wealth.

courses.title: Investment Banking
courses.description: This course prepares students for investment banking positions and internships. The focus of the class is on financial modeling, general knowledge of banking, and what it takes to succeed in the industry. Permission of the instructor and confirmed offer of investment banking analyst internship or full-time job. Honors version available.

courses.title: Introduction to Derivative Securities and Risk Management
courses.description: Introduction to derivative securities instruments (options and futures) and applications in investments and corporate finance. Honors version available.

courses.title: Fixed Income
courses.description: The course covers traditional bonds and term structure concepts as well as fixed income derivatives and interest rate modeling. Honors version available.

courses.title: Business Seminar
courses.description: Selected topics in business administration presented in seminar format with students engaged in individual and team study under the supervision of a member of the faculty. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Applied Private Equity: Real Estate
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course explores, at a very advanced level, all stages of the management of a real estate private equity fund: from capital formation, deal sourcing, due diligence, monitoring and adding value, and exiting of the fund's real estate holdings.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Sustainable Finance
courses.description: The transition toward a sustainable and inclusive economy faces multiple challenges with economic, environmental, and social implications. This introductory course explores how finance interacts with sustainability issues and its leading role in such transition. We will cover key economic and financial concepts and develop relevant knowledge and critical thinking on topics such as: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing; the financing of sustainable projects; real and financial implications of climate risk.

courses.title: Alternative Investments
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Open to seniors only. Exposes students to the benefits, opportunities, and risks of incorporating alternative investments into managed institutional investment portfolios, including pension funds, endowments, and foundations.

courses.title: Risk Management
courses.description: Develops methods for applied analysis of financial and operational risk. The course covers statistical methods of risk measurement such as value-at-risk. In addition, the course covers methods for designing and evaluating risk management procedures at both financial and non-financial companies. The course includes several guest lectures from senior managers.

courses.title: Real Estate Finance
courses.description: This course will focus on the different ways to finance real property, and how different financing techniques impact the feasibility and investment benefits for equity investors. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, BUSI 408 and BUSI 585.

courses.title: Strategic Economics
courses.description: This course focuses on decision making in the presence of strategic interaction. Students will apply game theory to yield insights into business decisions. Topics covered include pricing, entry, product market competition, first-mover advantage, capital budgeting, antitrust law, corporate governance, auctions, and mergers.

courses.title: Real Estate Development
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce undergraduate students to the financial and economic analysis of real estate development. The course will focus on both the physical and financial dimensions of the real estate development process. The course considers multiple asset classes, and students learn to complete financial analysis of real estate development projects.

courses.title: Real Estate and Capital Markets
courses.description: Introduces students to the capital markets for financing real estate assets. Topics include an overview of real estate as an asset class in the US economy, risk and return in real estate markets, the economics of discount and capitalization rates, the market for mortgage-backed securities (with a peek into the role that these instruments played in the recent financial crisis), and the valuation/analysis of Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs). Honors version available.

courses.title: Real Estate Capstone
courses.description: Case-based course covering a broad range of real estate issues. The cases studied focus on investment decisions made by practitioners in the industry, and will include investment feasibility and valuation, financing projects, leasing, development, individual and private equity structures, etc. This course is designed to allow students to utilize all prior real estate coursework in a practical manner. Offered to seniors completing the real estate minor or BSBA area of emphasis.

courses.title: Buyout Structures and Deals
courses.description: It improves students' understanding of how private equity firms evaluate risk/reward, create value in LBO transactions, and explores the role of private equity in the financial markets and corporate boardroom. Students will develop a better understanding of the decisions private equity firms face; covering challenges in going-private and private-to-private transactions, use of leveraged finance for LBOs and dividend recapitalizations.

courses.title: Inside the Capital Markets - Institutions, Players and Regulators
courses.description: This course provides a broad overview of the U.S. and global capital markets. It explores how the markets work, market participants (e.g. mutual funds, hedge funds, investment banks, and venture capital funds), and the infrastructure that supports the industry. Students will follow a "day in the life" of a trade and gain an understanding of the various systems and investment roles and responsibilities. The course will also provide an overview of investing in foreign markets.

courses.title: Introduction to FinTech - Blockchain Technologies and Cryptocurrencies
courses.description: This course is an introduction to FinTech, helping students to understand recent advances in blockchain technologies and cryptocurrencies. Topics include: Bitcoin and blockchain, Ethereum and smart contracts, fork, initial coin offerings (ICOs), cryptocurrency trading, blockchain industries, issues in the cryptocurrency market (e.g. market manipulation and regulations), and decentralized finance and the future of finance. Recommended preparation, BUSI 408.

courses.title: Global Environment of Business
courses.description: Issues in operating overseas, including analyses of differences in country settings, legal and economic systems, and governmental policies affecting foreign operations. Studies trade theory, country groupings, and financial issues; managing operations in foreign lands; exporting.

courses.title: Business and Global Development
courses.description: This course explores the pivotal role of businesses in tackling Global development challenges. Through four thematic modules - business and government, human development, market development, and the environment - students examine how firms interact with institutions, people, markets, and resources to foster growth. Integrating regional perspectives and current events, the course develops students' ability to analyze business strategies in emerging economies, apply theoretical frameworks to real cases, and evaluate the impact of trade, innovation, and sustainability on global development outcomes. Students actively engage in case studies and discussions for practical learning.

courses.title: Global Financial Markets
courses.description: Develops the foundation for financial decisions in a global economic environment. Extends the analytical concepts and tools learned in introductory investment and corporate finance courses to multicountry/multicurrency settings. Covers three major areas: the economics of exchange rates, international money and capital markets, and international corporate finance.

courses.title: Global Healthcare Management
courses.description: This course will provide students with an overview of numerous global healthcare topics. Students will learn about macro global healthcare issues, country-specific healthcare systems, healthcare interdependencies between regions and countries, global healthcare business strategies and solutions. The course will examine innovative global business models focused on analyzing the cost, access, and quality of healthcare around the globe.

courses.title: Introduction to Healthcare Management
courses.description: An overview of the dynamics of leading/managing a modern-day hospital/health system and of the US healthcare system including its characteristics/dynamics, structure and operation, how it has evolved over time, and how it may further evolve. It engages students in examining the major economic, political, technological, and social trends driving the US healthcare system, and the implications of those trends in the strategic leadership and operational management of hospitals/health systems.

courses.title: Healthcare Brand Plan
courses.description: This course will provide students with the skills and ability to effectively create and evaluate a brand plan in the healthcare industry. Students will learn the components of a brand plan and what is unique to a brand plan in healthcare. The course examines best practices from the pharma industry, how to evaluate and assess brand plans, and the difference between a launch plan and an existing brand plan. It will conclude with the development and presentation of a brand plan for an actual brand in the healthcare space. Sponsored company executives actively participate in the final brand plan presentations.

courses.title: Business of Health Capstone
courses.description: This capstone course for Business of Health Minors, integrates knowledge from business, public health, organizational behavior, and ethics to address a pressing real-world challenge: the adoption of artificial intelligence in healthcare. Students apply interdisciplinary frameworks to assess risks, benefits, governance, and stakeholder impacts of emerging AI technologies in large health systems. Students identify AI solutions, evaluate unintended consequences, and develop actionable business cases. The course culminates in final team presentations, where students pitch their recommendations to leaders at UNC Health, bridging academic insight with real-world healthcare innovation.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, BUSI 510, HPM 300; Pre- or corequisite, BUSI 411.

courses.title: Applied Learning: Symposium Core Committee
courses.description: Permission of the department. This course is by invitation only to students who previously served on the Undergraduate Business Symposium core committee. As senior advisors, students practice the leadership, organization, delegation, communication, and teamwork skills that they learn about in their other courses.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Applied Trading Strategies
courses.description: This seminar style course develops a set of financial tools useful for trading primary and derivative securities with the goal of obtaining specific exposures in equity, fixed income, and commodity markets. The course examines methods for managing financial price risk of positions and how hedge funds use derivatives in practice. Honors version available.

courses.title: Honors Research Proposal
courses.description: Permission of the department. Open to senior business administration majors with a minimum 3.5 grade point average in business courses. Students learn business research techniques and develop individual proposals for business research. Successful proposals may advance to honors thesis research and writing (BUSI 692H).

courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: Permission of the department. Open to senior business majors with a minimum 3.5 grade point average in business courses. Original investigation of a topic in business and preparation of a substantive research project under the direction of a faculty advisor. Written essay and oral presentation are required.

courses.title: Artistic Entrepreneurship
courses.description: This course is a study in entrepreneurship and the specific challenges faced by artistic entrepreneurs.

courses.title: Introduction to Social Entrepreneurship
courses.description: An overview of how entrepreneurship is transforming students' fields and disciplines and how the application of principles of entrepreneurship may be used to advance their professional objectives.

courses.title: Introduction to Commercial Entrepreneurship
courses.description: A cross-disciplinary curriculum that brings together the core field with the wide-ranging literature in entrepreneurship to seek new approaches to traditional problems.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship Capstone
courses.description: Capstone project, business plan, or paper that links the work done in the certificate to the field it is intended to complement.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship Capstone Project
courses.description: This Graduate Certificate in Entrepreneurship capstone project is self-paced, and overseen by the faculty director of each track (life sciences, public health, and artistic).

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study intends to extend a student's learning beyond the classroom or allows a student the opportunity to explore a topic not offered in a traditional format.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Applied Research Methods I
courses.description: Addresses fundamentals of empirical social science research. Topics include framing a research question, comparing research designs, instrumentation, reliability, validity, and exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis. Emphasizes application and analysis.

courses.title: Applied Research Methods II
courses.description: Continuation of BUSI 808. Topics include statistical control, categorical variables, interaction, curvilinear and similarity effects, longitudinal analysis, path analysis, structural equation modeling, and publication. Emphasizes application and analysis.

courses.title: Empirical Operations
courses.description: Required preparation, working knowledge of probability, statistics, and regression. The course prepares students to perform academic research, and it will be conducted in a manner that simulates an academic research conference. The course will focus on empirical research approaches used in solving many classical problems in operations management.

courses.title: Theory of Operations Management I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Rigorous study of traditional and modern issues, problems, and approaches in operations management.

courses.title: Theory of Operations Management II
courses.description: A continuation of BUSI 830.

courses.title: Theory of Operations Management III
courses.description: A continuation of BUSI 830.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Operations Management
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive study of a specific area in operations management.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Seminar in Operations Management
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive study of a specific area in operations management.

courses.title: Individual Behavior in Organizations
courses.description: Analysis of individual behavior, adjustment, and effectiveness. Examination of attitudes, stress, problem solving, decision making, motivation, and personality. Applications to management of human resources.

courses.title: Interpersonal and Intergroup Behavior in Business Organizations
courses.description: Intensive critical examination of interpersonal and intergroup behavior, including decision processes, communication, conflict, and conflict resolution in large organizations.

courses.title: Macro Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Graduate standing in business administration required. Intensive study of theory and research in organizational structure, coordinating and control mechanisms, design parameters, and environments.

courses.title: Organizational Design and Development
courses.description: The development of understanding and skills in changing and evolving organizational design, interpersonal relationships, and people to achieve organizational goals.

courses.title: Seminar in Organizational Behavior
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Intensive study of important current theory and research in organizational behavior.

courses.title: Seminar in Human Resource Management
courses.description: Review the research literature on how firms are made more effective through their people. Coverage includes topics like recruitment, hiring, compensation, socialization, culture, and performance management.

courses.title: Special Topics in Organizational Behavior
courses.description: BUSI 858 is a second doctoral course in organizational behavior, meant to be taken after completing BUSI 851: Individual Behavior in Organizations. While BUSI 851 gave an overview of many important topics in organizational behavior, the field is too broad to be covered, in depth, with a single class. The goal of this course is to introduce developing scholars to the history and current status of important topics in organizational behavior. This course is intended for developing scholars who intend to pursue academic careers.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Seminar in Marketing I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Overview of current paradigms and research in marketing. Topics include philosophy of science, differing views of what marketing is, strengths and weaknesses of various research approaches, and career socialization issues.

courses.title: Seminar in Marketing II
courses.description: Intensive study of the empirical and analytical literature involving problems in pricing, product development and management, advertising and promotion, distribution, and strategy.

courses.title: Marketing Models
courses.description: This class covers a range of econometric principles and models of relevance to marketing. The emphasis will be on model formulation and estimation.

courses.title: Seminar in Current Marketing Topics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced research in marketing. A seminar to discuss current research of doctoral candidates, faculty, and invited guests.

courses.title: Issues in the Design and Analysis of Research in Marketing
courses.description: Graduate standing in business administration required. A review of major issues in marketing, including philosophy of science, measurement, and experimental and quasi-experimental design.

courses.title: Seminar in Marketing Research Methodology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An introduction to multivariate data analysis methods including factor analysis, cluster analysis, logic, discriminant analysis and multidimensional scaling.

courses.title: Seminar in Research in Accounting
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An informal seminar to discuss current research in accounting.

courses.title: Financial Economics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Introduction to the theories of asset pricing.

courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.description: Introduction to corporate finance theory.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, BUSI 880; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Empirical Corporate Finance
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. An introduction to the empirical corporate finance literature.

courses.title: Seminar in Research in Finance
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced research in business finance and investment. An informal seminar to discuss current research of doctoral candidates, faculty, and others.

courses.title: Introduction to Empirical Finance
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the quantitative methods used in empirical asset pricing. Model specification and estimation issues are discussed at length. The course emphasizes both theoretical and practical research.

courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Finance
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Review of information generating and optimizing models and their applicability to decision making in finance.

courses.title: Seminar in Financial Markets
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced methods in finance.

courses.title: Strategic Management Overview
courses.description: A seminar to provide a broad and current understanding of strategic management. Exposure to the entire field is emphasized.

courses.title: Strategic Formulation
courses.description: This seminar emphasizes both process and content issues to provide students with an in-depth understanding of strategy formulation topics.

courses.title: Strategy Implementation
courses.description: This seminar focuses on strategy implementation, with particular emphasis devoted to the process, systems, and structures required for effective implementation.

courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Individual research in a special field under direction of a member of the department
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Individual research in a special field under direction of a member of the department.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Elementary Catalan
courses.description: Introduction to Catalan language and culture. Designed for students who already have proficiency in another foreign language.

courses.title: Intermediate Catalan
courses.description: Continuation of Catalan 401 with more emphasis on reading authentic texts.

courses.title: Biochemical Foundations of Chemical Biology
courses.description: This course is designed to emphasize the elements of biochemistry, bioorganic chemistry, and molecular biology required for the design and synthesis of biologically-active compounds.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 466, BIOC 505 or 601, and PHCO 643; Permission of instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Biochemical Foundations of Chemical Biology Journal Club
courses.description: This is a seminar based course that will run in concert with 804A. Students will present journal articles and interact with seminar speakers.
courses.requisites: Co-requisite, CBMC 804A; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the co-requisite.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Molecular Modeling
courses.description: Introduction to computer-assisted molecular design, techniques, and theory with an emphasis on the practical use of molecular mechanics and quantum mechanics programs.

courses.title: Foundations of Chemical Biology I: Organic and Medicinal Chemistry
courses.description: The elements of organic chemistry required for the design and synthesis of chemical probes and biologically active compounds.

courses.title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
courses.description: This grant writing course is an elective, 2-credit class for second-year graduate students who have selected labs for their dissertation work. The course aims to help students develop grant writing skills through 1) classroom instruction, 2) reading and critiquing grant applications, 3) writing a draft grant proposal, and 4) responding to critiques and revising the proposal. Although this is an elective course, one needs to be aware that serious commitment is essential to success as most writing and reading are done outside classes.

courses.title: The Cellular Agriculture Revolution
courses.description: Learn the foundational biological and chemical processes used to produce cultivated meat. Lectures will cover state-of-the-art techniques for cultivated meat production and will allow you to think critically about the future of food. Weekly guest speakers will expose students to innovative startups and academic researchers establishing a new paradigm for manufacturing sustainable commodity meat products. The course will also introduce the environmental, ethical, and economic drivers behind the mission of alternative protein science and technology.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, BIOL 101 and BIOL 101L; and either BIOL 103 or BIOL 205; or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: MiBio Seminar
courses.description: This class is designed to 1) enhance students' ability to present scientific material to their peers in a comprehensive, cohesive manner, 2) familiarize students with scientific concepts and technologies used in multiple disciplines, 3) expose students to cutting edge research, 4) prepare students to gain substantial meaning from seminars and to ask questions, and 5) enhance students' ability to evaluate scientific papers and seminars.

courses.title: Improving Presentation & Communication of Scientific Results
courses.description: Learning modern day techniques and approaches to convey scientific results effectively as a public speaker. Teaching how to implement the key aspects of effective presentation of scientific findings in public settings. Understanding the key components of an effective public talk including scientific content, body language, and voice. Learning how to captivate the target audience and yet still convey data driven scientific findings.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Communicating Scientific Results
courses.description: Practice in oral and written communication evaluated by peers and faculty. Includes delivery of coached presentations on topics in physiology and preparation of writing assignments typically encountered in scientific life.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Advanced Light Microscopy
courses.description: An intensive and comprehensive hands-on laboratory-oriented course in light microscopy for researchers in biology, medicine, and materials science. This course will focus on advanced quantitative fluorescence microscopy techniques used for imaging a range of biological specimens, from whole organisms, to tissues, to cells, and to single molecules. This course emphasizes the quantitative issues that are critical to the proper interpretation of images obtained with light microscopes.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Quantitative Image Analysis for Light Microscopy
courses.description: This course is a practical introduction to quantitative analysis of light microscopy images. During the class students will follow tutorials that will guide them through common tasks in analysis of biological images. They will be introduced to basic concepts of image processing like image registration, filtering, object detection etc.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Anatomy
courses.description: A general course for persons preparing for careers as dental hygienists. Two lectures and two laboratory hours a week.

courses.title: Gross Anatomy for Physical Therapists
courses.description: Fundamental principles and concepts of human gross anatomy for physical therapists taught by lectures and cadaver dissection. Emphasis on functional anatomy. Three lecture hours and six laboratory hours a week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, BIOL 474 and 474L; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Functional Neuroanatomy
courses.description: Study of basic structure of the brain and spinal cord, including both lecture and laboratory. Primarily for physical therapy students. Four hours a week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CBIO 607 and CBPH 791; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Seminar in Cell Biology & Physiology
courses.description: Current topics relevant for biomedical sciences students. May be repeated for credit. May be repeated in the same term for different topics.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Human Physiology I
courses.description: Graduate students only. This course provides an overview of the function and regulation of human body systems. Topics include cellular, muscle, neurological, cardiovascular, and respiratory physiology. Emphasis is placed upon mechanisms of integration and control. Permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Human Physiology II
courses.description: Graduate students only. This course provides an in-depth study of renal physiology, gastrointestinal physiology, endocrine physiology, and reproductive physiology. Students will learn physiologic mechanisms in each of these areas at the molecular, cellular, and system levels of organization. Emphasis will be placed on the integrated functions of organ systems.

courses.title: Cell Biology and Physiology in Health and Disease I
courses.description: CBPH 852 provides a broad introduction to cell biology and physiology in the context of human health and disease. Sessions will emphasize the integration of cell biological principles into physiological paradigms, and vise-versa. The course covers fundamental cellular processes such as cell organization, membrane trafficking, protein quality control, cytoskeleton, and cell motility. It also covers the development and function of the nervous and cardiovascular systems, as well as diseases of these organ systems. Journal clubs will enable students to integrate lecture material with published primary research articles (both classic and new studies) that answer important questions using cellular and physiological.

courses.title: Cell Biology and Physiology in Health and Disease II
courses.description: This course is ideal for first- or second-year graduate students with an interest in cell biology and physiology in the context of experimental medicine and translational approaches aimed at understanding and treating human diseases. Sessions will emphasize the integration of cell biological principles into physiological paradigms, and vise-versa. The course covers fundamental cellular processes, such as RNA and protein regulation, cell signaling, cell-cell communication, immune regulation, inflammation and fibrosis. Journal clubs will enable students to integrate lecture material with published primary research articles (both classic and new studies) that answer important questions using cellular and physiological systems to advance translational Permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Career and Research Enhancement Seminar (CaRES)
courses.description: Weekly seminar given by outside investigators from academia or industry; also includes research in progress seminars from current PhD students and their ongoing thesis work. Exposure to modern topics and cutting edge technologies in molecular cell biology and experimental physiology research. Must be an enrolled graduate student. Permission of the director of graduate studies.

courses.title: Career and Research Enhancement Seminar (CaRES)
courses.description: Weekly seminar given by outside investigators from academia or industry; also includes research in progress seminars from current PhD students and their ongoing thesis work. Exposure to modern topics and cutting edge technologies in molecular cell biology and experimental physiology research. Must be an enrolled graduate student. Permission of the director of graduate studies.

courses.title: Special Topics in Cell Biology & Physiology
courses.description: Modern day exploration of topics or methodologies of interest to PhD students in biomedical sciences. New or old relevant technologies/methodologies or subject areas of research, and/or professional skills enhancement will be addressed. This could be either for enhancing knowledge of subject materials or teaching skill sets (e.g., statistics) needed for biomedical researchers.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 5 total credits. 5 total completions.

courses.title: Special Topics in Biomedical Science
courses.description: Elective course in Cell Biology and Physiology offering a series of alternating mini courses. Depending on instructor availability and expertise the student would choose the specific topic course that best aligns with their past educational training and scientific interests and needs. The topic offerings are meant for the typical life science/biology degree postbaccalaureate MS student in health related field. The specific topic offered would vary between Fall and Spring semesters but includes biochemistry, genetics, microbiology/immunology, pharmacology, neuroscience, and research and clinical ethics. For Terminal Masters students in Cell Biology & Physiology.
courses.requisites: Corequisite, graduate student at UNC Chapel Hill.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.title: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
courses.description: Responsible conduct of research is a classroom-based graduate level course covering critical topics for ethical and responsible conduct of experimental research. There are both classroom lecture, workshop-type discussion components, in addition to assigned outside of class readings. Topics include: mentor and mentee relationships, publication authorship, collaboration, peer review, ethical use of human and animal subjects, conflicts of interest, intellectual property, plagiarism, data acquisition, and data processing.

courses.title: Research
courses.description: Credit to be arranged in individual cases.

courses.title: Research Laboratory Apprenticeship
courses.description: Enrollment in the cell biology and anatomy graduate program required. A course for first- and second-year graduate students in cell biology and anatomy, consisting of a research project of limited scope pursued under the supervision of a faculty member.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Research Practicum/Internship in Cell Biology and Physiology
courses.description: The Research Practicum/Internship in Cell Biology and Physiology (CBPH) is a planned, individualized, mentored, evaluated, experiential learning opportunity that serves as a bridge between academic training and post-training practice. The internship/practicum provides special opportunities for learning that are different from, supplementary to, and supportive of the academic components of the PhD program.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, None; Corequisite, None; Pre- or corequisite, None.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 9 total completions.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.description: Master's research for the non-thesis ("thesis substitute") track.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: You Don't Have to Be a Rocket Scientist
courses.description: The goal of this seminar is to develop tools for extracting information from or finding flaws in news reports and popular science writing. Group work on such issues as biomass fuels, the hydrogen economy, and other alternative energy sources will develop an understanding of their economic and environmental impact.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: From Atomic Bombs to Cancer Treatments: The Broad Scope of Nuclear Chemistry
courses.description: A course engaging the topic of nuclear chemistry on the introductory chemistry course level (e.g., CHEM 101/102). Atomic structure, nuclear fission, and nuclear fusion processes will be introduced to provide the background necessary to understand applications of the processes. Applications discussed will include power generation, medical treatments, weapons, and more. Honors version available.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Polymers: How Plastic Changed our World
courses.description: From milk bottles and grocery bags to contact lenses and diapers, polymers influence nearly every aspect of our daily lives. Through hands-on activities, readings, and interactive lessons, we will examine the role polymers have played, both positive and negative, on our society and world.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Bread from Air? The Chemistry of Fertilizers
courses.description: Fear of a global famine inspired chemist Fritz Haber's research into the production of ammonia from nitrogen in the air. Following a breakthrough laboratory discovery, engineer Carl Bosch led the development of a large-scale industrial process to produce ammonia...and together they changed the world. This First-Year Seminar introduces concepts of scientific inquiry and interdisciplinary collaboration in the context of the humankind's utilization of fertilizers.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.title: Foundations of Chemistry
courses.description: This course is an introduction to fundamental threshold concepts in chemistry as preparation for the two-course sequence of General Descriptive Chemistry (CHEM 101 and 102). This course emphasizes developing contextualized algebra skills for solving chemistry problems including physical unit conversions, molar mass, and reaction stoichiometry. Permission of instructor required.

courses.title: General Descriptive Chemistry I
courses.description: The first course in a two-semester sequence. See also CHEM 102. Atomic and molecular structure, intermolecular forces, stoichiometry and conservation of mass, and properties of gases. Honors version available. This course requires evening exams scheduled outside of regular class hours (fall, spring). Please review the class notes for exam times and dates before registering. Honors version available.

courses.title: Quantitative Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Computerized data collection, scientific measurement, basic laboratory skills, spectroscopy, molecular structure and bonding, and intermolecular forces. Laptop computer required. One three-hour laboratory a week.

courses.title: General Descriptive Chemistry II
courses.description: The course is the second in a two-semester sequence. See also CHEM 101. Solutions, thermochemical changes including conservation of energy, thermodynamics, reaction rates, chemical equilibria including acid-base chemistry, and electrochemistry. Honors version available. This course requires evening exams scheduled outside of regular class hours (fall, spring). Please review the class notes for exam times and dates before registering. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 101 and 101L; C- or better required in CHEM 101.

courses.title: Quantitative Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: Computerized data collection, basic laboratory skills, thermochemistry, colligative properties, chemical kinetics, and acid-base titrations. Laptop computer required. One three-hour laboratory a week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 101L; Pre- or corequisite, CHEM 102 or 102H.

courses.title: Special Topics in Chemistry
courses.description: An undergraduate seminar course that is designated to be a participatory intellectual adventure on an advanced, emergent, and stimulating topic within a selected discipline in chemistry. This course does not count as credit towards the chemistry major.

courses.title: Extraordinary Chemistry of Ordinary Things
courses.description: Coregistration in CHEM 200 and 101L fulfills the physical and life science with a laboratory requirement (PX). This course helps students understand the chemistry behind important societal issues and the consequences of actions aimed at addressing the issues. Students who have taken CHEM 200 cannot take CHEM 101 for credit.

courses.title: Service Learning in Chemistry
courses.description: This is an APPLES service-learning course that collaborates with a community partner. Students will develop research questions and test their hypotheses using chemistry lab techniques and instrumentation. Students will keep a reflection journal on their service work and a lab notebook for recording all experimentation. At the end of the semester, students will write a paper and present research posters. Findings will be shared with the community partner. Students must send applications to the instructor.

courses.title: Modern Analytical Methods for Separation and Characterization
courses.description: Analytical separations, chromatographic methods, spectrophotometry, acid-base equilibria and titrations, fundamentals of electrochemistry. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 102 or 102H; C- or better required.

courses.title: Laboratory in Separations and Analytical Characterization of Organic and Biological Compounds
courses.description: Applications of separation and spectrophotometric techniques to organic compounds, including some of biological interest. One three-hour laboratory a week. Students may not receive credit for both CHEM 241L and CHEM 245L.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 102L; pre- or corequisite, CHEM 241 or 241H.

courses.title: Honors Laboratory in Separations and Analytical Characterization of Organic and Biological Compound
courses.description: Applications of separation and spectrophotometric techniques to samples from the real world, including some of biological interest. Final portion of course consists of group research projects presented to the Department of Chemistry in poster session format. Honors equivalent of CHEM 241L. Students may not receive credit for both CHEM 241L and CHEM 245L. One three-hour laboratory each week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 102L; pre- or corequisite, CHEM 241H.

courses.title: Introduction to Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Chemical periodicity, introductory atomic theory and molecular orbital theory, structure and bonding in solids, descriptive nonmetal chemistry, structures and reactions of transition metal complexes, applications of inorganic complexes and materials. This course requires evening exams scheduled outside of regular class hours (fall, spring). Please review the class notes for exam times and dates before registering.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 102 or 102H; C- or better required.

courses.title: Introduction to Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: Molecular structure and its determination by modern physical methods, correlation between structure and reactivity and the theoretical basis for these relationships, classification of reaction types exhibited by organic molecules using as examples molecules of biological importance. This course requires evening exams scheduled outside of regular class hours (fall, spring). Please review the class notes for exam times and dates before registering. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 102 or 102H; C- or better required.

courses.title: Introduction to Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: Continuation of CHEM 261, with particular emphasis on the chemical properties of organic molecules of biological importance. This course requires evening exams scheduled outside of regular class hours (fall, spring). Please review the class notes for exam times and dates before registering. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 261 or 261H; C- or better required.

courses.title: Laboratory in Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Continuation of CHEM 241L or 245L with particular emphasis on organic chemistry synthesis protocols, separation techniques, and compound characterization using modern spectroscopic instrumentation. This course serves as an organic chemistry laboratory for premedical and predental students. Students may not receive credit for both CHEM 262L and CHEM 263L. One three-hour laboratory each week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 102L, and CHEM 241L or 245L; pre- or corequisite, CHEM 262 or 262H.

courses.title: Special Topics in Chemistry
courses.description: Elective topics in the field of chemistry. This course has variable content and may be taken multiple times for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Teaching Apprentice in Chemistry
courses.description: Experience includes facilitating in-class small group activities and, for an optional additional credit hour, preparing review sessions or supporting weekly recitations. Students will apply concepts in pedagogy, leadership, communication, and group dynamics. Does not fulfill chemistry major requirements. GPA above 3.0 required.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 102 or 102H, and MATH 231; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites; Pre- or corequisite, EDUC 150.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Internship in Chemistry
courses.description: The sponsored, off-campus work must involve at least 135 hours. Does not fulfill any requirement in the chemistry major or minor. Chemistry majors only. Permission of instructor/department

courses.title: Educational and Social Research in Chemistry
courses.description: This class is designed for students interested in pursuing educational or social research related to the field of chemistry under the mentorship of a faculty member in the UNC Department of Chemistry or another department on campus. This course does not count as a chemistry elective in the chemistry major or minor.

courses.title: Research in Chemistry for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent research in the field of chemistry under the supervision of a faculty mentor. Approved learning contract required. Students are encouraged to present their research at an appropriate symposium, conference, or seminar. May count only once as a required advanced chemistry elective. This course is for chemistry majors only. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Special Problems in Chemistry
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Literature or laboratory work equivalent of one to three hours each week. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Honors Colloquium in Chemistry
courses.description: Weekly meetings complement research carried out under CHEM 395H. Expands students' exposure to specialized areas of research through guided readings and seminars with invited speakers. Aids students in preparing their research for evaluation. CHEM 395H and 397H together can contribute no more than nine total hours toward graduation.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Environmental Chemistry Processes
courses.description: Required preparation, a background in chemistry and mathematics, including ordinary differential equations. Chemical processes occurring in natural and engineered systems: chemical cycles; transport and transformation processes of chemicals in air, water, and multimedia environments; chemical dynamics; thermodynamics; structure/activity relationships.

courses.title: Instructional Methods in the Chemistry Classroom
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course explores secondary school chemical education through current chemical education theory and classroom teaching. Students will develop a comprehensive approach to teaching chemistry content through student-centered activities.

courses.title: Introduction to Polymers
courses.description: Chemical structure and nomenclature of macromolecules, synthesis of polymers, characteristic polymer properties. Previously offered as APPL 420.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 261 or 261H; Pre- or corequisites, CHEM 262 or 262H, and 262L or 263L.

courses.title: Synthesis of Polymers
courses.description: Synthesis and reactions of polymers; various polymerization techniques. Previously offered as APPL 421.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymers
courses.description: Polymerization and characterization of macromolecules in solution. Previously offered as APPL 422.

courses.title: Intermediate Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: Polymer dynamics, networks and gels. Previously offered as APPL 423.

courses.title: Polymer Materials
courses.description: Solid-state properties of polymers; polymer melts, glasses and crystals.

courses.title: Introduction to Biological Chemistry
courses.description: The study of cellular processes including catalysts, metabolism, bioenergetics, and biochemical genetics. The structure and function of biological macromolecules involved in these processes is emphasized. Honors version available.

courses.title: Macromolecular Structure and Metabolism
courses.description: Structure of DNA and methods in biotechnology; DNA replication and repair; RNA structure, synthesis, localization and transcriptional reputation; protein structure/function, biosynthesis, modification, localization, and degradation.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 433 and BIOL 220 or BIOL 202.

courses.title: Metabolic Chemistry and Cellular Regulatory Networks
courses.description: Biological membranes, membrane protein structure, transport phenomena; metabolic pathways, reaction themes, regulatory networks; metabolic transformations with carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, and nucleotides; regulatory networks, signal transduction.

courses.title: Introduction to Biochemistry for Majors
courses.description: Chemistry is the scientific study of the composition and properties of matter and the investigation of the laws that govern them. All chemists have a common core of knowledge, learned through a highly structured sequence of undergraduate courses in which the content is divided into the classical subdisciplines. The B.S. chemistry, biochemistry track degree provides students with the opportunity to specialize in biochemistry and chemical biology. This course is for Chemistry or Biology Majors. All other majors require permission from instructor.

courses.title: Intermediate Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Spectroscopy, electroanalytical chemistry, chromatography, thermal methods of analysis, signal processing.

courses.title: Intermediate Analytical Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments in spectroscopy, electroanalytical chemistry, chromatography, thermal methods of analysis, and signal processing. One four-hour laboratory a week and one one-hour lecture.

courses.title: Surface Analysis
courses.description: This class will focus on analytical techniques capable of probing the physical and chemical properties of surfaces and interfaces. These analyses are extremely challenging, as the sample sizes are small (e.g., 1E14 molecules/cm2 of a material). The course will focus on complementary techniques to assess surface structure and topography, atomic and molecular composition, organization or disorder, and reactivity.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 441 or CHEM 481; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Separations
courses.description: Theory and applications of equilibrium and nonequilibrium separation techniques. Extraction, countercurrent distribution, gas chromatography, column and plane chromatographic techniques, electrophoresis, ultra-centrifugation, and other separation methods.

courses.title: Electroanalytical Chemistry
courses.description: Basic principles of electrochemical reactions, electroanalytical voltammetry as applied to analysis, the chemistry of heterogeneous electron transfers, and electrochemical instrumentation.

courses.title: Analytical Spectroscopy
courses.description: Optical spectroscopic techniques for chemical analysis including conventional and laser-based methods. Absorption, fluorescence, scattering and nonlinear spectroscopies, instrumentation and signal processing.

courses.title: Bioanalytical Chemistry
courses.description: Principles and applications of biospecific binding as a tool for performing selective chemical analysis.

courses.title: Mass Spectrometry
courses.description: Fundamental theory of gaseous ion chemistry, instrumentation, combination with separation techniques, spectral interpretation for organic compounds, applications to biological and environmental chemistry.

courses.title: Microfabricated Chemical Measurement Systems
courses.description: Introduction to micro and nanofabrication techniques, fluid and molecular transport at the micrometer to nanometer length scales, applications of microtechnology to chemical and biochemical measurements.

courses.title: Intermediate Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Introduction to symmetry and group theory; bonding, electronic spectra, and reaction mechanisms of coordination complexes; organometallic complexes, reactions, and catalysis; bioinorganic chemistry. Honors version available.

courses.title: Theoretical Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Chemical applications of symmetry and group theory, crystal field theory, molecular orbital theory. The first third of the course, corresponding to one credit hour, covers point symmetry, group theoretical foundations and character tables.

courses.title: Electronic Structure of Transition Metal Complexes
courses.description: A detailed discussion of ligand field theory and the techniques that rely on the theoretical development of ligand field theory, including electronic spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and magnetism.

courses.title: Organotransition Metal Chemistry
courses.description: Exploring the synthesis, bonding, and reactivity of of organotransition metal complexes. Topics typically include organometallic ligand classification, the elementary steps of organometallic reactions, and applications in catalysis.

courses.title: Intermediate Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Modern topics in organic chemistry. Honors version available.

courses.title: Bioorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Bioorganic chemistry integrates topics from synthetic chemistry, biochemistry, and biophysics to study biomacromolecules and develop tools and materials that utilize them.

courses.title: Mechanisms of Organic and Inorganic Reactions
courses.description: Kinetics and thermodynamics, free energy relationships, isotope effects, acidity and basicity, kinetics and mechanisms of substitution reactions, one- and two-electron transfer processes, principles and applications of photochemistry, organometallic reaction mechanisms.

courses.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: A survey of fundamental organic reactions including substitutions, additions, elimination, and rearrangements; static and dynamic stereochemistry; conformational analysis; molecular orbital concepts and orbital symmetry.

courses.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: Spectroscopic methods of analysis with emphasis on elucidation of the structure of organic molecules: 1H and 13C NMR, infrared, ultraviolet, ORD-CD, mass, and photoelectron spectroscopy.

courses.title: Synthetic Aspects of Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Modern synthetic methods and their application to the synthesis of complicated molecules.

courses.title: Organometallics and Catalysis
courses.description: Structure and reactivity of organometallic complexes and their role in modern catalytic reactions

courses.title: Fundamentals of Materials Science
courses.description: Crystal geometry, diffusion in solids, mechanical properties of solids, electrical conduction in solids, thermal properties of materials, phase equilibria. Previously offered as APPL 470.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, CHEM 482 or PHYS 128; Pre- or corequisite, PHYS 441.

courses.title: Chemistry and Physics of Electronic Materials Processing
courses.description: A survey of materials processing and characterization used in fabricating microelectronic devices. Crystal growth, thin film deposition and etching, and microlithography. Previously offered as APPL 472. Permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Chemistry and Physics of Surfaces
courses.description: The structural and energetic nature of surface states and sites, experimental surface measurements, reactions on surfaces including bonding to surfaces and adsorption, interfaces. Previously offered as APPL 473.

courses.title: Introduction to Biophysical Chemistry
courses.description: Does not carry credit toward graduate work in chemistry or credit toward any track of the B.S. degree with a major in chemistry. Application of thermodynamics to biochemical processes, enzyme kinetics, properties of biopolymers in solution.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 261 or 261H; and MATH 232; Pre- or corequisite, PHYS 105, or 115, or 117, or 119.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry I
courses.description: Thermodynamics, kinetic theory, chemical kinetics.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 102 or 102H, PHYS 118 or 116; pre- or corequisites, MATH 383 and PHYS 119 or 117; C- or better required in chemistry course prerequisites.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Experiments in physical chemistry. One four-hour laboratory each week.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry II
courses.description: Introduction to quantum mechanics, atomic and molecular structure, spectroscopy, statistical mechanics.

courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: Experiments in physical chemistry. Solving thermodynamic and quantum mechanical problems using computer simulations. One three-hour laboratory and a single one-hour lecture each week.

courses.title: Thermodynamics and Introduction to Statistical Thermodynamics
courses.description: Thermodynamics, followed by an introduction to the classical statistical mechanics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

courses.title: Chemical Dynamics
courses.description: Experimental and theoretical aspects of atomic and molecular reaction dynamics.

courses.title: Introduction to Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Introduction to the principles of quantum mechanics. Approximation methods, angular momentum, simple atoms and molecules.

courses.title: Introduction to Molecular Spectroscopy
courses.description: Interaction of radiation with matter; selection rules; rotational, vibrational, and electronic spectra of molecules; laser based spectroscopy and nonlinear optical effects.

courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
courses.description: Applications of quantum mechanics to chemistry. Molecular structure, time-dependent perturbation theory, interaction of radiation with matter.

courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Applications of statistical mechanics to chemistry. Ensemble formalism, condensed phases, nonequilibrium processes.

courses.title: Molecular Modeling in Chemistry
courses.description: This course is offered to first-year graduate and upper-class undergraduate students in different chemistry disciplines who are interested in gaining skills in molecular modeling using modern methodologies from computational chemistry. No prior experience is required. An overview of quantum mechanics (QM) and molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies will be provided. It will also provide extensive experiences to perform different types of computations with abundant hands-on exercises using Gaussian package for QM and LAMMPS for MD simulations.

courses.title: Advanced Methods in Computational Chemistry
courses.description: The course is offered to graduate students and advanced undergraduate students. The course covers the foundations of modern computational chemistry from a theoretical perspective: Hartree-Fock theory, DFT, post-Hartree-Fock methods, classical force fields, basis sets, photochemistry, QM/MM frameworks, molecular dynamics, optimization algorithms. Lectures are accompanied by in-class exercises and tutorials.

courses.title: Polymer Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Various polymerization techniques and characterization methods. One four-hour laboratory each week. Previously offered as APPL 520L.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisite, CHEM 420 or 421 or 425.

courses.title: Laboratory Techniques for Biochemistry
courses.description: An introduction to chemical techniques and research procedures of use in the fields of protein and nucleic acid chemistry. Two four-hour laboratories and one one-hour lecture a week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, BIOL 202 or BIOL 220; Pre- or corequisite, CHEM 433.

courses.title: Advanced Instrumentation and Analytical Measurement Laboratory
courses.description: A laboratory devoted to modern instrumental methods and analytical techniques. One four-hour laboratory and one one-hour lecture each week.

courses.title: Synthetic Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: A laboratory devoted to synthesis and characterization of inorganic complexes and materials. A four-hour synthesis laboratory, a characterization laboratory outside of the regular laboratory period, and a one-hour recitation each week.

courses.title: Honors Synthetic Chemistry Lab
courses.description: This is an honors laboratory course designed to lead you from challenging introductory experiments to five weeks of laboratory work on an independent research project. In addition to exposing you to advanced synthetic techniques, this course will allow you to use multiple modern techniques to characterize the inorganic and organometallic complexes you prepare. Students may not receive credit in both CHEM 551L and CHEM 550L.

courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.description: CHEM 395 or equivalent must have been in the same laboratory as 692H. Senior majors only. Required of all candidates for honors or highest honors.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, six credit hours of CHEM 395 or equivalent research experience in same laboratory as 692H.

courses.title: Introduction to Laboratory Safety
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. This introductory course in laboratory chemical safety is required for all entering chemistry graduate students. Topics include laboratory emergencies, chemical hazards, laboratory inspections and compliance, working with chemicals, waste handling, case studies of university accidents, laboratory equipment, biosafety, radiation, animals, and microfabrication and nanomaterials.

courses.title: Seminar in Materials Chemistry
courses.description: Graduate standing required.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Chemical Biology
courses.description: Application of chemical principles and tools to study and manipulate biological systems; in-depth exploration of examples from the contemporary literature. Topics include new designs for the genetic code, drug design, chemical arrays, single molecule experiments, laboratory-based evolution, chemical sensors, and synthetic biology.

courses.title: Seminar in Biological Chemistry
courses.description: Graduate standing required. Literature survey dealing with topics in protein chemistry and nucleic acid chemistry.

courses.title: Advances in Macromolecular Structure and Function
courses.description: In-depth analysis of the structure-function relationships governing protein-protein and protein-nucleic acid interactions. Topics include replication, DNA repair, transcription, translation, RNA processing, protein complex assembly, and enzyme regulation. Course includes both the current and classic literature that highlight the techniques used to study these processes.

courses.title: Special Topics in Biological Chemistry
courses.description: Modern topics in biological chemistry.

courses.title: Literature Seminar in Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Graduate standing required. Colloquium of modern analytical chemistry topics presented by graduate students and select invited speakers.

courses.title: Analytical Research Techniques
courses.description: Introduction to chemical instrumentation including digital and analog electronics, computers, interfacing, and chemometric techniques. Two one-hour lectures a week.

courses.title: Laboratory in Analytical Research Techniques
courses.description: Experiments in digital and analog instrumentation, computers, interfacing and chemometrics, with applications to chemical instrumentation.

courses.title: Special Topics in Analytical Chemistry
courses.description: Modern topics in analytical chemistry, including advanced electroanalytical chemistry, advanced mass spectrometry, chemical instrumentation, and other subjects of recent significance. Two lecture hours a week.

courses.title: Analytical Technical Writing Workshop
courses.description: Students will participate in 12 workshop sessions co-presented by the instructor and TA covering the basics of technical writing.
