courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.title: Collaboration with Families and Other Professionals
courses.description: Instructs students about the resources available to them, their students, and their students' families. Students will develop skills in working with parents and professionals as partners in the instruction and planning of programs for students with learning disabilities.

courses.title: Master's Internship in Learning Disabilities Education
courses.description: Provides supervised experience in a phase of special education or literacy studies appropriate to the student's qualifications and future educational goals. May require a minimum of 300 clock hours at the internship site per semester depending on student placement. See your advisor for credit hours needed.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.title: Diversity in Education
courses.description: Restricted to graduate students in the M.A.T. program. Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Along with providing overview of schools, their structure, and their role in American society, the course introduces students to the necessity of differentiated instruction based on race, culture, special education, and English as second language learners.

courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Sociocultural Diversity Studies
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth, critical review and analysis of a current topic pertinent to sociocultural diversity in human development. Each offering of this course will focus on a specific domain to be determined by the course instructor in collaboration with the Applied Developmental Science and Special Education program faculty. Potential topics for this course include: The Development of Black, Indigenous, and Persons of Color in America; The Health and Well-Being of LGBTQ+Youth.

courses.title: Foundations of Educational Research
courses.description: Applies the philosophies of science, social science, language, and history (including recent theoretical issues) to the understanding of how educational research is conducted and what contribution it makes.

courses.title: Proseminar in Education
courses.description: Students develop an in-depth understanding of scholarly traditions within education, histories of curricular area and current issues facing these areas and education as a whole, and application of these histories and issues to classrooms and schools.

courses.title: Seminar in Culture, Curriculum, and Change
courses.description: Open to doctoral students only. Critical examination of topics and policy issues related to curriculum and educational change, considered in cultural context.

courses.title: Professional Seminar I
courses.description: Introductory seminar for graduate students. Review current issues in early childhood, special education, and literacy and introduces students to the research of current faculty members.

courses.title: Professional Seminar II: Research and Scholarship in the Educational Sciences
courses.description: Course explores history of psychological studies in education and examines areas of current inquiry such as cognition and learning, teaching and instruction, academic motivation, contextual influences, and theory-based intervention.

courses.title: Seminar in Applied Developmental Sciences and Special Education
courses.description: Open to doctoral students only. Critical examination of theoretical and research issues related to learning, development, teaching, assessment, and quantitative methods of research, from a psychological perspective.

courses.title: Social Studies and Arts
courses.description: Looks at social studies as a discipline that easily integrates other disciplines, particularly the arts, which includes literature. It emphasizes curriculum and instruction, as well as theoretical underpinnings.

courses.title: Foundations of Clinical Mental Health Counseling
courses.description: An overview of the history of community mental health counseling and current topics impacting the profession. The emerging identity of the clinical mental health counselor is explored in terms of theoretical influences, diverse roles and tasks of counselors within various community settings, and professional ethics. There will be an emphasis on multicultural and social justice perspectives shaping the field of clinical mental health counseling with regards to best practice, research, and program development.

courses.title: Problems in Special Education
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Provides an opportunity for post-master's students who wish to engage in supervised field and pilot research. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Psychology of Career Development
courses.description: Open to doctoral students only. Reviews theories and research in the psychology of career development and counseling. Emphasis is on theory and implications for practice.

courses.title: Problems in School Counseling
courses.description: Provides students the opportunity for directed study in school counseling.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Practicum in School Counseling
courses.description: Provides students experiences that may include working with individual, family, or group counseling and consultation.

courses.title: Doctoral Internship in School Counseling
courses.description: Provides students a supervised professional predoctoral internship training experience in counseling.

courses.title: Supervision and Teaching in School Counseling
courses.description: Enables students to gain supervision and teaching skills that will enhance their functions as professors and as leaders in counseling agencies. Strategies of practicum supervision are summarized and research literature is reviewed.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in School Counseling
courses.description: Provides an in-depth appraisal of topics of theoretical and/or clinical nature that are of particular relevance to the field.

courses.title: Transformational Education
courses.description: Examines 20th-century schools that have attempted to redefine and deepen United States democracy, embracing pedagogies and values that offer alternatives to mainstream education.

courses.title: Introduction to Educational Research
courses.description: Course provides introduction to purposes of educational research, roles of theories, hypotheses, questions, and ethical issues. While being exposed to a range of research designs, students are to become critical reviewers and develop research proposals or a master's thesis.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: School Psychology Intervention and Assessment III
courses.description: We will develop knowledge and skills that relate to the implementation of evidenced-based interventions. This innovation implementation course is based on Forman (2009).

courses.title: School Psychology Intervention and Assessment IV
courses.description: This project-based course focuses on utilizing the fields of intervention research and social entrepreneurship to design a novel educational innovation.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Professional School Psychology
courses.description: Required preparation, appropriate courses. Permission of the instructor. Considers advanced topics in the field of school psychology such as professional issues, standards and ethics, and interdisciplinary relations.

courses.title: Doctoral Externship in School Psychology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Supervised field placement experiences for doctoral-level students in school psychology, integrating training with field responsibilities at a systems level in schools and school-related settings.

courses.title: Doctoral Internship in School Psychology
courses.description: Supervised doctoral internship in school psychology for advanced training in professional skills and research in schools and school-related settings.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Policy Development in Education
courses.description: Graduate course about the political process and policy dynamics. With a focus on the U.S. domestic context, the course addresses the policy process in general and examines the workings of that process in education.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Educational Research
courses.description: Explores and analyzes the range of educational research designs including experimental, correlational, survey, descriptive, case study, ethnography, narrative, policy, and longitudinal research.

courses.title: Development and Learning
courses.description: Introduces influential theoretical approaches to the study of development and learning. Students learn how to apply various methodological approaches and theoretical frameworks. Readings include developmental psychology, learning sciences, and cultural anthropology.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Seminar in Mental Health and School-Based Counseling
courses.description: This course provides an overview of some of the major mental health problems facing children and adolescents. Equips students entering the school counseling profession with pivotal knowledge needed to develop and implement comprehensive school counseling programs that include collaborative approaches to addressing mental health and wellness. An emphasis will be placed on cognitive-behavioral research-based methods and strategies for addressing emotional and behavioral difficulties of the most prevalent mental health diagnoses of children and adolescents.

courses.title: Human Development
courses.description: School of Education majors only. Emphasizes theories of child and adolescent development as well as research findings that aid in the understanding of human behavior and development.

courses.title: Educational Measurement and Evaluation
courses.description: Identifies the basic concepts in measurement and evaluation, describes the role of evaluation in curriculum construction and revision, and describes the development and use of teacher-constructed tests.

courses.title: Applied Measurement Theory for Education
courses.description: An examination of the logic and theory of educational measurement. Practical applications of measurement theory to the construction and use of a variety of educational measurement devices.

courses.title: Qualitative Research Methods I: Philosophical Foundations of Qualitative Research
courses.description: This course serves as an introduction to the foundations of qualitative research, including histories and philosophies that shape methods and frameworks for conducting research, as well as the importance of core concepts such as subjectivity, positionality, ontology, and epistemology. Students will learn skills such as developing basic research designs, research questions for conducting interviews, as well as preliminary approaches to data analysis. Throughout the semester, students learn to critically read and write about qualitative research while gaining understandings of this field of inquiry.

courses.title: School Law: Justice and Equity
courses.description: Required preparation, six semester hours of graduate school work in school administration. Provides an overview of the legal structure of education, liability, constitutional rights, contractual relationships, federal regulations, and collective action. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Politics of Education
courses.description: Students study the politics surrounding the nation's largest public institution (education) along with the motivations and maneuvering of people with power to shape it.

courses.title: Development and Systems Leadership
courses.description: Focused on the issues pertaining to personnel, planning, facilities, administrative applications of technology, superintendent/board relations, district-level curriculum and assessment issues, and creating and sustaining community inter-agency partnerships.

courses.title: Organizational Behavior and Theory in Education
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Analyze the theoretical assertions and empirical knowledge claims that have led to the dominant structures, power relationships, and performance expectations of American schools.

courses.title: Instructional Leadership for Supervision, Curriculum, and Technology
courses.description: Provides fundamental knowledge of instructional design, techniques of teaching/learning, evaluation of the teaching/learning process, and ways in which school-based leaders can support excellence in classroom instruction.

courses.title: School Finance and Economic Equity
courses.description: Covers the area of financing school corporations in the current economic and political setting, with emphasis on the interrelationships of educational, economic, and political decisions. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Cultural Aspects of Leadership and Instruction in School Reform
courses.description: Designed to provide students with perspectives regarding the interplay of cultural issues that challenge the partnership between administration and instruction.

courses.title: School Governance
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Focuses on governance and policy at the school building level and how district-wide governance, state educational policy, federal involvement in education, and educational special interest groups impact school-sized governance.

courses.title: The Excellent School Seminar I
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Research and models on high-performing organizations, instructionally effective schools and school systems, and national school reform efforts presented in the context of traditional and emerging organizational theory and research. .

courses.title: Advanced Leadership Theories
courses.description: Requires students to integrate previous studies to focus on management applications, dilemmas, and conflicts.

courses.title: Development of a Research Proposal
courses.description: Requires students to integrate previous studies to focus on theory, inquiry, and organizational practice.

courses.title: The Excellent School Seminar II
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Research and models on high-performing organizations, instructionally effective schools and school systems, and national school reform efforts presented in the context of traditional and emerging organizational theory and research.

courses.title: Seminar in Educational Studies
courses.description: Focuses on educational issues and theories involving culture, curriculum, and change. Issues and theories addressed will vary.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Seminar and Supervised Internship in Educational Administration
courses.description: An advanced internship and seminar relevant to the program in administration and to the student's progress toward advanced administrative certification. May be repeated for credit.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EDUC 727, 750, 832, 834; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Instructional Strategies for Teaching and Learning in Digital Contexts
courses.description: Will prepare students to enact evidence-based strategies that integrate digital tools and resources for delivering instruction in blended, hybrid, and fully online contexts. Students will design an aligned unit of instruction that includes objectives, assessments, and instructional activities that adhere to instructional design standards and utilize an array of contemporary digital tools. Will consider design approaches that enable the gathering and visualization of data that reflect student activity and performances.

courses.title: Personalized and Adaptive Learning
courses.description: This blended, seminar-and-workshop style course (1) provides an overview of learning and instructional design theories, then (2) introduces ways that theory can guide personalization of instructional materials and provision of adaptive design features to produce improved learning experiences and outcomes. Personalization topics in include definitions and policies, approaches that accommodate learners' interests, and ways to provide choice and promote ownership of learning. Adaptivity topics include provision of feedback and support, and designing for learning efficiency.

courses.title: Human Resource Management
courses.description: This doctoral-level course examines strategic alignment between human resource management (HRM) and an organization's mission, vision, and long-term goals. Emphasizing synergies between HRM practices and organizational strategy, the course covers performance, innovation, and sustainable growth. Topics follow the organizational life cycle, from job analysis and design to workforce planning, talent acquisition, training, and professional development. Students critically explore contemporary HRM practices, methods, and functions, focusing on evidence-based and ethical approaches. The course evaluates HRM's influence on organizational culture, employee engagement, and competitive advantage, equipping students to design effective HRM strategies that contribute to organizational effectiveness and long-term success.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EDUC 834 EDUC 858, EDUC 859, EDUC 893, EDUC 905, EDUC 914, EDUC 920 and EDUC 956.

courses.title: Data Informed Decision Making
courses.description: This course focuses on identifying data sources to inform (1) how a problem of practice is perceived by its stakeholders, (2) the effectiveness of interventions in response to the problem, and (3) measures to solidify the interventions' effectiveness over time. An emphasis will be placed on the use of data to make evidence-based decisions within organizational contexts.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EDUC 834, EDUC 858, EDUC 859, EDUC 893, EDUC 905, EDUC 914, EDUC 920 and EDUC 956.

courses.title: Change Leadership and Systems Improvement
courses.description: The course is a core requirement for all students enrolled in the Interprofessional Certificate in Improvement Science and Implementation as well as the Masters of School Administration program. Introduces students to cutting-edge approaches to change leadership and system improvement. It leverages lessons from implementation and improvement sciences to help students learn to drive system change in the nation's schools, social service agencies, community organizations, and healthcare settings.

courses.title: Curriculum Theory
courses.description: Relates curriculum development to relevant theories and research in humanistic and behavioral studies. This is an advanced course.

courses.title: Instructional Systems Development
courses.description: Delineates strategies for developing instructional systems, including needs assessment, job analysis, goal setting, use of criterion tests, delivery systems, project management, and evaluation of learners and programs.

courses.title: Supervision and Instruction
courses.description: Examines the history, nature, and purposes of educational supervision, with an emphasis on the supervisor's role in improving teaching, curriculum development, and staff development.

courses.title: Seminar in Curriculum and Instruction
courses.description: Review and interpretation of existing research in the area of curriculum and instruction.

courses.title: Problems in Curriculum and Instruction
courses.description: Required preparation, two courses in graduate education. Provides an opportunity for advanced students to do independent study under supervision in an area of study. (Sections include early childhood, intermediate, secondary subjects, media, literacy, and general.) May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Practicum in Curriculum and Instruction
courses.description: Experiences may include projects, field studies, or internships with one of a number of agencies concerned with education. (Sections include early childhood, intermediate, secondary subjects, media, literacy, and general.)
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Research Apprenticeship
courses.description: Research apprenticeship for all students in the Curriculum and Instruction Ed.D. program. Individually arranged with a faculty advisor and an appropriate placement.

courses.title: Foundations of Inquiry - Quantitative
courses.description: In this course we focus on quantitative forms of inquiry, highlighting the types of questions quantitative data are best positioned to answer and common forms of data collection and analysis. To foster your development as a scholar-practitioner, the course will provide you with the foundational knowledge to be a discerning consumer of quantitative research and help you find the tools to answer your own well-formed practice-based research questions. For students enrolled in the online Ed.D. in Organizational Learning and Leadership program cohort.

courses.title: Foundations of Inquiry - Qualitative
courses.description: Foundations of Inquiry - Qualitative Methods is a graduate level course designed to support students in developing an understanding of qualitative research methods and designs. The focus of this course is on the creation of research questions, the development of qualitative designs, employment of data collection approaches, and analysis procedures to address those problems. For students enrolled in the online Ed.D. in Organizational Learning and Leadership program cohorts.

courses.title: Seminar in Special Education
courses.description: Emphasis on developmental deviation exhibited by exceptional children in cognitive, language, social, and affective development.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Teaching and Personnel Development
courses.description: Focuses on teaching and personnel development at the preservice and inservice levels. Topics include: application of adult learning principles and styles; syllabus development; technology and teaching; supervision; mentorship and research innovations in college teaching.

courses.title: Families, Schools, and Child Development: Successful Intervention Strategies
courses.description: The purpose of this seminar is to provide an introduction to the theory, research, methods, and current issues related to the influence of families and schools on children's development.

courses.title: College Teaching Internship
courses.description: Open to graduate students only. Permission of the instructor. This course is designed to give doctoral and masters' students experience at college teaching prior to taking on full responsibility for a class of her/his own. The student will fully participate as a teaching assistant in the class of an experienced tenured, tenure track, or clinical professor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Policy to Practice
courses.description: Examine relationships between broader social, economic, and political currents and the chosen instruments for education reform. Students examine what purposes stakeholders believe schools serve and how policy is/isn't translated into practice.

courses.title: Issues in Educational Policy and Research
courses.description: Course familiarizes students with public policy in education and its influence on schools and schooling. Students learn methodological perspectives of education policy research. Examine major policy initiatives in education.

courses.title: Qualitative Research II: Data Collection
courses.description: This course introduces students to field research methods and analysis of qualitative data that focuses on the application of these techniques in evaluation and policy research.

courses.title: Qualitative Research III: Data Analysis
courses.description: This advanced seminar focuses on the needs of doctoral students immersed in qualitative research, with an emphasis on data analysis and representation.

courses.title: The Business of Education
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of the education sector and the multiple types of organizations that operate within it. The multiple activities, assignments, and topics of study in this course are aligned to the following learning objectives and outcomes.

courses.title: Seminar in Education
courses.description: Required preparation, two courses in graduate education. Permission of the instructor. Provides for seminar treatment of appropriate topics.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Problems in the Philosophical Foundations of Education
courses.description: Provides an opportunity for advanced doctoral students to do independent study under supervision.

courses.title: Problems in the Sociological Foundations of Education
courses.description: Provides an opportunity for advanced doctoral students to do independent study under supervision.

courses.title: Design Thinking for Leaders
courses.description: Graduate-level course explores the intersection of design thinking principles and social constructs to drive organizational success and innovation. Students will engage with frameworks that emphasize empathy, collaboration, and iterative problem-solving, equipping them to navigate complex challenges across a broad range of organizations. Through case studies and hands-on projects, participants will learn to apply design thinking methodologies to foster people-centered cultures, enhance team dynamics, and implement creative solutions that align with organizational goals. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to leverage design thinking as a strategic tool to inspire innovation and achieve sustainable outcomes within their organizations.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EDUC 834, EDUC 858, EDUC 859, EDUC 905, and EDUC 956.

courses.title: Histories of School and Schooling
courses.description: Course provides an understanding of the history of American public education, its current status and research in education based in a larger context of society, and its schools and schooling practices.

courses.title: Critical Multicultural Education
courses.description: Examination of the current issues in multicultural education, cultural study, and the development of curriculum for critical multicultural education.

courses.title: Seminar in Educational Studies
courses.description: Involves an in-depth exploration of theories and issues involving culture, curriculum, and change. Topics will vary.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Causal Inference in Educational Research
courses.description: The seminar will explore issues related to causal inference in educational research and discuss several research designs that are well-suited for making causal inferences. We will draw upon the counter-factual model of causality to discuss what it means to observe a cause and effect relationship and then focus on the problems researchers regularly encounter. The course will provide a detailed discussion of a wide range of experimental and quasi-experimental research designs.

courses.title: Seminar in Human Development and Individual Differences
courses.description: Required preparation, at least one course in human development at the graduate level or permission of the instructor. Analyzes research data and theoretical positions pertaining to individual differences in human development in the educational setting.

courses.title: Seminar in Human Learning and Cognition
courses.description: Required preparation, one or two courses in educational and developmental psychology. Studies theoretical aspects and practical implications of psychologies of learning.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Case Study Methods
courses.description: Provides students with an overview of the methodology of case study research and to enhance students' skills in using research techniques.

courses.title: Statistical Analysis of Educational Data III
courses.description: An extension of the general linear model to analysis of educational data with multiple dependent variables, with computer applications.

courses.title: Secondary Data Analysis
courses.description: Provides students who have an introductory background in statistics with an overview of secondary data analysis and enhances students' skills in using data analysis to test hypotheses.

courses.title: Advanced and Applied Leadership Practice
courses.description: Building on foundational leadership knowledge, this course examines the epistemological assumptions underlying modernist and postmodernist leadership theories. Students critically analyze how power, context, and identity shape leadership discourse and practice, engaging with critical, relational, and complexity-based perspectives. Through rigorous theoretical inquiry and applied analysis, the course challenges students to question whose voices have been centered in leadership scholarship and to develop theoretically grounded approaches that address equity, social justice, and the future of leadership. Ultimately, students synthesize diverse paradigms into a coherent leadership philosophy that integrates critical consciousness with practical wisdom.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, Online doctoral students enrolled in the EdD-OLL program concentration only.

courses.title: Teacher Education Seminar for MAT Supervisors
courses.description: This course is required during both fall and spring semesters for all MAT supervisors. The course will focus on exploring teacher education through the lens of field-based supervision. Weekly meetings to bring teacher education research and literature to supervisors' ongoing practice through discussion of selected readings, book study, dialogue about problems of practice. The course will align supervisors' practice in the field with MAT methods pedagogical approaches for supervisors to best support candidates.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EDUC 754 highly recommended but not required.

courses.title: Introduction to Structural Modeling
courses.description: Introduces structural equation modeling with both observed and latent variables. Applications include confirmatory factor analysis, multiple group analyses, longitudinal analyses, and multitrait-multimethod models.

courses.title: Special Topics in Education
courses.description: This course provides students the opportunity for intensive exploration and discussion of selected topics in education.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Educational Policy Doctoral Seminar
courses.description: Provides for seminar treatment of appropriate topics related to education policy.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Foundations of Leadership
courses.description: The course aims to provide a systematic examination of leadership in practice and how these examples result in successful leadership practices relative to theories of leadership, ethical frameworks, and your personal strengths and abilities. From these reflections you will develop an intellectually rigorous, personal statement of leadership. For students enrolled in the online Ed.D. in Organizational Learning and Leadership program cohort.

courses.title: Item Response Theory
courses.description: A first course in test theory (e.g., EDUC 829, PSYC 842) is recommended but not required. Please ask the course instructor if you are unsure about prerequisites. This course covers basic and advanced topics in item response theory (IRT). Examples are taken from educational testing, psychological assessment, and patient-reported health outcomes. Students produce a term project applying IRT to assessment data, and / or addressing mathematical or computational aspects of IRT.

courses.title: Organizational Learning and Leadership Capstone I
courses.description: This course is designed to guide students through a process to elevate scholarly writing, effective alignment with a research to practice structure, and implement a peer review process. Through a portfolio-based examination, students will identify artifacts that will contribute to a root cause analysis, design thinking, or program evaluation writing approach. Through accessing campus resources, including the Odum Institute for Research, library services, and Institutional Review Board (IRB) procedures, students will gain the necessary skills and knowledge to successfully navigate their doctoral learning journey. This course aims to foster a collaborative and rigorous academic environment, preparing students for successful completion.

courses.title: Sociology of School Improvement
courses.description: This course aims to develop a sociological understanding of the complex relationship between education and society.

courses.title: Advanced Techniques in School Counseling: Evidence-Based Practices
courses.description: This advanced elective is designed for graduate-level students in school counseling who are ready to deepen their clinical skillset and translate theory into practice. Through a hands-on, project-based approach, students will explore and apply evidence-based counseling techniques, including Internal Family Systems, Motivational Interviewing, Expressive Arts Techniques, Narrative Therapy, and Acceptance and Commitment/Dialectical Behavior Therapy adapted for the school setting. Students create practical, school-ready individual and group intervention plans that can be immediately used in K--12 environments. Students will engage in experiential learning, peer consultation, and reflective practice to ensure that each plan is both clinically sound and contextually relevant.

courses.title: Exploring Representations of Education in Popular Culture
courses.description: Students in this course explore and analyze how education has been represented in popular culture. Theoretical foundation of the course from seminars and readings.

courses.title: Leading Organizations to Equitable Practice
courses.description: This course will provide the foundational knowledge for creating, sustaining, and leading an inclusive culture within organizations. You will learn to incorporate multiple stakeholders' voices within and outside the organization through an equity-minded leadership lens. We will place a strong emphasis on collaboration and coalition building within organizations to create an effective organizational culture in which all stakeholders can thrive. For students enrolled in the online Ed.D. in Organizational Learning and Leadership program cohort.

courses.title: Education of African Americans
courses.description: Students examine historical and contemporary aims for and assumptions underlying the public "education" of African Americans in the United States. Analysis of published histories, theories, qualtitative and quantitative research, encounters, events, and issues.

courses.title: Applied Quantitative Methods in Curriculum and Teacher Education
courses.description: Applied statistics course designed to introduce students to how descriptive and inferential statistics are used in curriculum studies and teacher education. Students explore how statistical procedures are used in school, school district, state, and national settings.

courses.title: The Science of Implementation in Organizations
courses.description: This course introduces implementation science as a practical discipline for understanding and improving how evidence informed practices, programs, and policies are enacted within complex organizational systems. Designed for practitioners working across sectors, the course emphasizes conceptual fluency and applied use of implementation frameworks rather than preparation for implementation research. Students will examine core principles of implementation science and the functions of major frameworks, including determinant, process, strategy, and evaluation frameworks. Students will apply these frameworks to a real change initiative in their organization to diagnose implementation challenges, design implementation processes, align strategies, and define meaningful measures of implementation success.

courses.title: Applied Qualitative Methods
courses.description: This course will provide students with opportunities to collect, analyze, and use data and evidence to evaluate and reflect on the process of organizational learning, while learning to make ethical and effective methodological choices that support organizational improvement and advancement.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EDUC 834 EDUC 858 EDUC 859 EDUC 905 EDUC 956.

courses.title: Introduction to Learning Sciences
courses.description: Course is designed to provide an overview of the field of learning sciences. Goals of learning sciences are: 1) understand the physical, cognitive, and social aspects of learning environments and 2) use these understandings to design more effective learning environments.

courses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science and Sociocultural Perspectives on Learning
courses.description: Course provides an overview of learning theories in education with a special emphasis upon a sociocultural perspective. Course examines how learning theories are or can be enacted in research, policy, and practice.

courses.title: Design of Technology-Enhanced Learning Environments
courses.description: This course provides a studio-based approach to the design of technology-enhanced learning environments for formal and informal education. Students will explore various forms of emerging technologies for education, engage in a design thinking process, and design prototypes to solve a specific learning problem.

courses.title: Change Leadership Across Organizational Systems
courses.description: Course examines the complex dynamics of organizational change and leadership within a broad range of contexts. Through a critical analysis of change theories, leadership models, and case studies, students will explore strategies to successfully lead and manage change processes in organizations. Emphasis on understanding the social, cultural, and structural factors influencing change, including ethical and strategic considerations necessary for effective leadership. Students will engage in applied research, reflective practice, and collaborative projects to develop advanced competencies in diagnosing organizational challenges, designing change initiatives, and fostering resilient leadership practices through a blend of learning to make connections between theory and practice.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EDUC 834 EDUC 858 EDUC 859 EDUC 905 EDUC 956.

courses.title: Mixed Methods Research
courses.description: Explore foundations of mixed methods. Build familiarity with research designs and methods, learning how to integrate data from mixed methods designs. Learn to critique mixed methods research and designs. Provides preparation for proposing mixed methods projects.

courses.title: Design Based Research
courses.description: DBR is a multi-disciplinary and mixed methods approach. When developing interventions DBR designers draw theoretical insights from various disciplines (e.g. cognitive science, sociology, learning sciences, instructional design, etc.). When researching interventions, DBR researchers draw from numerous modes of inquiry. Thus, this course is not a substitute for further work in quantitative or qualitative courses. Students in this course should have some grounding in quantitative and qualitative methods and we draw upon this knowledge.

courses.title: Economics of Education
courses.description: Students consider and critically reflect upon the contributions of economic theory to educational policy issues. Course provides an overview of economic theories as they pertain to the provision of public education and an overview of econometrics. Focuses on salient topics in educational policy and their analysis through an economic lens.

courses.title: School Law and Public Policy
courses.description: Course examines the judiciary's role in policy making, and its direct impact on school law and policy issues as they pertain to schools, stakeholders, and society.

courses.title: Multilevel Modeling
courses.description: The primary goal for the course is to assist the students in investigating research problems in social sciences, particularly when data is meaningfully organized into multiple layers as a hierarchy, or contextual levels. Multilevel models (MLM) are also known as hierarchical linear models (HLM), random coefficient models, or random effects models. MLM can be used to analyze a variety of questions with either categorical or continuous dependent variables, and explained by many independent variables.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EDUC 710 and 784; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Diversity in Teacher Education
courses.description: Focus on research in teacher education that addresses diversity issues, a particular focus on sociocultural and sociopolitical approaches. Course emphasizes the relationship between theory and practice by focusing on the teacher as an agent of change.

courses.title: Research in Teacher Education and Diversity
courses.description: Course looks at research in teacher education that addresses diversity issues, with a particular focus on sociocultural and sociopolitical approaches. Course will emphasize the relationship between theory and practice by focusing on the teacher as an agent of change in addressing issues of equity and social justice in diverse classrooms.

courses.title: Institutional Logics of Curriculum and Teaching
courses.description: Learn about institutional theory and management and issues, policies and practices that describe, define, complicate, and confine those whose work focuses on curriculum and teaching.

courses.title: Advanced Curriculum in the Humanities
courses.description: Course brings together those with interests in academic disciplines of literature, history, foreign languages and literatures, English as a second language, and the arts to examine the status of the humanities in our society and in our P-12 schools. Students will consider socio-cultural and political contexts and contributions to the humanities.

courses.title: Research and Policy in Teacher Education
courses.description: Study different approaches taken to studying teacher education and the implications of that work on policy, tracing the trajectory from research to policy.

courses.title: Leading Organizations to Equitable Practice
courses.description: This course will provide the foundational knowledge for creating, sustaining, and leading an inclusive culture within organizations. You will learn to incorporate multiple stakeholders' voices within and outside the organization through an equity-minded leadership lens. We will place a strong emphasis on collaboration and coalition building within organizations to create an effective organizational culture in which all stakeholders can thrive. This course is core course in the curriculum for the EdD concentration in Organizational Learning and Leadership.

courses.title: Applied Quantitative Methods
courses.description: In this course, students learn how to analyze quantitative data from various sources (e.g., administrative, survey) to answer pragmatic questions. The course focuses on generating and interpreting graphical descriptive summaries and the associations between multiple continuous or categorical variables. You will also be introduced to the inferential statistics concepts of hypothesis testing and confidence intervals to characterize the uncertainty of conclusions based on the data. Students will use data visualization software. This course is a required methods course in the curriculum for the EdD concentration in Organizational Learning and Leadership.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EDUC 858, EDUC 893, EDUC 859, and EDUC 905.

courses.title: Applied Theory and Research: Dissertation Proposal Prep
courses.description: Course explores planning and conducting qualitative research. Students will apply knowledge of qualitative research to dissertation proposal/projects. They will also explore different research proposals and data collection strategies.

courses.title: Critical Race Theory: History, Research, and Practice
courses.description: Course will explore the historical development of Critical Race Theory (CRT) from its origins in Critical Legal Studies through the more recent frameworks established in education, including intersections with LatCrit Theory, AsianCrit, QueerCrit, TribalCrit, and Critical Race Feminism.

courses.title: Schooling Experiences of Men of Color
courses.description: Focus, through a critical lens, will be on African American and Latino men, also covers experiences of Asian American and Native American males. Study of research that addresses issues of identity, masculinities, system barriers, cultural capital, and peer group dynamics.

courses.title: Critical Social Theory
courses.description: Course explores critical social theories through popular culture texts. Course challenges the perception that popular culture texts have little to offer in the way of educational discourse.

courses.title: Autoethnography Educational Research
courses.description: Course will focus on the theory and practice of autoethnography, or "reading" significant patterns in everyday experience and connecting those patterns to the self and to broader social concerns. Students will read models of autoethnography, methodological works, do writing exercises, and create independent autoethnographic projects.

courses.title: Supervised Research
courses.description: Open to graduate students only. Provides students with the opportunity to work with individual faculty members in collaborative research activities in association with a seminar during the second, third, and fourth semesters of study. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.description: Focuses on the development of a master's project or a major paper other than a thesis.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Global Warming: Science, Social Impacts, Solutions
courses.description: Students will examine evidence that human activity has caused global warming, investigate scientists' ability to predict climate change, and discuss the political and social dimensions of global climate change. Course previously offered as MASC 51.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Living with Our Oceans and Atmosphere
courses.description: Modern theories of changing weather, severe weather events, oceanic hazards, interactions between the oceans and atmosphere, and changes that are linked to human activity. Course previously offered as MASC 52.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Ends of the Earth: Polar Oceanography and Exploration
courses.description: What explains the "pull of the poles"? This seminar combines a modern survey of polar oceanography with historical views of early polar explorations, as reported by the explorers themselves. Course previously offered as MASC 53.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Change in the Coastal Ocean
courses.description: This course provides an opportunity to explore changes in marine and closely linked terrestrial environments caused by the interactions of fascinating oceanographic processes. Introductory presentations and discussions will focus on published works of active marine scientists who combine disciplinary training with knowledge and skills from other fields. Course previously offered as MASC 55.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Connections to the Sea: Challenges Faced at Coastal Inlets
courses.description: This course explores the natural history of several inlets, impact of human intervention, and political/policy challenges faced; includes several group projects/presentations and a field trip to a coastal inlet.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Extreme Microorganisms: Pushing the Limits of Life on Earth and Beyond
courses.description: This seminar focuses on some of the most extreme microorganisms on the planet, microorganisms that thrive without oxygen, under high temperatures (e.g., in pressurized water above the boiling point), and under chemical stress factors (high sulfide and heavy metal concentrations) that were once thought to be incompatible with life. Course previously offered as MASC 59.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Myths and Realities of Sharks: A Field-Based Course of Apex Predators
courses.description: This course will provide a foundational introduction regarding the biology, ecology, and conservation science of sharks. Leveraging the local environment near UNC-CH's Institute of Marine Sciences (Morehead City, NC), the class will also focus heavily on field-based experiences demonstrating shark research methodologies and concepts related to the natural history of sharks, as well as the 'ecosystem roles' of sharks within coastal marine habitats.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: How Rivers Shape the World
courses.description: Rivers and streams are everywhere. They have shaped societies for all of human history serving as both a critical resource and a force of destruction. Rivers provide food, water, transportation, and energy... as well as flood and droughts. We will dive into the science and history of rivers: How rivers flood and shape the earth and influence the evolution and destruction of civilizations, and in return, how people have changed rivers. This course will involve regular discussion, data literacy assignments, and student-driven research project.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Soundscape of Our Planet
courses.description: This seminar explores acoustic waves in the Earth's environment including ambient biological, physical, and human communication with an emphasis on observation and laboratory analysis. Course previously offered as GEOL 68.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Field Geology of Eastern California
courses.description: This seminar provides a hands-on introduction to active geologic and environmental processes in eastern California, including active volcanoes, earthquake-producing faults, and extreme climate change. Course previously offered as GEOL 72H.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Energy Resources for a Hungry Planet
courses.description: Discussions are centered on the most pressing issues of our time: environmental deterioration and construction of a sustainable (livable) world during and after the depletion of traditional energy resources. Course previously offered as GEOL 76.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Volcanoes and Civilization: An Uneasy Coexistence
courses.description: Volcanoes provide a breathable atmosphere, a habitable climate, and precious ores, but they have the potential to destroy civilization. This seminar will explore the uneasy coexistence of volcanoes and civilization. Course previously offered as GEOL 77.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Coasts in Crisis
courses.description: An investigation of the geologic evolution and function of coastal environments, the recent effects of coastal development and engineering, and an examination of existing coastal management strategies and the tensions between coastal development and the desire to preserve natural environments. Course previously offered as GEOL 79.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester. Course previously offered as GEOL 89.

courses.title: Planet Earth
courses.description: Major geologic events: earthquakes, volcanic activity, mountain formation, plate tectonics, and erosion. Landscape development by glaciers, streams and groundwater, ocean currents and waves, wind. Optional laboratory: EMES 101L. PX credit for EMES 101+101L. Course previously offered as GEOL 101.

courses.title: Planet Earth Laboratory
courses.description: Study of common minerals and rocks. Use of topographic and geologic maps to illustrate geologic processes. Two laboratory hours a week. Course previously offered as GEOL 101L.

courses.title: The Marine Environment
courses.description: Introduction to marine sciences emphasizing physical, chemical, biological, and geological phenomenon in oceanic and coastal environments. Human use of, and impact on, marine resources. Science majors should take EMES 401. Students may not receive credit for both EMES 103 and EMES 202. Course previously offered as GEOL 103/MASC 101.

courses.title: The Marine Environment Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory exercises aimed at investigating the marine environment including physical, chemical, and biological processes. Two laboratory hours per week. Students must also enroll in the EMES 103 lecture or have taken EMES 103 in a previous semester. Course previously offered as MASC 101L.

courses.title: Natural Disasters: Hollywood versus Reality
courses.description: Natural hazards arise from a suite of dynamic processes that operate within the Earth and along its surface. How individuals and communities prepare for and respond to natural disasters is strongly influenced by our perception of the risk associated with these processes. This course investigates a range of natural hazards, using the popular media as a starting point for analyses and discussions of the causes of disasters.

courses.title: Diving into Drawdown
courses.description: This course will take a deep dive into Project Drawdown (https://drawdown.org), which seeks to quantify and rank contributions to global warming of diverse human activities and offer truly impactful solutions for climate change mitigation from direct atmospheric capture of CO2 to modifying food production practices and blue carbon sequestration. The class will explore the range of proposed climate change solutions and conduct a capstone-type project examining topics of relevance to NC in the Drawdown framework.

courses.title: Special Topics in Earth, Marine, and Environmental Sciences at an Introductory Level
courses.description: An undergraduate seminar course that is designed to be a participatory intellectual adventure on an advanced, emergent, and stimulating topic within a selected discipline in earth, marine and environmental sciences. Course previously offered as GEOL 190.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Special Topics and Earth, Marine, and Environmental Sciences, FC-PAST
courses.description: An undergraduate seminar course that is designed to be a participatory intellectual adventure on an advanced, emergent, and stimulating topic within a selected discipline in earth, marine and environmental sciences.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: The Solid Earth
courses.description: An introduction to the solid earth for students continuing in EMES and other sciences. Topics include synthesis of the elements, formation of the solar system and earth, plate tectonics, earth materials, internal energy, magnetism, geochemical cycles, and earth resources. Course previously offered as GEOL 200.

courses.title: Earth's Surface: Processes, Landforms, and History
courses.description: This course focuses on the biological, chemical, and physical processes that shape the surface of the earth. Major points of emphasis will include earth's climate, the global water cycle, geomorphic processes and the landforms they create, sedimentology and depositional environments, and elements of earth history recorded by earth surface processes. Course previously offered as GEOL 201.

courses.title: Oceanography
courses.description: Required preparation, major in a natural science or two courses in natural sciences. Studies origin of ocean basins, seawater chemistry and dynamics, biological communities, sedimentary record, and oceanographic history. Students lacking science background should see EMES 103. Students may not receive credit for both EMES 103 and EMES 202. Course previously offered as GEOL 403/MASC 401/EMES 401.

courses.title: Data Analysis for Earth, Marine, and Environmental Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the analysis, manipulation, presentation and interpretation of data, with a focus on Earth and marine sciences, environmental sciences, ecology, and geography.

courses.title: The Microbial World: Foundations in Structure, Metabolism, and Ecology
courses.description: This course will provide a basic introduction to microbiology and microbial ecology and evolution, covering topics such as cell structure, energetics, genomics, evolution and gene flow, ecological interactions, population and community dynamics, and biogeochemical cycling.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, BIOL 101 or BIOL 103; permission of the instructor.

courses.title: North Carolina Estuaries: Environmental Processes and Problems
courses.description: Natural processes and human impacts on estuarine systems using the Neuse River estuary as a case study. Course includes one week of intensive field work based at the Institute of Marine Sciences. A student may not receive credit for this course after receiving credit for ENEC 222. Course previously offered as MASC 220.

courses.title: The Blue Economy Revolution
courses.description: This course will provide a foundational introduction to the Blue Economy, which has been defined by the US Congress (2024) as: "the sustainable use of marine, lake, or other aquatic resources in support of economic development objectives". The connection between the ocean and economy will be defined though examination of ecological, social, and economic interactions that define the blue economy systems. Lectures will delve into diverse topics such as (but not limited to) trade routes/exploration, NC coastal development policy, wind farms, marine reserves, sustainable fishing, seafood farming, ecotourism, restoration, novel marine sensors, carbon crediting, and venture capital.

courses.title: Teaching Apprentice in Earth and Marine Sciences
courses.description: Permission required. Previous grade of B or higher in course that student will be teaching. Experience as an Undergraduate Learning Assistant includes preparations, demonstrations, assistance, and attendance at weekly meetings. Apprentices will not be involved in any aspects of grading. May be repeated for credit. Requires a learning contract.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Special Topics and Earth, Marine, and Environmental Sciences, FC-NATSCI
courses.description: An undergraduate seminar course that is designed to be a participatory intellectual adventure on an advanced, emergent, and stimulating topic within a selected discipline in earth, marine and environmental sciences.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Earth's Critical Mineral Resources
courses.description: Minerals in sedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic environments: their economic importance, properties, occurrence, and uses. Methods of identifying minerals, including use of physical and optical properties, and scanning electron microscopy. Course previously offered as GEOL 301.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EMES 101 or EMES 200 or any EMES FYS; Pre- or corequisite, CHEM 101; permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- or corequisite.

courses.title: Earth's Critical Mineral Resources - Laboratory
courses.description: This is a 1-credit lab focusing on minerals, the building blocks of rocks! Students will have the opportunity to conduct hand-sample and microscope work on rocks from sedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic environments. Lab exercises will cover (physical, optical and scanning electron) methods of identifying minerals within a variety of rocks.

courses.title: Structural Geology
courses.description: Introduction to the mechanical behavior and dynamic evolution of the earth's crust through the study of deformed rocks. Course previously offered as GEOL 302.

courses.title: Sedimentology and Stratigraphy
courses.description: Introduction of principles involved in description and classification of sedimentary rocks and stratigraphic units as well as stratigraphic correlation. Students will be introduced to relationships of processes, depositional environments, and sedimentary facies. Course previously offered as GEOL 303.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EMES 200 and 201; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Petrology and Plate Tectonics
courses.description: Studies of the origin and evolution of igneous and metamorphic rocks, including microscopic, X-ray, and field methods; volcanology; plate-tectonic interpretation of rock sequences. Three lecture and three laboratory hours a week. Course previously offered as GEOL 304.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EMES 200 and 301; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Planetary Geology: Meteorites and Asteroids
courses.description: Required preparation, one introductory geology course numbered below EMES 202, except first-year seminar. Effects and probable effects of meteorite and asteroid impacts on earth and other planets: craters, new meteorites, and tektites; giant sea waves; reduction of species and extinction of organisms. Course previously offered as GEOL 204/GEOL 305.

courses.title: Earth and Life through Time
courses.description: This course investigates the history of Earth as a dynamic, interconnected system reconstructed from the geologic record. Students examine how interactions among the geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere drive change through time. Emphasis is placed on analyzing scientific evidence, interpreting data, and evaluating competing explanations for major transitions in Earth and life history, including mass extinctions, climate change, and evolutionary radiations. Students apply scientific reasoning to reconstruct past environments and consider how insights from Earth history inform our understanding of contemporary environmental challenges. Pre- or co-requisites recommended: EMES 101, 200 or 201.

courses.title: Coastal Environmental Change
courses.description: An exploration of the large-scale evolution of coastal environments, including relevance of geologic setting, wave and sediment transport processes, the evolution of beach and barrier island morphology, and issues of coastal environmental management. Course previously offered as GEOL 310/MASC 316.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EMES 101,103, 200, 201, or 401; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Earth Systems in a Changing World
courses.description: This course presents an integrated view of our planet, how it evolved during the past, why it has changed (and continues to change), and what makes Earth a habitable planet. Course previously offered as MASC 314.

courses.title: Marine Life in a Fluid World
courses.description: This course examines how the functioning of marine organisms and ecosystems is impacted by water motion. Hydrodynamic forces as applied to locomotion and disturbance. Advective and diffusive transport as applied to nutrient supply and acquisition, larval transport, phytoplankton dynamics. The role of ocean circulation in establishing environmental conditions and distributions of organisms. Covers processes from the microscale to the ocean basin scale.

courses.title: Marine Life in a Fluid World Laboratory
courses.description: Field trips to sites in coastal North Carolina and lab experiments that introduce students to water motion in the marine environment and its impacts on marine organisms and ecosystems. Reinforces concepts taught in EMES 320. Offered at the Institute of Marine Sciences as part of the Morehead City Field Site.

courses.title: Geology of North America
courses.description: General introduction to the geologic evolution of North America through intensive study of a particular region. Includes mandatory Spring Break field trip. Course previously offered as GEOL 221/EMES 221.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EMES 72H, 101, 200, or 201; Permission of instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Water in Our World: Introduction to Hydrologic Science and Environmental Problems
courses.description: This introductory course will cover two broad themes: the physical processes of the hydrologic cycle and how human use (and abuse) of freshwater resources can lead to major environmental problems. PX credit for ENEC/EMES 324 + 324L. PL credit for ENEC/EMES 324. Course previously offered as GEOL 324.

courses.title: Water in Our World Laboratory
courses.description: Students will conduct laboratory and field experiments to reinforce the topics covered in ENEC/GEOL 324. PX credit for ENEC/EMES 324 + 324L. Course previously offered as GEOL 324L.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics for Environmental Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to the physical principles that can be used to describe, understand and predict water motion in natural water bodies. Fluids at rest and in motion. Conservation of mass and momentum. Forces that drive and resist fluid motion. Energy conservation. Scaling and dimensional analysis. Principles developed in lectures will be applied to understand water motion in rivers and streams, lakes, and the ocean. Previously offered as EMES 460.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, MATH 232 and PHYS 114 or PHYS 118.

courses.title: Marine Fisheries Ecology
courses.description: Gives students a foundation in population biology and the ecological processes that influence populations of economically important fish and shellfish. Students will gain practical quantitative skills including statistical analyses, model development, and data visualization. Familiarity with introductory statistics concepts is preferred but not necessary.

courses.title: Special Topics in Earth, Marine, and Environmental Sciences
courses.description: Topics and instructors vary from semester to semester. Course may be repeated. Course previously offered as GEOL 390/GEOL 390H. Permission of the department. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Earth, Marine, and Environmental Sciences
courses.description: Directed readings with laboratory study on a selected topic. Course previously offered as MASC 395. Permission of a faculty research director.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 8 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.title: Independent Study in Earth, Marine, and Environmental Sciences
courses.description: Independent study under the supervision of a selected instructor. Learning contract required. May be repeated up to four times for a maximum of 12 credits. Course previously offered as GEOL 396. Permission of the instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.title: Physical Oceanography
courses.description: For graduate students and upper-level undergraduates. Descriptive oceanography, large-scale wind-driven and thermohaline circulations, ocean dynamics, regional and nearshore/estuarine physical processes, waves, tides. Three lectures per week. Course previously offered as GEOL 506/MASC 506.

courses.title: Geochemistry
courses.description: Dive into the world of geochemistry, now enriched with data analytics and machine learning techniques. Engage with thermodynamics, kinetics, and isotope geochemistry through a contemporary lens. This course is a reimagined version tailored for the forward-thinking Earth, Marine and Environmental scientists. Previously offered as GEOL 405/MASC 455.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EMES 101, 200, or 201; permission of instructor for those students who lack the prerequisites.

courses.title: Introduction to Geophysics
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of global geophysics: gravity, seismology, magnetism, heat, and plate tectonics. Both shallow and deep processes are considered. Emphasis is aimed at problem solving by applying concepts. Course previously offered as GEOL 406.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, PHYS 114 or 118, and either PHYS 115 or 119.

courses.title: Shallow Geophysics: Geological, Archaeological and Environmental Applications
courses.description: The course focuses on the use of shallow geophysical principles and techniques to address geological, archaeological, and environmental problems. The course will study the strengths and weaknesses of geophysical techniques in various geologic settings and how to collect and interpret field data for defined applications. Written reports and group projects will be required.

courses.title: Earth Processes in Environmental Systems
courses.description: Principles of geological and related Earth systems sciences are applied to analyses of environmental phenomena. The link between the lithosphere and other environmental compartments is explored through case studies of environmental issues. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour a week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 102, GEOL 200, and MATH 231; and PHYS 115 or 119; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Oceanic Processes in Environmental Systems
courses.description: Principles of analysis of the ocean, coast, and estuarine environments and the processes that control these environments are applied to the analysis of environmental phenomena. Case studies of environmental issues. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour a week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, BIOL 101, CHEM 102, ENEC 222, MATH 231, PHYS 115 or PHYS 119; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Principles and Methods of Teaching Earth Science
courses.description: Required preparation: any introductory geology course. This course develops the knowledge and skills teachers need to implement student-centered, inquiry-based earth science instruction at any level level by teaching instructional design and cognitive science and learning theories. Primary literature review and development of lesson modules will be complemented by classroom observations and teaching experiences in formal and informal settings. Course previously offered as GEOL 412.

courses.title: Limnology
courses.description: This course explores the interdisciplinary study of inland waters, including lakes, rivers, wetlands, and groundwater. It examines the physical, chemical, and biological processes that shape freshwater ecosystems. Topics include lake formation, water movement, biogeochemical cycling, aquatic organisms, and food web dynamics. Students will analyze how these factors interact to influence water quality, biodiversity, and ecosystem functioning. The course also addresses contemporary issues such as eutrophication, climate change impacts, and invasive species. Through lectures, data analysis exercises, and case studies, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of limnological principles and their application to water resource management and conservation.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, BIOL 101 and CHEM 101; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Environmental Systems Modeling
courses.description: This course explores principles and strategies for studying environmental phenomena, and presents methods for developing explanatory and predictive models of environmental systems, e.g., predator-prey, estuaries, greenhouse gases, and ecosystem material cycles.

courses.title: Surface Processes and Landscape Evolution
courses.description: The interplay among the fluxes of water, energy, and sediment through geologic time sculpt landscapes and drive environmental change. In both lectures and laboratory exercises, students will learn how simple physical principles applied to rivers and hillslopes allow us to understand the evolution of topography and mountain belts, predict hazards arising from floods, landslides and debris flows, and lead to sustainable management of natural resources such as soil. Previously offered as GEOL 417.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, EMES 200 and EMES 201; permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- or corequisites.

courses.title: Mountain Belts
courses.description: This course will explore mountain belts with a focus on the tectonic processes and climatic interactions that sculpt their deep structure and surface expression. We will discuss all components of mountain systems including fold-thrust belts, accretionary prisms, basins, and the magmatic arc. The course will largely follow the lifecycle of orogens, from subduction initiation, to Cordilleran orogenesis, collisional orogenesis, and ultimate orogenic collapse. An emphasis will be placed on techniques that are used to study different parts of the system. This course is designed for graduate students and upper-level undergraduates.

courses.title: Archaeological Geology
courses.description: The application of geological principles and techniques to the solution of archaeological problems. Studies geological processes and deposits pertinent to archaeological sites, geologic framework of archaeology in the southeastern United States, and techniques of archaeological geology. Field trips to three or more sites; written reports required. Course previously offered as GEOL 421. Permission of the instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Physics of the Earth's Interior
courses.description: Origin of the solar system: the nebular hypothesis. Evolution of the earth and its accretionary history. Earthquakes: plate tectonics and the interior of the earth. The earth's magnetic field. Mantle convection.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, MATH 383, and either PHYS 201 and 211 or 311 and 401.

courses.title: Introduction to Field Geology
courses.description: Introduction to geologic field methods. Includes making observations, mapping, identification of structures and features, and interpretation to solve basic geologic problems. Many field trips. Course previously offered as GEOL 425.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, GEOL 200 and 201; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Major World Rivers and Global Change: From Mountains to the Sea
courses.description: What are the linkages between rivers and global change? This course examines the hydrological, geological and biogeochemical processes that control material flux from land to the oceans via rivers. Course previously offered as MASC 432.

courses.title: Ancient Climates: Greenhouse and Icehouse Worlds
courses.description: This course examines Earth's climate system across geologic time using an inquiry-driven approach. Students investigate how paleoclimate proxies, including isotopic, sedimentary, and biological records, are used to reconstruct past environmental conditions. The course incorporates analysis of paleoclimate datasets and primary scientific literature to evaluate mechanisms of climate change across multiple timescales. A semester-long research project guides students in developing questions, applying analytical methods, and synthesizing evidence. Emphasis is placed on data interpretation, uncertainty, and integration of multiple lines of evidence and provides a foundation for understanding Earth system processes and their relevance to contemporary climate change. Previously offered as GEOL432.

courses.title: Wetland Hydrology
courses.description: Study of wetland ecosystems with particular emphasis on hydrological functioning, the transition from terrestrial to aquatic systems, wetlands as filtration systems, and exchange between wetlands and other environments. Course previously offered as MASC 433.

courses.title: Blue Carbon and Coastal Environments
courses.description: Readings and discussions about processes in traditional "Blue Carbon" environments (marshes, sea grass beds, and mangroves) and an exploration of carbon burial in other coastal ecosystems such as floodplains and oyster reefs. Course previously offered as MASC 434. Permission of the instructor is required.

courses.title: Principles of Environmental Consulting: Mechanics of Groundwater Flow
courses.description: Water is an essential resource for all life, and the availability of clean water will become one of the most important socio-political and economic discussions over the coming decades. This course covers fundamentals of groundwater storage, subsurface flow, and contaminant transport, emphasizing the role of groundwater in the hydrologic cycle, the relation of groundwater flow to geologic structure, and the management of contaminated groundwater and drinking water resources. Course previously offered as GEOL 435.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EMES 324; MATH 232; PHYS 114 or 118; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Geochemistry of Natural Waters
courses.description: Required preparation, one introductory geology course. Survey of processes affecting the compositions of streams, lakes, the ocean, and shallow ground waters. Course previously offered as GEOL 436.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, CHEM 102 and MATH 231; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Principles of Seismology
courses.description: Descriptive account of global seismology, earthquake distribution, and focal mechanics. Principles of geometrical optics and applications to imaging the earth's interior. Principles of seismic prospecting of hydrocarbon and geothermal reservoirs. Course previously offered as GEOL 440.
