courses.title: Theory and Practice of Modern Dance Technique - Elementary-Level Elective
courses.description: An introduction to modern dance technique, history, and philosophy focusing on the physical principles of movement and their choreographic application. Students will participate in a combination of lectures and studio time.

courses.title: Analysis of Sport Skills I
courses.description: A professional preparation course in the skills, knowledge, safety, and teaching progressions of basketball and soccer.

courses.title: Analysis of Sport Skills II
courses.description: A professional preparation course in the skills, knowledge, safety, and teaching progressions of tennis and volleyball.

courses.title: Coaching Principles
courses.description: A professional preparation course for teaching and coaching. Includes basic instruction in coaching education and principles, pedagogy for coaching, conditioning for athletes, and team building.

courses.title: Health and Physical Education in the Elementary School
courses.description: This course deals with methods and materials of health and physical education in school levels kindergarten through sixth grade. Required of elementary education majors. Does not count toward physical education major.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education
courses.description: A study of problems related to body mechanics and the needs of the physically handicapped student.

courses.title: Fitness Management
courses.description: Students develop a working knowledge of theories, principles, and operating procedures involved in managing programs, staff, and facilities in the health/fitness industry, including management, marketing, operations, legal aspects.

courses.title: Introduction to Sport Administration
courses.description: In this course, students are introduced to the policies and problems of organizing and administering sport in public and private settings.

courses.title: International Sport Management
courses.description: Because sport cuts across all international boundaries, students must understand the global implications of the sport industry. This course introduces students to the organization, governance, business activities, and intercultural issues in international sport.

courses.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II
courses.description: This course is targeted to students enrolled in Department of Exercise and Sport Science majors as well as other students with interest in medical professions. This course involves a systematic approach to human anatomy and physiology with an emphasis on the metabolic, endocrine, digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, integumentary and immune systems.

courses.title: Women and Sport
courses.description: A broad based perspective of women's participation in sport including history of participation, physiological differences, and socio-cultural influences including work, politics, family, economics, and gender roles and identity.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Sports Medicine
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce the undergraduate student to the sports medicine profession and to provide the basic knowledge and skills necessary to recognize, evaluate, and treat injuries to the head and face, cervical spine, thoracic region, abdominal/urogenital region, and extremities.

courses.title: Research in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: An introduction to research in the fields of physical education, exercise, and sport science with emphasis on understanding and application of research findings.

courses.title: Human Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: EXSS 275L is a basic human anatomy laboratory course designed to accompany EXSS 155 or EXSS 175. For students endeavoring to major in the allied health professions.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175 with a grade of B or better.

courses.title: Human Physiology
courses.description: Instructor may approve equivalents for prerequisite. A lecture course in elementary physiology, covering the various systems of the body.

courses.title: Emergency Care of Athletic Injuries and Illnesses
courses.description: Recommended preparation, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175. Theory and practice of basic first aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and the acute care of athletic injuries.

courses.title: Special Topics in EXSS
courses.description: Variable topics course in Exercise and Sports Science. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Theory and Practice of Modern Dance Technique - Intermediate-Level Elective
courses.description: An intensive study of modern dance technique and philosophy, focusing on the physical principles of movement and their choreographic application. One hour seminar and four and one-half hours laboratory.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 191; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Internship in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide the student with a structured, supervised practical experience in exercise and sport science professional settings. Students will be individually mentored by on-site supervisors who will be responsible for assigning and assessing meaningful work, as well as providing training, feedback, and opportunities for participation in organizational activities. Students will receive guidance for professional development from their lead instructor in the form of in-class activities, assignments, and guest speakers. Restricted to EXSS general majors (not Fitness Professional or Sport Administration) with at least junior-year standing who are within 4 semesters of graduation, and a minimum 2.0 GPA (overall and within major).

courses.title: The Art and Science of Expertise
courses.description: This course is structured around theoretical frameworks of expertise development, self-regulation, and creativity. Topics will include deliberate practice, the psychology of motivation and positive functioning, accountability, personal narratives, competitiveness, leadership, resilience, flow, learned optimism, performance measurement, well-being, and the role of creativity and design in solving complex problems. Students will learn to compose, design, build, present, or perform a work that reflects immersion in their chosen domain of expertise; to explain the influence of creativity, technologies, materials, and processes on performance and expression; and to evaluate their own and others' work through structured critique to create value in creative domains.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Sport Marketing
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to marketing within the sports industry, including the unique aspects of the sport product and sport consumer markets.

courses.title: Sport Facility and Event Management
courses.description: This course is designed to develop practical competencies necessary for effectively managing sport facilities and events while providing students with experiential learning opportunities inside and outside the classroom.

courses.title: Finance and Economics of Sport
courses.description: This course provides an understanding of the financial and economic growth of sport, economic theory applied to the sport industry, and the basic principles and methods of sound fiscal control.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, ECON 101 and EXSS 221; Pre- or corequisite, STOR 151 or STOR 155 recommended.

courses.title: The Role of Intercollegiate Athletics in Higher Education
courses.description: This course is designed to help students interested in working in college sports understand what that role has been and might be in the future, with an emphasis on maximizing the educational value of intercollegiate athletic participation and the integration of athletics with academic and student life dimensions on college campuses.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Sport
courses.description: This course provides a foundation in general legal concepts and familiarizes students with the legal areas they are most likely to encounter as managers in the sports and fitness industry.

courses.title: Predictive Analytics in Sport
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with an introduction to predictive analytics utilizing regression-based modeling approaches. As a CURE course, students will learn the iterative process of model building through trial and error and by working with other students on hands-on problems. At the conclusion of this course, students will be able to analyze sport-related data using predictive analytics, whether the dependent variable is continuous or binary in nature. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, STOR 151 or 155 with a grade of B or better.

courses.title: Sport Business Venture
courses.description: This course will provide students an introduction to practical entrepreneurial business tools for starting a new business (or for use in an existing organization) in the sport industry.

courses.title: Sport Communication
courses.description: This course introduces students to professional communication in sport contexts. Contexts of focus are media (i.e., broadcast and digital) and organizations related to sport. Through readings, in-class activities, lectures, group projects, and guest speakers, students learn about the development of communication professions and practices in sport media and organizations, strategic approaches to communication challenges and opportunities in these contexts, the role of research and social forces in sport communication, and vocational paths in sport communication.

courses.title: Sociocultural Aspects of Sport and Exercise
courses.description: This course will enhance students' understandings about social and cultural dimensions of sport and exercise contexts. Through directed readings, classroom conversations, assignments/projects, and guest speakers, students in this course will learn how these sociocultural realities 1) are explored through academic research, and 2) impact sport and exercise policy, programs, and innovation, and 3) impact sport and exercise constituents, such as participants, planners, leaders, and advocates. This is an elective course for all junior/senior EXSS majors.

courses.title: Sports Nutrition
courses.description: The role of nutrition in maximizing physical performance, promoting health, and controlling body weight. Includes individual nutritional assessments.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 256 or EXSS 276 or NUTR 240.

courses.title: Foundations of Sports Medicine Rehabilation
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce undergraduate students to the basic principles and skills used to rehabilitate sport related injuries with an emphasis on musculoskeletal injuries.

courses.title: Therapeutic Modalities
courses.description: This is an advanced athletic training course, designed to provide the athletic training student with knowledge and skills necessary for treating injuries.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 265, EXSS 288, and EXSS 366.

courses.title: Therapeutic Exercise and Rehabilitation
courses.description: This is an advanced athletic training course, designed to provide the athletic training student with knowledge and skills necessary for rehabilitating injuries.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 265, EXSS 288, EXSS 366, and EXSS 367.

courses.title: Athletic Training Seminar
courses.description: A presentation of the historical and current perspectives on athletic training, including techniques for organizing and administering athletic training programs.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 288.

courses.title: General Medicine in Athletic Training
courses.description: Advanced course focusing on understanding instrumentation used in assessing internal injury related to sport. Pharmacology, drug testing, psychosocial interventions, and selected emergency procedures pertaining to athletic injury are also presented.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 265 and EXSS 288.

courses.title: Physiological Basis of Human Performance
courses.description: Instructor may approve equivalents for EXSS prerequisites. Students must take laboratory section along with class. The application of physiological principles to sport and physical activity. Both immediate and chronic adaptations to exercise are studied. Two lecture and two laboratory hours a week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

courses.title: Neuromuscular Control and Learning
courses.description: This course introduces neuromuscular control and motor learning through a general understanding of neuroanatomy/neurophysiology, sensory contributions to human movement, initiation and regulation of voluntary movement, and the acquisition of motor skills. Course topics include central and peripheral nervous system functions in the production and regulation of human movement, neural pathways and control mechanisms, and enhancement of motor learning in the rehabilitation and training settings. Honors version available.

courses.title: Biomechanics of Sport
courses.description: This course introduces the principles of biomechanics, including kinematics, kinetics, projectile motion, fluid forces and statics analysis. It includes the application of both kinematics and kinetic variables to joint motion and sport activities. Instructor may approve equivalents for EXSS prerequisite.

courses.title: Undergraduate Learning Assistanship
courses.description: This course is designed for undergraduate students to provide course support to their peers. This course provides opportunities for students to prepare, demonstrate, and consult with their peers via in- and out-of-class activities. Students will gain an enhanced understanding of Exercise and Sport Science content with a lens towards explaining to less experienced students, gaining pedagogical knowledge and experience, and engaging in comprehensive, concise, and clear oral and written communication. EXSS Majors only; Successful completion, with a grade of C or higher, of the course you are assisting.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Sports Medicine Clinical
courses.description: This field experience offers implementation of theories and practices of athletic training and sports medicine under the supervision of a certified athletic trainer.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 265 or EXSS 288.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 5 total credits. 5 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research Course
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Majors preferred. Laboratory/research study addressing exercise and sport science questions. Requires final written report. Repeatable for six total credits.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Independent Studies in Exercise and Sport Science Elective
courses.description: Required preparation, any two relevant courses. Permission of the instructor. Individually designed in-depth study in an area of interest within exercise and sport science. Available to both majors and nonmajors under the supervision of selected EXSS faculty members.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Critical Analysis of Literature in Sport and Exercise Psychology
courses.description: This course will expose students to research in sport and exercise psychology using the C.R.E.A.T.E. (Consider, Read, Elucidate the hypotheses, Analyze and interpret the data, and Think of the next Experiment) framework. Students will follow the historical publications of one sport and exercise psychology research group to better understand the research process. Each research paper will be digested/critiqued in phases. Student will also formulate their own novel research questions and present them to the class.

courses.title: Theory and Application of Strength Training and Conditioning for Fitness Professionals
courses.description: Students will learn to design an individualized fitness plan for a "healthy" adult for common fitness goals by assessing their movement and fitness, exercise leadership, and program design. This class, in part, prepares students for the NASM certified personal training (CPT) certification.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

courses.title: Exercise Prescription for Special Populations
courses.description: Exercise benefits everybody. This course will teach evidence-based information for developing, modifying and implementing fitness programs for individuals with chronic disease, metabolic, cardiac, pulmonary, and other issues deemed as special populations. The knowledge and skills attained in this course will enhance any basic personal training certification and give a better understanding of working with what could be considered the general public.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 376.

courses.title: Exercise Testing and Prescription
courses.description: This course is designed to provide theoretical and practical knowledge in basic exercise testing and prescription for both healthy and select special populations. This course includes both lectures and a lab. Priority registration is given to EXSS- Fitness Professional students and permission to enroll is obtained by completing the form linked in the registration section in Connect Carolina.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 376.

courses.title: Athlete Performance and Sport Science
courses.description: This course invites students who are passionate about sport to explore how data science is transforming athletic performance. You will examine how data-driven approaches optimize strength, conditioning, physiology, psychology, nutrition, and overall wellness. Through hands-on projects and applied case studies, you will learn to track physical performance, monitor health and recovery, and analyze psychological factors that influence success.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisite, EXSS 273, PSYC 210, or appropriate statistics course with permission of instructor.

courses.title: Program Planning in Recreation Services
courses.description: This experiential course covers the concepts and skills used in program planning. Students apply their program planning skills to real-life situations and implement a recreation program for a community agency. Previously offered as RECR 420.

courses.title: Sport Sales and Revenue Production Seminar
courses.description: This course will analyze and produce skills essential to the revenue production and sales process commonly found in the sport business. In this class students will develop an understanding and appreciation for the sales and revenue-production process related to a sport franchise and/or organization.

courses.title: Introduction to Leadership and Group Dynamics
courses.description: An analysis of the techniques, methods, and motives of group and community leaders. Special attention is focused upon the roles of organizational structure, personnel policies, and in-service training programs. Previously offered as RECR 430.

courses.title: Exercise Technique
courses.description: This course is designed to teach students how to lead and coach a group of individuals toward movement proficiency in common athletic-based exercises.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

courses.title: Essentials of Corrective Exercise Training
courses.description: Students will learn to explain, design, and execute a corrective exercise program to improve movement quality. Students will be introduced to skills such as range of motion, strength, and movement quality assessments. This class, in-part, prepares students for the NASM corrective exercise specialist (CES) certification.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

courses.title: Functional Anatomy
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of joint mechanics. It exposes students to motions of the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine as well as the extremities, and relates these concepts to movement of the body during specific activities.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 385.

courses.title: Sports Performance Training
courses.description: This course focuses on the foundational knowledge needed to train athletes, including performance assessment, coaching exercise technique, and program design. This class, in part, prepares students for the NSCA Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS) certification.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256; or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276.

courses.title: Performance Enhancement Specialization for Health Professionals
courses.description: This course is designed for certified athletic trainers (ATC) and gives them advanced rehab and performance skills that can be used during an athlete's return to sport progression. Students will learn to assess movement quality and performance, lead an individual through common strength and conditioning exercises, and write a basic performance plan based on NASM strategies. This class, in-part, prepares students for the NASM performance enhancement specialist (PES) certification.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 366 and EXSS 368.

courses.title: Field Experience in Sport Administration
courses.description: This field experience offers implementation of theory and the practical application of sport administration in a sport organization worksite, under the direct supervision of a business professional.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 221 and at least two of the following: EXSS 322, 323, 324, 326; permission of the instructor required for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Sport Injury Epidemiology
courses.description: This course will introduce the student to the public health importance and epidemiology of injuries and other medical conditions in sport and physical activity. Previously offered as EXSS 373.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 273, PSYC 210, or appropriate statistics course with permission of instructor.

courses.title: Data Science Applications in Exercise, Sport, and Movement Science
courses.description: The goal of this course is to give students an introduction to and hands-on experience with all phases of the data science process and applications to exercise, sport, and movement science. Topics that will be covered include data formats, loading, and cleaning. This course will also concentrate on the concepts and structures necessary to design and implement a database system as well as basic programming with open source software to help navigate databases and conduct basic analyses. Fundamental ethical issues in data science will also be covered.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 273, PSYC 210, or appropriate statistics course at the permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Exercise Endocrinology
courses.description: Advanced course examining the responses of the endocrine system to exercise and the adaptations that occur with exercise training. Provides the fundamentals necessary for exercise science and allied health science students to understand the integral role that the endocrine system plays in exercise.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256, or EXSS 175 and EXSS 276; and EXSS 376.

courses.title: Neuromechanics of Human Movement
courses.description: This course explores interactions between the nervous and musculoskeletal systems via integration of concepts from neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, anatomy, neuromuscular control, and biomechanics. Topics include muscle mechanics, sensorimotor function, joint stability, movement disorders, neurocognition, and neuroplasticity following injury and disease.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 155 or EXSS 175; and EXSS 380 and EXSS 385.

courses.title: Biopsychosocial Aspects of Sport Injury
courses.description: This course is designed to explore the theory and research related to the biopsychosocial approach to treating patients experiencing sport injury and undergoing rehabilitation. Application and synthesis of biopsychosocial theories and biopsychosocial therapy interventions into sport injury research and clinical practice will occur. The focus is on theory and application of various psychological concepts.

courses.title: Fundamentals of MRI for Brain Mapping
courses.description: An introduction to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) methods and applications for mapping brain networks, with a specific focus on understanding how MRI is used to study brain and behavior relationships.

courses.title: Neurotrauma Involving the Head and Neck: Overview of Neurophysiology, Assessment, and Management
courses.description: This course is designed to expand on graduate and upper-level undergraduate student's foundational knowledge to provide an advanced overview of neurotrauma associated anatomy, physiology, assessment, and management associated with sports and physical activity, with a specific focus on concussion and cervical spine/spinal cord injury. The course will include higher level concepts, application, and synthesis of knowledge concerning these areas of focus.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, EXSS 155 and EXSS 256 or equivalent courses at the instructor's discretion.

courses.title: Special Topics in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: Variable topics course in exercise and sports science for undergraduate and graduate students.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Practicum in Physical Fitness and Wellness
courses.description: A field experience (i.e., internship) in a local fitness & wellness or strength and conditioning setting designed for students to apply their classroom knowledge and skills, in a worksite of their choice, under the direct supervision of certified professionals. This class is only open to EXSS - Fitness Professional students. Permission to enroll is obtained by attending a practicum Permission to enroll is obtained by attending a practicum registration meeting one semester in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 9 total completions.

courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.description: Required preparation, a cumulative grade point average meeting the University standard and permission of the department. Directed independent research under the supervision of a faculty advisor who teaches in the exercise and sport science curriculum.

courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.description: Required preparation, a cumulative grade point average meeting the University standard and permission of the department. Preparation of an honors thesis and an oral examination on the thesis.

courses.title: Applied Statistics and Research Methods in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: Required preparation, undergraduate statistics course. Applied statistical analysis - interpretation of data from exercise and sport science. Emphasis: choosing method of analysis, using statistics software to run analyses. Major topics: experimental and nonexperimental research design, sampling, hypothesis testing, power calculation, t-tests, ANOVA, correlation, simple and multiple regression, and chi square.

courses.title: Research Design and Methods
courses.description: Required preparation, any undergraduate statistics course. Builds heavily upon material presented in EXSS 700. Planning, conducting, and reporting of research. Thesis writing and writing for publication. Problem-solving and practical experience in applied statistical analysis, interpretation, and presentation of data from the field of exercise and sport science.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Management of Athletic Injuries
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Designed to provide basic knowledge and skills that aid in the prevention and treatment of injuries common to athletics.

courses.title: Human Anatomy for Athletic Trainers
courses.description: Graduate standing in exercise and sport science or permission of the instructor. The study of gross human anatomy, with emphasis on the functional and clinical aspects of the neck, back, and extremities as related to athletic injuries.

courses.title: Psychological Considerations for Injury and Rehabilitation
courses.description: Athletic training graduate students only. Psychological impact of injury and rehabilitation on the injured athlete. Stress from injury, coping skills for the rigors of rehabilitation, and the improvement of communication skills in order to better the relationship between the athletic trainer, the injured athlete, and the injured athlete's coach.

courses.title: Sports Medicine Analysis: Special Problems Related to Sports Medicine
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Problem and research oriented.

courses.title: Clinical Methods in Athletic Training
courses.description: Analysis of theories and techniques used in clinical sports medicine settings.

courses.title: Advanced Muscular Assessment and Treatment
courses.description: Discussion of mechanical properties and healing of musculoskeletal tissues throughout the life cycle, and laboratory/seminar units concerned with assessment and treatment of musculoskeletal pathology.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 730, 732, and 736; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Laboratory Techniques in Sports Medicine
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to measurement techniques used in sports medicine/athletic training research. Course meetings involve lecture and laboratory sessions which encompass data collection, analysis, and interpretation techniques.

courses.title: Practicum in Exercise, Sport, and Movement Science
courses.description: Graduate standing in exercise and sport science or permission of the instructor. The implementation of theories and practices in a professional setting under the direction of a professional with expertise in exercise, sport and/or movement science.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Administration of Sport
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Policies and problems of organization and administration of athletic programs in colleges.

courses.title: Social Issues in Exercise and Sport
courses.description: A comprehensive study of race and gender discrimination, adherence, value development, violence, and other socialization factors in youth, collegiate, and Olympic sport.

courses.title: Collegiate Sport Marketing
courses.description: Graduate standing required. This course is designed to develop a thorough understanding of sport marketing principles and their application to collegiate athletics.

courses.title: Organizational and Financial Management of Sport
courses.description: Graduate standing in exercise and sport science or permission of the instructor. The study of administrative structures and financial concerns of collegiate athletic programs. An intensive study of NCAA regulations is included.

courses.title: College Sport Facility and Event Management
courses.description: This course provides students with necessary knowledge and skills to manage college-sport facilities and plan a complete sport event. Students also evaluate facility functions related to risk and event management.

courses.title: Legal Issues in Collegiate Sport
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the United States legal system, legal principles, and legal issues related to intercollegiate athletics.

courses.title: NCAA Governance and Compliance
courses.description: The implementation of theories and practices in a professional setting under the direction of a competent practitioner.

courses.title: Sport Administration Leadership Seminar I
courses.description: Successful completion of first year in sport administration graduate program. An introduction of organizational leadership concepts in a practical applied context. Students will lead class discussion tying relevant current events with leadership theory.

courses.title: Sport Administration Leadership Seminar II
courses.description: Successful completion of first year in sport administration graduate program. An introduction of organizational leadership concepts in a practical applied context. Students will lead class discussion tying relevant current events with leadership theory.

courses.title: Motor Learning
courses.description: A study of the physical and psychological factors that influence skill acquisition and performance in sport and exercise, including applications to teaching and coaching.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 380; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Physiology of Exercise
courses.description: The study of the physical, biochemical, and environmental factors that influence human performance. Emphasis is placed on metabolic, cardiovascular, respiratory, muscular, and endocrine systems. Three hours of lecture and two hours of laboratory per week.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, EXSS 256 or EXSS 276 or EXSS 376.

courses.title: Clinical Exercise Prescription and Testing
courses.description: This course concentrates on the knowledge and skills necessary for providing exercise testing and prescription in the clinical setting, emphasizing cardiac rehabilitation.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 376; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Nutritional Aspects of Exercise
courses.description: Graduate standing in physical education or permission of the instructor. Exploration of the role of macronutrients and micronutrients as they apply to exercise, physical conditioning, and competition. Students obtain experience in dietary analysis as it applies to athletic populations.

courses.title: Assessment of Physiological Functions in Exercise
courses.description: Designed to develop laboratory techniques and experimental design skills as applied to the physiology of human performance.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 780; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Exercise Physiology
courses.description: Required preparation, completion of a graduate level exercise physiology course. Graduate standing required. This course deals with current and rapidly developing aspects of the exercise physiology field. Specifically enhancing and adding to the content area of basic physiology acquired in EXSS 780.

courses.title: Seminar in Exercise Physiology
courses.description: Graduate standing in exercise and sport science or permission of the instructor. In-depth study of selected advanced topics in exercise physiology. Emphasis on metabolism, biochemical, and cardiorespiratory physiology, with student presentations on selected topics.

courses.title: Practicum in Exercise Physiology
courses.description: The implementation of theories and practices of fitness or cardiac rehabilitation in a professional setting under the direction of an experienced practitioner.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, EXSS 410L, 780, or 781; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Special Topics in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor. The study of special topics directed by an authority in the field.

courses.title: Research in Exercise and Sport Science
courses.description: Graduate standing in exercise and sport science or permission of the instructor. Individually designed research projects conducted by students under the direction of a graduate faculty member.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Poetic Roots of Hip-Hop: Hidden Histories of African American Rhyme
courses.description: What are the roots of hip-hop's masterful rhymes and tongue-tripping flow? This seminar explores hip-hop's poetic prehistory, looking to the rhyming and oral poetics that have long defined African American experience. In so doing, we'll uncover hidden histories of everyday eloquence and explore spoken/sung poetry's role in marking cultural identity. Honors version available.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Anthropology of the Caribbean
courses.description: Theories and examples of how Caribbean people live, act, and see themselves within various cultural, social, economic, and political contexts across time. Attention to North American views of the Caribbean.

courses.title: Everyday Cultures: Folklore in America
courses.description: An introduction to the study of creativity and aesthetic expression in everyday life, considering both traditional genres and contemporary innovations in the material, verbal, and musical arts.

courses.title: Environmental Humanities
courses.description: While scientific research and technological innovation are critical to addressing the ecological challenges of our time, the environmental humanities can offer equally vital insights by examining how cultural values, artistic expressions, and ethical perspectives have formed -- and been formed by -- humans' relationships with the environment. By consulting artists, poets, writers, and thinkers, students will untangle the intertwined connection between ''nature'' and ''culture,'' tapping into key existential questions about what it means to be humans who not only live in this world, but who seek to solve the environmental problems that they have caused or exacerbated.

courses.title: U.S. Historical Geographies
courses.description: A study of selected past geographies of the United States with emphasis on the significant geographic changes in population, cultural, and economic conditions through time. Previously offered as FOLK/GEOG 454. (GHA)

courses.title: Fairy Tales
courses.description: A study of fairy tales as historical artifacts that reveal the concerns of their times and places, as narrative structures capable of remarkable transformation, and as artistic performances drawing upon the expressive resources of multiple media, intended to challenge conventional presuppositions about the genre.

courses.title: Art, Nature, and Climate Change
courses.description: This course will draw from folkloristic and anthropological theories and methods to explore how people turn to their artistic expressions--such as storytelling, painting, cooking, weaving, and more--to understand, react, and adapt to environmental changes, ranging from natural disasters to controversial land management policies. By attending to case studies of climate change at a geographically expansive scale, the course connects the local to the global and invites students to consider how environmental changes and creative expressions manifest in disparate cultural contexts. Our examination of globally diverse examples is counterbalanced by immersive experiential activities in and speakers from North Carolina.

courses.title: Southern Legacies: The Descendants Project
courses.description: In this Course-based Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) class, students will explore the legacy of racial terrorism in North Carolina. Students will search archival sources to discover the family histories of lynching victims, tracing those families to the present, interviewing their descendants, and working with communities to build public awareness of - and perhaps public memorials to - the victims of racial violence.

courses.title: Critical Issues in Contemporary Food Studies
courses.description: Students explore, analyze, and research the politics and ethics of food debates in contemporary American culture. These include the struggles of the National School Lunch Program, the Minimum Wage Act's effect on the restaurant business, and the impact of social media on body image. Through engaging a combination of media discourse on food politics, scholarly articles, and narratives of people working in the food system, students are invited into vibrant debates. By the end of the course, students will not only analyze food systems but also design and conduct original research projects that contribute to ongoing debates in Food Studies. Restricted to Food Studies Minors and American Studies majors.

courses.title: Ritual, Festival, and Public Culture
courses.description: This course explores rituals, festivals, and public cultural performances as forms of complex, collective, embodied creative expression. As sites of popular celebration, conflict resolution, identity definition, and social exchange, they provide rich texts for folkloristic study. We consider how local and global forces both sustain and challenge these forms.

courses.title: Religion and Anthropology
courses.description: Religion studied anthropologically as a cultural, social, and psychological phenomenon in the works of classical and contemporary social thought. Honors version available.

courses.title: Culture and Power in Southeast Asia
courses.description: The formation and transformation of values, identities, and expressive forms in Southeast Asia in response to forms of power. Emphasis on the impact of colonialism, the nation-state, and globalization.

courses.title: Medicine and Anthropology
courses.description: This course examines cultural understandings of health, illness, and medical systems from an anthropological perspective with a special focus on Western medicine.

courses.title: Traditions in Transition: Jewish Folklore and Ethnography
courses.description: This seminar examines Jewish stories, humor, ritual, custom, belief, architecture, dress, and food as forms of creative expression that have complex relationships to Jewish experience, representation, identity, memory, and tradition. What makes these forms of folklore Jewish, how do source communities interpret them, and how do ethnographers document them? Previously offered as FOLK 380/FOLK 505/JWST 380/JWST 505.

courses.title: Anthropology of the Body and the Subject
courses.description: Anthropological and historical studies of cultural constructions of bodily experience and subjectivity are reviewed, with emphasis on the genesis of the modern individual and cultural approaches to gender and sexuality.

courses.title: Graffiti, Gods, and Gardens: Urban Folklore
courses.description: What is the relationship between distinctive features of urban environments and the expressive forms found in those settings? This course explores the impact of the urban setting on folk traditions. We examine how people transform urban spaces into places of meaning through storytelling, festival, ritual, food, art, music, and dance.

courses.title: Vernacular Traditions in African American Music
courses.description: Explores performance traditions in African American music, tracing development from African song through reels, blues, gospel, and contemporary vernacular expression. Focuses on continuity, creativity, and change within African American aesthetics. Previously offered as FOLK 610/AAAD 432.

courses.title: Jewish Belonging/s: The Material Culture of Jewish Experience
courses.description: What makes an object "Jewish"? This seminar examines how we think about, animate, repurpose, and display "Jewish" objects in the public realm, cultural institutions, religious spaces, and the home. We consider how makers and users negotiate objects' various meanings within the domains of prayer, performance, entertainment, and exhibition. The class curates a final group exhibition of Jewish material culture based on original fieldwork.

courses.title: Discourse and Dialogue in Ethnographic Research
courses.description: Study of cultural variation in styles of speaking applied to collection of ethnographic data. Talk as responsive social action and its role in the constitution of ethnic and gender identities.

courses.title: Everyday Stories: Personal Narrative and Legend
courses.description: Oral storytelling may seem old-fashioned, but we tell true (or possibly true) stories every day. We will study personal narratives (about our own experiences) and legends (about improbable, intriguing events), exploring the techniques and structures that make them effective communication tools and the influence of different contexts and audiences.

courses.title: Topics in Folklore
courses.description: Topics vary from semester to semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Field Research
courses.description: Research at sites that vary.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Directed Readings in Folklore
courses.description: Permission of the department. Topic varies depending on the instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Myths and Epics of the Ancient Near East
courses.description: An examination of Babylonian, Canaanite, Egyptian, Hittite, and Sumerian texts from the prebiblical era, focusing on representative myths, epics, sagas, songs, proverbs, prophecies, and hymns. Honors version available.

courses.title: Gender and Performance: Constituting Identity
courses.description: Examines the culturally and historically variable ways in which individuals constitute themselves as cis- or transgendered subjects or nonbinary subjects, drawing upon extant expressive resources, modifying them, and expanding options available to others. Performance of self as the product of esthetically marked or unmarked, everyday actions.

courses.title: Oral History and Performance
courses.description: This course combines readings and field work in oral history with the study of performance as a means of interpreting and conveying oral history texts. Honors version available.

courses.title: Southern Music
courses.description: Explores the history of music in the American South from its roots to 20th-century musical forms, revealing how music serves as a window on the region's history and culture.

courses.title: Folklore in the South
courses.description: An issue-oriented study of Southern folklore, exploring the ways that vernacular artistic expression (from barns and barbecue to gospel and well-told tales) come to define both community and region.

courses.title: Introduction to Oral History
courses.description: Introduces students to the uses of interviews in historical research. Questions of ethics, interpretation, and the construction of memory will be explored, and interviewing skills will be developed through field work.

courses.title: Ethnographic Method
courses.description: Intensive study and practice of the core research methods of cultural and social anthropology.

courses.title: Observation and Interpretation of Religious Action
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Exercises (including field work) in learning to read the primary modes of public action in religious traditions, e.g., sermons, testimonies, rituals, and prayers.

courses.title: Studies In Folklore
courses.description: Topic varies from semester to semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Honors Project in Folklore
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. For honors candidates. Ethnographic and/or library research and analysis of the gathered materials, leading to a draft of an honors thesis.

courses.title: Honors Thesis in Folklore
courses.description: Writing of an honors thesis based on independent research conducted in FOLK 691H. Open only to senior honors candidates who work under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.title: Public Folklore
courses.description: A graduate seminar addressing theory and praxis in public sector cultural work. Focusing on public folklore, this course explores broad issues of representation, cultural politics, and cultural tourism.

courses.title: Performance Ethnography
courses.description: This seminar focuses on methods of ethnography and fieldwork ethics. Performance as theory and practice informs methodological inquiries as well as the analysis of specific ethnographic texts and case studies.

courses.title: Seminar in Performance and Cultural Studies
courses.description: This course focuses on performance-related issues in the emergent field of cultural studies.

courses.title: Seminar in Contemporary Performance Theory
courses.description: An advanced graduate seminar, this course will address recent developments and problems in performance theory. It will consider cross- and multidisciplinary approaches to performance as sites for consideration and debate.

courses.title: Approaches to Folklore Theory
courses.description: A systematic overview of the major issues and theoretical perspectives that have informed the study of folklore historically and that are emerging in contemporary scholarship.

courses.title: Art of Ethnography
courses.description: A field-based exploration of the pragmatic, ethical, and theoretical dimensions of ethnographic research, addressing issues of experience, aesthetics, authority, and worldview through the lens of cultural encounter. Field research required.

courses.title: Seminar in Folklore
courses.description: Graduate seminar exploring selected topics in the theory and practice of Folklore.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Directed Readings
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Independent reading programs for graduate students.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Directed Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topics and credit hours vary according to the needs and interests of the individual student and the professor supervising the research project.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.description: Research in a special field under the direction of staff members.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: La mode: Fashion in French Culture
courses.description: This seminar investigates what fashion has meant to French-speaking writers, artists, and philosophers through the centuries. We will explore key episodes in the history of French fashion and discover how French thinkers have interpreted the allure and significance of fashion from multiple perspectives. Taught in English; no knowledge of French required. First Year Seminar.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Wonder and Energy in Science Fiction
courses.description: This course explores critical approaches to science-fiction texts and media, paying particular attention to the energies that structure their worlds and to the experience of wonder. Course materials will be chosen from across the French-speaking world. Taught in English; no knowledge of French required.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Déjà vu. Medicine and Narration across Time and Space
courses.description: This seminar explores how French-speaking writers and artists have engaged with medical culture. Hallucinations, depression, hysteria, paranoia, anxiety, neurosis, body dysmorphic disorder, obsession, and pain are some symptoms that will be reflected in the narratives of this course. We will study a group of writers and artists across time and space who explore, adapt, and converse with contemporaneous medical learning in their creative works. Taught in English; no knowledge of French required. First Year Seminar.

courses.title: Elementary French I
courses.description: Introduces the essential elements of French structure and vocabulary and aspects of French and francophone culture. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Students may not receive credit for both FREN 101 and FREN 111.

courses.title: Elementary French II
courses.description: Continues the study of essential elements of French structure, vocabulary, and aspects of French and francophone culture. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Students may not receive credit for more than one of the following: FREN 102, 105 or 401.

courses.title: French for High Beginners
courses.description: Accelerated course that covers FREN 101 and 102 for students with previous study of French. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Students may not receive credit for both FREN 105 and FREN 102 or 401.

courses.title: Globalization and the French-Speaking World
courses.description: Gives students the opportunity to better understand the different facets of French-speaking regions across the modern world (including Africa, the West Indies, and North America) by looking at their geography, their historical and political development, varied cultural aspects, and their links with the United States. In English.

courses.title: The French Love Affair with Philosophy
courses.description: This course is for students who are interested in knowing more about the history and experience of thinking like philosophers. The course is taught in English.

courses.title: Food for Thought: Cultures of Cuisine in Modern France
courses.description: Exploration of French food culture in film, literature, and historical texts, examining gastronomy in relation to national and individual identity, immigration, cultural specificity, tradition and innovation, markets, sociability, and excess and lack. In English. Formerly offered as FREN 286.

courses.title: Intermediate French I
courses.description: Develops language skills for communication. Review of elementary French with increasing emphasis on reading and writing in the context of contemporary French and francophone culture. Students may not receive credit for both FREN 203 and 402. Honors version available.

courses.title: Intermediate French II in Context
courses.description: Continued development of language skills for communication through reading and discussion of texts and authentic materials. Emphasis on accurate grammar in written and oral expression. Students may not receive credit for both FREN 204 and 402. Honors version available.

courses.title: Conversation I
courses.description: Introductory conversation for building oral proficiency while increasing awareness of French culture. Emphasis on vocabulary and grammatical accuracy; writing activities support speaking. Honors version available.

courses.title: Literature and the French-Speaking World
courses.description: Skills for literary studies through poetry, theater, and prose from the Renaissance to the present. Lectures, discussions, and written assignments. Honors version available.

courses.title: Cultural and Linguistic Variety in the French-Speaking World
courses.description: French is evolving, changing, and becoming a multifaceted language, adapting to modernity and cultural realities. This course focuses on today's French across the French-speaking world and explores the diversity of relationships that French-speakers have with this shared heritage. Previously offered as FREN 250.

courses.title: French "Discoveries" of the Americas in Translation
courses.description: Exploration of cultural relations between France and the Americas from early modern colonial encounters to 21st-century perspectives on diversity and multiculturalism.

courses.title: Sex, Philosophy, and Politics: Revolutionary Literature in Translation
courses.description: Exploration of questions related to sex and gender during the French Revolution and their reflection in literature, philosophy, and art. In English.

courses.title: Francophone Caribbean Literature in Translation
courses.description: This course examines the literary, social, and political issues brought to the fore in 20th and 21st century Francophone Caribbean literature (e.g. Haiti, Guadeloupe, and Martinique) with a particular emphasis on language, identity, race, and gender.

courses.title: Course Correspondent Project in French
courses.description: Learning contract required. Students participating in UNC-led study abroad programs develop activities to supplement instruction in on-campus courses. Supervised by the on-campus instructor, students file reports on the sites, language, and culture of the country in which they are studying. Pass/Fail only. Permission of the instructor and the instructor's department.

courses.title: Special Topics in French, FC-GLOBAL
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary by each semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: French Composition and Grammar Review
courses.description: Recommended preparation, FREN 255, 260, or 262. Intensive grammar review and composition to improve accuracy and develop writing skills, using process and task-oriented approaches.

courses.title: Healthcare in France and the Francophone World
courses.description: Corequisite FREN 300. This course examines the evolution of the French healthcare system from its creation to today and the depiction of illnesses as well as healthcare workers in contemporary culture. Current issues related to health, illnesses, and healthcare in France and the Francophone World will be discussed.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 255, 260 or 262; Pre- or corequisite, FREN 300.

courses.title: LAC Recitation
courses.description: A recitation section or stand-alone course for selected courses that promote the use of foreign language proficiency across the curriculum (LAC). May count toward the major or minor in French. Co-registration required unless a stand-alone LAC course, contact instructor or view Notes to determine.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 204; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Conversation and Composition II
courses.description: Intermediate conversation to expand speaking skills through vocabulary building, discussion of selected texts, and activities that produce conversation. Ongoing development of writing skills.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 255, 260, or 262; pre- or corequisite, FREN 300.

courses.title: Communication Skills for Cultural Immersion
courses.description: Students will expand their active vocabulary, refine their mastery of grammar and hone communication skills to facilitate their cultural immersion during study abroad in Montpellier. Topics of current interest will allow students to explore French and regional culture while perfecting their written and oral expression and comprehension. Open only to students in France.

courses.title: French University Methodology through Literature
courses.description: Open only to students in Montpellier, France. Introduction to French literature through the study of a selection of representative texts. Prepares students for the academics required at a French university. Students will also gain knowledge and experience of the intellectual culture and educational organization of France.

courses.title: Imposteur!: Faking and False Identities in French and Francophone Drama and Film
courses.description: Examines how French-language plays and films explore questions of identity through stories of imposture, disguise, cross-dressing, and mistaken identity. Authors studied include Molière, Marivaux, De la Chenelière, and others.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 255, 260, or 262; Pre- or corequisite, FREN 300; permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisites.

courses.title: Business French
courses.description: Practice of vocabulary and discourse strategies pertinent to business-related activity in French. Readings and discussions emphasize cultural awareness for interaction in cross-cultural settings.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 255, 260 or 262; pre- or corequisite, FREN 300; permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisites.

courses.title: Crime and Literature in French and Francophone Contexts
courses.description: This course explores the depiction of crime in literature: from medieval tricksters and classical tyrants to romantic crimes of passion; from the destruction of social and ethical codes to the global victims of (civil) war.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Cultures of Resistance in the French-Speaking World
courses.description: Exploration of cultures, arts, theories, politics, and histories of resistance in France and the French-speaking world from 1789 to the present.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Approaches to French and Francophone Studies
courses.description: Focuses on important aspects of the culture, society, history, geography, politics, art, and literature of France and its regions as well as the French-speaking world.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: The Art and Power of Conversation: The Enlightenment Salon
courses.description: The Enlightenment has been called the "age of conversation" on account of its salons- sociable gatherings where men and women of different backgrounds assembled to debate issues of the day with wit and elegance and to discuss how to change society. This course offers a deep dive into salon culture, its development of the arts of spoken language and sociability, its impact on Enlightenment thought on key issues such as inequality, and its historical legacies.

courses.title: Current Societal Issues: France and Beyond
courses.description: Oral communication and composition on contemporary topics in French and francophone cultures. Study of cultural texts, articles from the French press, and video documents.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Bandes dessinées / Comics and Graphic Novels
courses.description: The course provides a survey of bandes dessinées and graphic novels (BDs) with a view to exploring how this medium has changed over time in the French-speaking world. Students will analyze the BDs' aesthetic, stylistic, compositional, and sociopolitical effects in works ranging from Tintin, Astérix, or Lucky Luke to a more recent and diverse array of authors and artists who all testify to the evolving role of the bandes dessinées.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 300, or one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Francophone Drama and Multimedia Productions
courses.description: French-language theater. Specific topics to be announced in advance by the instructor. Previously offered as FREN 380.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300, and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Francophone Poetry and Slam
courses.description: Specific topics to be announced in advance by the instructor. Previously offered as FREN 381.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300, and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Visual Francophone Studies
courses.description: Specific selections announced in advance by the instructor. Previously offered as FREN 382.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300, or one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Littérature et philosophie
courses.description: What is the philosophical novel? Fiction written by a philosopher? A philosophical book in disguise? A fun story that explores serious ideas? From eighteenth-century radical philosophy, the great social changes of the nineteenth century, to the existentialist and feminist literature of the twentieth century, we will read texts by Denis Diderot, Madame de Staël, Jean-Paul Sartre, and others.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 255, 260, or 262; Pre- or corequisite, FREN 300; permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisites.

courses.title: Les jeux - Games
courses.description: This course is dedicated to games. We will explore critical approaches to media, paying particular attention to the technologies underlying their use and to theories of mediation.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 255, 260, or 262; Pre- or corequisite, FREN 300; permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisites.

courses.title: Introduction to Translation
courses.description: Theory and practice of translation through a dual approach of conceptual readings and classroom discussion and workshops in interdisciplinary fields. Emphasizes cultural role of the translator as mediator.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Environment, Society, and Public Policy in Southern France
courses.description: The course focuses on the exploration of a range of problems posed by the effects of human activity on our environment and examines initiatives undertaken in France and specifically in the Occitania region to combat these problems. Course open to students in UNC in Montpellier Summer. Course taught in English.

courses.title: French and Francophone Studies to 1789
courses.description: An overview of literatures, cultures, and histories of the French-speaking world from Antiquity to 1789.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: French and Francophone Studies since 1789
courses.description: An overview of literatures, cultures, and histories of the French-speaking world since 1789.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Francophone Literature and Film
courses.description: Readings in francophone literatures from literary and cultural perspectives. Areas of study may vary (African, Canadian, European, etc.).
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Identity and Nationhood in Québécois Literature
courses.description: The evolution of identity and nationhood in Québécois literature from the 1960s to the present. Includes the study of francophone literature of immigration in Québec.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: The Evolution of Frenchness since WWII
courses.description: How wars, women's movements, immigration, and globalization have influenced the notion of Frenchness.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: French and European Transmigrations: Global Contexts
courses.description: Interdisciplinary studies of France's role in the construction of European identity.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Special Topics in French and Francophone Studies
courses.description: Possible topics include cinema, transnational francophone literatures, gender studies. In English.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Franco-Asian Encounters
courses.description: Examines the cultural encounters between France and Vietnam and China, the socio-historical context of French colonialism in Vietnam, and the literary and cultural production to which it gave rise.

courses.title: French New Wave Cinema
courses.description: Films of the major directors of the French New Wave of the 1950s through the 1970s, including Jean-Luc Godard, François Truffaut, and Eric Rohmer. Examination of earlier films informing these directors. The impact of the New Wave on global cinema. In English. Recommended preparation: FREN 260 or CMPL 143 or the equivalent.

courses.title: Paris/Versailles: The Court and the City in the 17th Century
courses.description: During Louis XIV's reign, the French monarchy reinforced its majesty through the power of art. Magnificent buildings, stunning spectacles, and laudatory literature enhanced the reputation of the king. At the same time, art and literature served as tools of resistance, as writers and artists produced overt critiques or subtle satires of the regime. We will study Louis XIV's France as a case study to understand the ambivalent social and political force of art.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: History of French Cinema I: 1895-1950
courses.description: Study of French cinema from 1895 through 1950, including early French film, silent cinema, surrealism, poetic realism, and postwar cinema. Concepts and vocabulary for film criticism. Conducted in English. Recommended preparation: FREN 260 or CMPL 143 or the equivalent.

courses.title: History of French Cinema II: 1950 to the Present
courses.description: Study of French cinema from 1950 to the present, including postwar cinema, the New Wave, and the French film industry in the age of globalization. Concepts and vocabulary for film criticism. Conducted in English. Recommended preparation: FREN 260 or CMPL 143 or the equivalent.

courses.title: Special Topics in French and Francophone Studies
courses.description: Examines selected topics in French and francophone studies. Content varies by semester and instructor.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Research for Advanced French Students
courses.description: Research project on topic agreed upon by the student and faculty member. Includes bibliographic work and research approaches.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Beginning Accelerated French
courses.description: Covers levels one and two of the basic language sequence in one semester. Designed for highly motivated undergraduate/graduate language learners, especially those who have experienced success with learning another language. Intensive approach to developing all skills but with an emphasis on speaking. Students may not receive credit for both FREN 401 and any of the following: FREN 101, 102, 105.

courses.title: Intermediate Accelerated French
courses.description: A continuation of FREN 401. Covers levels three and four in one semester. Develops all skills, with increasing emphasis on reading, writing, and cultural analysis. Designed for highly motivated undergraduate/graduate language learners, especially those who have experienced success with learning another language. Prepares students for advanced courses. Students may not receive credit for both FREN 402 and any of the following: FREN 203 and 204.

courses.title: Advanced Composition
courses.description: Review of advanced grammar. Exercises in translation from English into French of literary and critical materials. Free composition and training in the use of stylistic devices.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Old French
courses.description: An introductory course designed to enable students to read medieval texts with rapidity and accuracy. Phonology, morphology, semantics, and syntax. In English.

courses.title: Currents in Caribbean Literature
courses.description: Scrutinizes the political, philosophical, aesthetic, and literary movements produced in and about the Francophone Caribbean (Haiti, Guadeloupe, Martinique) and its signature texts.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300, and FREN 255, or 260, or 262.

courses.title: Literary and Cultural Theory in France
courses.description: A study of structuralist and poststructuralist methods in poetics, semiotics, psychoanalysis, sociology, and philosophy.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Muslim Women in France and the United States
courses.description: This class will follow Muslim women's experiences and changing roles in France and the United States from the 1970s through today.

courses.title: 19th-Century Literature and Culture
courses.description: Intensive study of a single major author of the romantic or postromantic period. The subject changes from year to year among writers in the different literary genres.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.

courses.title: Special Topics in French and Francophone Studies
courses.description: Examines selected topics in French and francophone studies. Content varies by semester and instructor.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one of the following: FREN 255, 260, or 262.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Research Methods in French and European Studies
courses.description: Provides training in research methodology either for a B.A. honors or M.A. thesis topic related to contemporary European studies. Students will learn to conceptualize an original research project and to identify and assess the current intellectual debates in their chosen areas of research.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: French for the Health Professions
courses.description: Aimed at health care professionals in a variety of fields, this class is designed to help them practice, consolidate, and improve their language skills, while encouraging students to develop a fuller understanding of health care systems in French-speaking regions of the world and to compare conditions with those in the United States. This course does not fulfill the FL requirement and does not count for the French major. Previously offered as FREN 405.

courses.title: Cultural Wars: French/United States Perspectives
courses.description: This course examines the limits of universalism in today's "multicultural" France and how the European Union affects French universalism and French resistance to identity politics.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: African Francophone Cinema
courses.description: Study of the production of films from francophone sub-Saharan and North African communities.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: 20th- and 21st-Century French Literature and Culture
courses.description: Studies of a single author, a literary movement, or an aesthetic movement from the avant-garde to postmodernism.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Social Networks: Technology and Community in Modern France
courses.description: Exploration of the interaction between technology and sociability in 19th- through 21st-century French literature, with an emphasis on questions of modernization, industrialization, colonization, globalization, subjectivity, and ethics.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: French Middle Ages
courses.description: Readings in a variety of medieval texts in light of contemporary literary theory.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Postmodernisms
courses.description: Theory, literary texts, films, and cultural phenomena associated with postmodernism and the interaction of art, philosophy, film, literature, and popular culture.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Writing the Mediterranean
courses.description: Explores early modern literary representations of the Mediterranean as a space of cross-cultural encounter, exchange, rivalry, and negotiation.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Crossing Gazes: Multidirectional and Conflicting Memories of Algeria
courses.description: Focus on contemporary fictions and films, and the writing of history from both the French (French-Algerian or "Pieds noirs," French draftees) and the Algerian sides.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, FREN 300 and one additional course above FREN 330; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: French Renaissance Literature and Culture
