courses.description: A continuation of MUSC 226 and 227, allowing students the opportunity to develop further performance skills and pedagogical techniques in music education. Offered in sections: instrumental, vocal, strings.

courses.title: Tonal Musicianship Skills III
courses.description: A continuation of MUSC 133, with emphasis on intermediate- to advanced-level musicianship skills.

courses.title: Theory III
courses.description: A continuation of MUSC 132, covering topics including chromatic harmony and form. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 132; prerequisite requires a grade of C or better.

courses.title: Studies in Performance Practices
courses.description: The study of vocal and instrumental performances practices in specific periods and repertories.

courses.title: World Musics in Theory and Practice
courses.description: Through the use of various ethnomusicological methodologies, students explore a range of non-Western musical systems in their cultural contexts. Topics of study may include aesthetic theories, cultural meaning, and conflict.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 131 or MUSC 135 or MUSC 137.

courses.title: Keyboard Skills II
courses.description: Continues group piano instruction for music majors begun in MUSC 136.

courses.title: Introduction to Music Technology
courses.description: A practical study of selected aspects of computerized music technology, including one or more of music-notation software, MIDI sequencing, digital sound production and storage, and computer composition.

courses.title: Performance in Southeast Asia: Gongs, Punks, and Shadow Plays
courses.description: The study and comparison of contemporary Southeast Asian performance genres (music, theatre, dance, ritual) in historical and cultural contexts.

courses.title: Dance in Indonesia
courses.description: This course is concerned with the performance and interpretation of Indonesian dance. It covers three areas of study: practical learning of traditional Indonesian dance repertoire, theoretical analyses and interpretation, and learning the music accompanying the dance.

courses.title: Gender on the Musical Stage
courses.description: An exploration of gender on the musical stage in the past and present, with an emphasis on female-identified creators and characters, onstage and behind the scenes.

courses.title: Studies in Medieval and Early Modern Music
courses.description: The study of music in its historical and cultural contexts in the medieval and early modern eras. May not count toward the requirements of the music major. May count as credit hours toward graduation, subject to the overall limit on music hours.

courses.title: Studies in Music History I, Antiquity to 1750
courses.description: A survey of music's development from antiquity to 1750, in its stylistic, geographical, political, social, and cultural contexts.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 131; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Studies in Music History II, 1750 to the Present
courses.description: A continuation of MUSC 254, surveying music of the period since 1750 in its stylistic, geographical, political, social, and cultural contexts.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, MUSC 132 and 254; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Advanced Beat Making Lab
courses.description: Building upon the foundations of MUSC 156, this course prepares students in professional beat making techniques within various settings of the music industry. The course implements a module-based instruction model, emphasizing student development in creating multiple extended play projects (EPs) with different utilizations (studio, live performance, screen) concluding with the development of a Final Portfolio review, using the computer-based DAW Ableton 11, MIDI controllers, and synthesizers and samplers accessed in the Music Department's Beat Lab.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 156 or permission of instructor.

courses.title: Musical Movements: Migration, Exile, and Diaspora
courses.description: The musical results of migrations of all types, voluntary or forced, by way of case studies drawn from historical and/or contemporary musics of Africa, the Americas, Asia, and Europe.

courses.title: Music Production II
courses.description: As a continuation of MUSC 161, this course will include more advanced techniques in mixing, mastering, and music production. Listening and ear training with practical exercises will be explored. The work of notable engineers and producers will be looked at with an ear towards their production values and critical listening of the material.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 161 or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Jazz Improvisation II
courses.description: Continuation of MUSC 163, examining more advanced improvisational techniques, harmonic materials, and compositional tune types.

courses.title: Jazz Composition and Arranging
courses.description: Composing and arranging for small- and large-group jazz ensembles.

courses.title: Composition
courses.description: May be repeated for credit. Original compositions in various forms.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Orchestration
courses.description: Practical orchestral scoring with emphasis on understanding and imitating historical styles from Mozart through Ravel.

courses.title: Making Music Happen
courses.description: This class is broadly about music teaching, but not exclusively about the formal music teaching that occurs in public and private elementary, middle, and high schools across the U.S. We will embrace an expansive definition of teaching that includes engaging with music as teacher, facilitator, performer, ambassador, and presenter. Because the research and literature in music education and community music is well-developed, we will often borrow strategies and pedagogies that can be applied to nearly any situation to learn and practice how a person can lead others to understand or create music more effectively.

courses.title: Music in the Community
courses.description: Connecting academic inquiry in community music with an experiential project in the making, organization, or documentation of music locally.

courses.title: Critical Approaches to Music: Object Lessons
courses.description: Critical approaches to the study of music through a variety of research approaches and sources, both visual and oral, examining meaning, expression, and values through close analysis.

courses.title: Critical Approaches to Music: Critical Moves
courses.description: Critical approaches to understanding music as a human activity, including questions of embodiment, dis/ability, difference, and power through a variety of research approaches and sources, both visual and oral.

courses.title: Jazz Innovators
courses.description: Musical, historical, cultural, and social issues in jazz studied through the examination of innovative and influential jazz artists.

courses.title: Popular Song in American Culture
courses.description: The relationship between popular song and culture in American society is explored by focusing on an important historical repertoire or interpretive theme.

courses.title: Bach and Handel
courses.description: The culmination of baroque music, emphasizing Bach's cantatas, concertos, organ music, and instrumental music, and Handel's oratorios and operas, all in their cultural contexts. May not count toward the requirements of the music major. May count as credit hours toward graduation, subject to the overall limit on music hours.

courses.title: Haydn and Mozart
courses.description: The high point in Viennese music of the late 18th century, emphasizing Haydn's symphonies and quartets, and Mozart's operas and piano concertos. May not count toward the requirements of the music major. May count as credit hours toward graduation, subject to the overall limit on music hours.

courses.title: Beethoven and His Era
courses.description: Beethoven's music will be studied in the context of social structures and concepts about artists during his lifetime. May not count toward the requirements of the music major. May count as credit hours toward graduation, subject to the overall limit on music hours.

courses.title: Musical Modernism
courses.description: A study of the work of diverse composers characteristic of music since ca. 1880 viewed in their broader artistic and other contexts. May not count toward the requirements of the music major. May count as credit hours toward graduation, subject to the overall limit on music hours.

courses.title: Music as Culture
courses.description: May be repeated for credit if on a different topic. Music in the framework of its social, political, economic, and cultural contexts. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Opera as Drama
courses.description: An introduction to music as related to drama, especially the development of opera and related genres. Study of selected works from different periods and styles. Honors version available.

courses.title: The Orchestra and Its Music
courses.description: Study of the symphony orchestra, its instruments, and its historical development from the mid-18th century to the present, and the music it plays, including selected works in a variety of styles.

courses.title: Sounds of War and Revolution
courses.description: Music's roles in war and revolution within various political, social, and cultural contexts. Part of the cluster "War, Revolution and Culture-Transatlantic Perspectives, 1750-1850."

courses.title: Music and Politics
courses.description: The relationship between music and politics studied through a global range of historical and geographical contexts. The course covers specific musical and political manifestations as well as theoretical approaches to the issue.

courses.title: Media and Social Change in Africa
courses.description: The historical and ongoing tradition of protest by African artists with particular focus on the aesthetics, politics, and geography of innovative grassroots movements on the African continent that effect social change through music and film.

courses.title: Bluegrass Music, Culture, and History
courses.description: The history, culture, musical sound, and practice of bluegrass music, with an intensive focus on critical listening. Covers significant performers, musical styles, and both fan and performance culture and meaning.

courses.title: Special Studies for Undergraduates
courses.description: Available only to music majors by permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Intensive study on a particular topic under faculty supervision.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Special Topics in Music, FC-GLOBAL
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Keyboard Lessons and Recital
courses.description: Advanced individual keyboard lessons leading to a public recital.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Voice Lessons and Recital
courses.description: Advanced individual voice lessons leading to a public recital. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced String Lessons and Recital
courses.description: Advanced individual string lessons leading to a public recital. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Woodwind Lessons and Recital
courses.description: Advanced individual woodwind lessons leading to a public recital. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Brass Lessons and Recital
courses.description: Advanced individual brass lessons leading to a public recital. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Percussion Lessons and Recital
courses.description: Advanced individual percussion lessons leading to a public recital. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Composition/Recital
courses.description: This course is conceived as a culminating project that showcases a student's original musical compositions.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Intermediate Lessons in Conducting
courses.description: Intermediate conducting for instrumental or vocal ensembles.

courses.title: Advanced Lessons in Conducting
courses.description: May be repeated for up to six hours of credit. Advanced conducting for instrumental or choral ensembles.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Study in Music Theory
courses.description: This course will address a particular issue in music theory as it pertains to a genre, repertoire, composer, questions of harmony, rhythm, form or musical structure in Western, non-Western, jazz, or popular musics. Subject matter will vary with instructor. May be repeated for credit if on a different topic. Permission of instructor required.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Musical Form and Analysis
courses.description: The study of analytical techniques as applied to significant works of the period.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 232; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Counterpoint
courses.description: The study of two-, three-, and four-voice counterpoint, for example in the style of Palestrina, Bach, or 20th-century idioms.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 232; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Analysis of Popular Music
courses.description: Analysis and transcription of blues, rock, ballads, and jazz, with an emphasis on rock music since 1955.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 232; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Analysis of Music since 1900
courses.description: The study of analytical techniques as applied to significant works of the period.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 232; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Critical Approaches to Music: Guided Research
courses.description: An intensive research-based course resulting in an original paper and/or creative work on a topic of the student's own development and presentation of the same. Honors version available.

courses.title: History and Culture of Music
courses.description: Course will address a particular genre, composer, compositional issue, or repertoire, including non-Western and popular musics. Subject matter will vary with the instructor. May be repeated for credit if on a different topic. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Vocal Production
courses.description: An in-depth study of recording, editing, mixing, and producing vocals with widespread applications for commercial and media projects. The course will cover vocal production for podcasts, radio, audition tapes, voice overs/ADR, animation/TV/film, and commercial single/EP/album releases. The collective projects throughout the semester will be the start of a professional portfolio for students interested in pursuing a career in audio production. The course will ensure students have knowledge and experience producing their own professional recordings in a workforce where media and self-promotion is prevalent.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 161 or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Studies in Jazz
courses.description: May be repeated for credit if on a different topic. Advanced study on a selected topic in jazz. Topics will vary and may address a particular genre, composer, performance practice, compositional issue, or repertoire.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: UNC Summer Jazz Workshop
courses.description: Lectures on theory and improvisation, small ensemble coaching, and instrument-specific master classes in a classroom/lecture format. Intensive listening component through required attendance at four evening concerts. Final public student concert for a community audience. Can be repeated for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Scoring for Film and Video Games
courses.description: Practical, hands-on training in the art of composing music for film and video games. In addition to analyzing and discussing influential film/game music, the course develops skills such as orchestration, underscoring, musical narrative, and thematic development. Students enrolled in the course are expected to have some prior experience composing and notating music for a variety of instruments and ensembles.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, MUSC 166 (Introduction to Composition) or permission of instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Inside the Song: Analysis of Songcraft
courses.description: Explore form, structure, and narrative in American popular song during the era of recorded sound. Students will analyze the elements of different songs -- melody, lyrics, harmony, musical arrangement, form, narrative, and structure. Students will write songs using different models and forms; edit and revise their songs; and perform those songs publicly. Familiarity with basic chords and melodies expected.

courses.title: Seminar in Music
courses.description: Detailed investigation of a specific musical topic from historical and/or theoretical perspectives. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Music
courses.description: This is a hands-on, research or creative-based learning opportunity for a student, under the guidance and supervision of a faculty advisor. The research or creative project will result in a tangible outcome, in the form of a research paper, research presentation, public-facing experience, or realization of a creative project.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Instrumental Performance Repertory
courses.description: Advanced study of selected performance issues.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Music Internship
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Internship directly related to the study, practice, or the business of music. Students must complete at least 100 hours and submit a journal and report upon completion of the internship. No more than three credit hours may count toward the requirements of the music major. Excess hours may count as credit hours toward graduation, subject to the overall limit on music hours.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Digital Media and Live Performance
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. Intended for students from various majors, this course provides a foundation in the history, theory, and practice of developing live, technologically-intensive, multimedia performance works. The course analyzes new media masterworks, addresses techniques of interdisciplinary collaboration, and offers workshops in specific software/technology applications.

courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis in Music I
courses.description: Admission by permission of the honors advisor. Independent study by a student who has been designated a candidate for undergraduate honors in music.

courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis in Music II
courses.description: Continuance and completion of an honors thesis in music.

courses.title: Resources and Methods of Musicology I
courses.description: Introduction to the field of musicology, including its scope, methodology, and bibliography. Taught in three-week modules, each directed by a different member of the academic faculty. Individual modules will include music history, music theory, ethnomusicology, music aesthetics, and cultural studies.

courses.title: Resources and Methods of Musicology II
courses.description: When offered, continuation of MUSC 750.

courses.title: Proseminar in Music Theory
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Proseminar in Musicology
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Proseminar in Ethnomusicology
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Special Studies
courses.description: The faculty assists and advises graduate students in work on particular research projects. Available to musicology graduate students only (M.A.T. students taking special studies must register under MUSC 471).
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Seminar in Music Theory
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Seminar in Musicology
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Seminar in Ethnomusicology
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Dissertation Colloquium
courses.description: Forum for group discussion of on-going dissertation work and professional development.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.description: MUSC 992 is required for all graduate students enrolled in the MA/PhD program in Musicology. Graduate students should take this course in fall semester of their second year of completing the program's MA requirements. Required assignments will teach skills that are key for successful completion of the PhD.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, Students registering for MUSC 992 under their instructor's section number should have successfully completed 18 credit hours of graduate seminar and met the program's foreign language requirement.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Introduction to Naval Science
courses.description: Fundamental orientation to the Naval service emphasizing the mission, organization, regulations, customs and traditions, broad warfare components, and major challenges facing Navy/Marine Corps officers.

courses.title: Seminar in Topics of Naval Science
courses.description: Permission of the department. Seminar of topics regarding the United States Navy.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Independent Study in Naval Science
courses.description: Readings and research by an individual student on a subject related to the United States Navy. Permission of the department.

courses.title: Naval Leadership and Management
courses.description: A study of organizational principles, management theory, and leadership styles, with emphasis on applications in the Navy and Department of Defense.

courses.title: Navigation
courses.description: A comprehensive study of the theory, principles, and procedures of ship navigation, movements, and employment. Course includes spherical trigonometry, mathematics, analysis, study and practices of navigation, sextants, navigation publications, and report logs. Covers rules of the road, lights, signals, navigational aids, and electronic and mechanical positioning devices.

courses.title: Navigation Laboratory
courses.description: Practical application of the theories and principles of navigation as presented in the lecture series.

courses.title: Marine Option Naval Science Laboratory
courses.description: One laboratory hour per week designed to introduce topics and activities relevant to the professional development of the prospective Marine Corps officer. Required for Marine Option 2/C.

courses.title: Naval Ships Engineering Systems
courses.description: An introductory course and survey of ship design, characteristics, propulsion (including nuclear power) and control systems, and the principles of ship stability.

courses.title: Naval Weapons Systems
courses.description: A descriptive survey course in engineering aspects of ships' weapons guidance, control, and propulsion systems and characteristics of ships' weapons systems.

courses.title: Evolution of Warfare
courses.description: Survey of the evolution of warfare through the study of selected campaigns and classic battles, with special emphasis on the principles of war, the military impact of leadership, and the evolution of tactics and weaponry.

courses.title: Naval Operations
courses.description: A study of the maneuvering of ships in formation, and the operations in which naval vessels engage daily.

courses.title: Naval Leadership and Ethics
courses.description: Capstone leadership course in NROTC curriculum, emphasizing leadership skills and their ethical implications for the competent commissioned officer in areas of human resources and material management.

courses.title: Amphibious Warfare
courses.description: A survey of the projection of sea power ashore, with special emphasis on the evolution of amphibious warfare in the 20th century, through the study of historical amphibious landings and campaigns.

courses.title: Naval Science Laboratory
courses.description: Required of all NROTC students. Meets once a week to provide supplemental military training, including close order drill, physical fitness, inspections, guest lectures, and leadership training.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 0 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.title: Operational Leadership Enhancement Course
courses.description: Provides leadership training in a military environment. Professional development is achieved through academics, physical fitness, marksmanship, and leadership experiences. Course reviews leadership lessons in an at-sea or training environment. Restricted to ROTC members who participate in summer cruise, training, or OCS.

courses.title: Brain & Behavior I
courses.description: Graduate standing required. A survey of psychological and biological approaches to the study of sensory and perceptual information processing, with an emphasis on touch and pain.

courses.title: Brain & Behavior II
courses.description: A survey of psychological and biological approaches to the study of basic learning and higher integrative processing.

courses.title: Advanced Biological Psychology: Central Nervous System
courses.description: Each fall one special topic will be covered in depth (e.g., neural bases of memory storage, homeostasis, and perception). Format includes lectures and seminar meetings with student presentations.

courses.title: Applications of Experimental Psychology to Health Research
courses.description: This course provides a critical analysis of interdisciplinary research within experimental psychology, including such topics as psychopharmacology, psychoneuroimmunology, psychophysiology, and animal models of brain/behavior disorders.

courses.title: Behavioral Pharmacology
courses.description: Basic principles of pharmacology and behavior analysis are considered in relation to drugs that affect the central nervous system.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, PSYC 404; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Research Design and Statistics in Neuroscience
courses.description: Limited to graduate students in psychology, neuroscience, and neurobiology. Experimental design, hypothesis testing, power analyses, ANOVAs, regression, correlations. Hands on data analysis with you being able to use your own data sets. Analyses will be conducted with SPSS and Prism. Permission of the instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Advanced Light Microscopy
courses.description: An intensive and comprehensive hands-on laboratory-oriented course in light microscopy for researchers in biology, medicine, and materials science. This course will focus on advanced quantitative fluorescence microscopy techniques used for imaging a range of biological specimens, from whole organisms, to tissues, to cells, and to single molecules. This course emphasizes the quantitative issues that are critical to the proper interpretation of images obtained with light microscopes.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.title: Introductory Pain Neurobiology
courses.description: Advanced level understanding of the underlying biological processes that contribute to the transmission and modulation of acute and chronic pain and pharmacologic management of acute and chronic pain: detailing the mechanism of action of commonly used drugs as well as exploring new drug targets.

courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology
courses.description: Introduces topics including brain cell biology, molecular biology applied to neurons, membrane potentials and imaging methods. The second block introduces such topics as resistance, capacitance, passive membranes, classes of ion channels, potassium and calcium channels, and action potential initiation. Final blocks, focus on neurotransmitter release and signaling through distinct receptor subclasses. Topics include G-protein coupled receptors and associated signaling, receptor binding/ligand theory, ionotropic and metabotropic glutamate and GABA receptors, receptor trafficking and localization. Permission of the department.

courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology: Introduction and Electrical Signaling
courses.description: Permission of the department. This course explores the experimental and theoretical function of the nervous system. Typically, the first hour is fundamental material presentation and the second hour may be a presentation led by the students. Topics covered include: cellular diversity in the CNS, gross brain anatomy, human and rodent brain imaging, neuromolecular genetics, behavioral methods, membrane potentials/resistance/capacitance, ion channel structure, electrophysiology and propagation of electrical signals in neurons. Basic undergraduate biology, chemistry, physics and intro calculus is assumed.

courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology: Postsynaptic Mechanisms-Receptors
courses.description: Permission of the department. Consideration of membrane receptor molecules activated by neurotransmitters in the nervous system with emphasis on ligand binding behavior and molecular and functional properties of different classes of receptors. Course meets for four weeks with six lecture hours per week.

courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology
courses.description: Block one covers neural stem cells, glial development, neural cell death and neurotrophin. The second block introduces the sensory pathways of vision, audition, taste, olfaction, pain, and touch, and the motor pathways of the spinal cord, basal ganglia, cerebellum, and motor cortex. Includes sensory information processing, motor execution, peripheral and central mechanisms of pain. Final block covers CNS imaging, regeneration, and such diseases as Alzheimer's, ALS, Parkinson's, epilepsy, addiction, autism, and schizophrenia. Permission of the department required.

courses.title: Developmental Neurobiology
courses.description: A survey of nervous system development emphasizing detailed analysis of selected research topics such as neuronal induction, neural crest development, neuronal differentiation, synapse formation, neurotrophic factors, glial development, and the effects of experience.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NBIO 722; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Experimental Neurophysiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Six or more laboratory hours a week.

courses.title: Translational Seminar in Cognitive and Clinical Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduces new neuroimaging techniques and their application to the study of neural correlates of cognitive and behavioral impairments in brain disorders. Reviews the theories and research methodologies that investigate how brain functions support and give rise to mental operations such as attention, memory, emotions, social cognition in the healthy brain.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Diseases of the Nervous System
courses.description: Explores the basic neurobiology and the clinical aspects of a range of diseases of the nervous system, including ALS, Alzheimer's, autism, schizophrenia, multiple sclerosis, deafness, epilepsy, pain, brain tumors, stroke, Parkinson's, and other neurodegenerative diseases.

courses.title: Sensory Neural Information Processing and Representation
courses.description: Additional required preparation, one year of calculus, familiarity with MATLAB or Python, or permission of the instructor. A discussion/reading seminar covering the fundamentals of nervous system information processing and integration, with examples from sensory systems.

courses.title: Microscopy: Principles & Applications
courses.description: This course aims to provide the knowledge one may need to understand the reach of microscopy imaging techniques, to be able to choose the right imaging modality, label the sample, carry out the experiment, analyze data, troubleshoot any pitfalls that may occur, and put together a custom optical setup.

courses.title: Biological Concepts
courses.description: Overview of structures and biological determinants of conditions and diseases of the oral cavity. Both growth and development and pathophysiology will be introduced in the context of three areas of oral biology: biology of extracellular matrices, host-pathogens interactions, and orofacial neurobiology.

courses.title: Neurocircuits and Behavior Journal Club
courses.description: This is journal club course will meet once per week for 90 minutes to discuss new research papers focused on delineating how neurocircuits function to orchestrate various behavioral states. Papers for discussion will be chosen by the instructor and students, and students will rotate in leading discussions.

courses.title: Seminar in Chemical Neurobiology
courses.description: Required preparation, two semesters of biochemistry.

courses.title: Neuroanalytics: Introduction to Big Data Science for Neuroscientists
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide both practical and theoretical training in advanced data analysis approaches commonly used in neuroscience research. Making biological insights into complex neuroscience data requires familiarity with computer programming, distributed computing, visualization, and statistics. This course aims to provide an introduction to these analysis techniques to make the aspiring neuroscientist comfortable with data science.

courses.title: Neurodevelopmental Basis of Brain Disorders
courses.description: The basic principles guiding in the formation and maintenance of human nervous system and how do distinct genetic/ epigenetic disruptions during development cause different types of human neurodevelopmental disorders. The intent of this course is to present latest advances in developmental neuroscience in the context of this theme. Topics covered IMII include neural patterning, neurogenesis, neural cell ate specification, neuronal migration, axon/dendritic growth and connectivity.

courses.title: Gene-Brain-Behavior Interactions in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Perspectives on Disease Mechanisms
courses.description: This seminar examines the topics of genetics, neuroanatomy, physiology, and behavioral development to provide a broad-based and integrated background to understand the etiology and potential mechanism underlying neurodevelopmental disorders.

courses.title: Clinical Syndromes and Neurodevelopmental Disorders
courses.description: This seminar will review the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis and treatment of neurodevelopmental syndromes and disorders. Topics will range from single gene (e.g. fragile X syndrome and tuberous sclerosis) to complex genetic (e.g., autism, schizophrenia), to environmental disorders with varied phenotypes, pathogenetic mechanisms, and treatments.

courses.title: Improving Presentation & Communication of Scientific Results
courses.description: Learning modern day techniques and approaches to convey scientific results effectively as a public speaker. Teaching how to implement the key aspects of effective presentation of scientific findings in public settings. Understanding the key components of an effective public talk including scientific content, body language, and voice. Learning how to captivate the target audience and yet still convey data driven scientific findings.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Seminar in Comparative Animal Behavior
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Advanced seminar in comparative animal behavior. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Seminar in Comparative Physiology
courses.description: Advanced seminar in comparative physiology.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, BIOL 451; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Special Topics in Neurobiology
courses.description: Special topics in neurobiology. Content will vary from semester to semester.

courses.title: Special Topics in Physiology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Individually arranged in-depth programs of selected topics such as membrane function, transport physiology, renal physiology, etc.

courses.title: Neuroscience Seminar Series
courses.description: Diverse but current topics in all aspects of neuroscience. Relates new techniques and current research of notables in the field of neuroscience. Content focuses on presentations by invited, non-UNC faculty, UNC faculty and mini-series presentations from current Neuroscience students. Topics vary from week to week.

courses.title: Research in Neurobiology
courses.description: Permission of the department. Research in various aspects of neurobiology. Six to 24 hours a week.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.description: Course is designed to certify that the students have achieved a high level of knowledge competence in clinical and basic neurosciences, without the rigorous research experience required of a Ph.D.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Clinical rotation in Neurophysiology and Polysomnography
courses.description: Students will be exposed to real life clinical neurophysiology and sleep laboratory practice and develop competence in the performance of these studies in the clinical setting. Students should apply the knowledge and skills necessary to perform basic neurophysiological and sleep studies, including recording and interpreting basic studies. Upon completion, students should be able to demonstrate competence performing these studies. Students will discuss the cases, review waveforms, and identify events with clinical mentors.

courses.title: Basic Neurophysiology and Sleep for Clinical Neurophysiology
courses.description: This course provides a concentrated study of anatomy and physiology essential to the practice of neurodiagnostics and polysomnography. Emphasis is placed on the physiology of the nervous, cardiovascular, and pulmonary systems and basic pharmacological principles. Upon completion, students should be able to demonstrate competence in concepts through written evaluation.

courses.title: Intro to Basic Sleep and Neurophysiology Instrumentation and Technology
courses.description: This course introduces fundamental concepts of NDSS equipment and recording of bio-electric potentials. Topics include concepts of basic electronics and instrumentation, key features of recording bio-electric potentials, function and application of neurodiagnostic equipment, construction of montages, display mechanisms, limitations of the recordings and essential clinical settings for the recording. Upon completion, students should be able to demonstrate basic competence in understanding neurodiagnostics and polysomnography and bio potentials.

courses.title: Polysomnographic and Neurophysiologic Technology/Lab
courses.description: This course provides practical application of theories covered in the basic instrumentation course. Emphasis is placed on NDSS procedures. Students will have a hands-on laboratory practice and develop competence, knowledge and skills to perform these studies. Students will extend their understanding through application and review of clinical cases. Upon completion, students should be able to successfully complete practice lab exams and competencies.

courses.title: Pathophysiology of Sleep, Neurological, and Related Disorders
courses.description: Students will learn about diseases affecting the nervous system, the sleep/wake cycle, and psychiatric and behavioral disorders. Topics include etiology, clinical manifestations, pharmacology, disease prevention, and overview of treatments. Restricted to NDSS Majors, Advanced undergraduates (instructor permission required).

courses.title: Neurological and Sleep Diagnostic and Therapeutic Methods, and Monitoring
courses.description: Students will learn about services available at sleep and neurophysiology laboratories and interpretation of diagnostic findings. Topics include sleep procedures, electroencephalography, and long-term epilepsy monitoring. Students participate in laboratory practice sessions. Restricted to NDSS Majors, Advanced undergraduates (instructor permission required).

courses.title: Evidence Based Practice in Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science
courses.description: Admittance into NDSS program required. An Introduction to the concept of evidence-based practice and an opportunity to acquire the skills necessary to be able to incorporate evidence and best practices into professional work. These include an understanding of research methods and the approach to critical appraisal of research literature. (Fall, On demand).

courses.title: Advanced Sleep and Neurodiagnostic Clinical Procedures
courses.description: Students will learn advanced procedures performed in sleep centers and neurophysiology laboratories. Topics include nerve conduction velocities, actigraphy, and autonomic testing techniques. Students participate in laboratory practice sessions. Restricted to NDSS Majors, Advanced undergraduates (instructor permission required).

courses.title: Informational Technology and Analytics in Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science
courses.description: A study and focus on information technology and analytics used specifically in Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science. Emphasis is placed on development of the knowledge and competencies necessary for selective use and evaluation of research, data acquisition, computer transfer of acquisition studies, acquisition interpretations, and data management in the healthcare of Neurodiagnostic and Sleep Science patients.

courses.title: Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science Practicum
courses.description: Sleep disorders center and clinical neurophysiology laboratory clinical experience. Students participate in direct working experience in clinical neurophysiology and sleep laboratories (note that students may not be substituted as staff). Students may participate in practicum rotations in private practices and acute care centers accredited by the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and/or The American Board of Registration of Electroencephalographic and Evoked Potential Technologists, or other accreditation as deemed appropriate by the instructor. Majors only.

courses.title: Principals and Practice of Healthcare Education
courses.description: This course provides a foundation in the principles and practice of healthcare education. Topics include the educational process, learner characteristics, and teaching and learning theories, techniques, and strategies. Restricted to NDSS Majors, Advanced undergraduates (instructor permission required).

courses.title: Program Administration: Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science Department Management
courses.description: Admittance in to NDSS program required. Students will be introduced to the concepts of project development and management related to Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science. Administration, financial, human resources, legal and policy concepts and issues in outpatient, public, and private sector settings. Topics and emphasis may vary. Students will be required to solve a clinical question using an inter-professional team-based approach.

courses.title: Advanced Physiological Monitoring and Data Acquisition
courses.description: Students will learn advanced clinical procedures performed in clinical neurophysiology laboratories and operating rooms. Topics include evoked potentials, nerve conduction studies, autonomic testing, and intraoperative neurophysiologic monitoring. Students participate in laboratory practice sessions. NDSS majors only.

courses.title: Leadership in Healthcare Organizations
courses.description: Admittance into NDSS program required. This course focuses on the theories and practices of leadership in health care. Global, social, legal, political, economic, and ethical issues are explored.

courses.title: Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science Internship
courses.description: Sleep and Clinical neurophysiology laboratory educational and management internship with mentoring component. Direct working experience in one or more of the following setting: educational facility; clinical facility or hospital; NDSS related company or business; other as deemed appropriate by the instructor. The student and internship supervisor negotiate a learning contract outlining the internship schedule and specific tasks to be learned and completed. Majors only.

courses.title: Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science Capstone
courses.description: Students complete a research project and presentation culminating from the undergraduate course of study. Project topics provide students the opportunity to summarize, evaluate, and integrate knowledge gained throughout the undergraduate major. Teaching methods include direct student exposure and significant time spent in a healthcare/clinical/educational environment specific to practice interests. The capstone project is in the form of research, or other scholarly activity that articulates the design, organization, statistics and data analysis used. Majors only.

courses.title: Neurodiagnostics and Sleep Science Capstone II
courses.description: This course is a continuation of NDSS 697. Students complete a research project and presentation culminating from the undergraduate course of study. Project topics provide students the opportunity to summarize, evaluate, and integrate knowledge gained throughout the undergraduate major. Teaching methods include direct student exposure and significant time spent in a healthcare, clinical, or educational environment that is specific to practice interests. NDSS majors only.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Drug Addiction: Fact and Fiction
courses.description: The course will tackle questions through classroom discussions, lectures, movies, writing assignments, and a visit to a research laboratory and a treatment facility. Students will be introduced to fundamental concepts in addiction research. Honors version available.

courses.title: First Year Seminar: Plasticity and the Brain
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the recent research and debate regarding neural plasticity and the ability of the healthy adult brain to change. Exciting new research suggests that the ability of the adult brain to change goes well beyond simply acquiring new knowledge and memories. Previously offered as PSYC 71.

courses.title: Synapses & Screens: Your Brain in a Connected World
courses.description: This course examines how brain development and maturation are shaped by digital technologies. Students will explore concepts of neuroplasticity, attention, and memory in the context of a hyperconnected world, while considering both the promises and challenges of living with rapidly evolving technologies.

courses.title: First Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Content varies by semester. Honors version available.

courses.title: Introduction to Neuroscience
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the structure and function of the nervous system. Fundamental principles will be introduced including nervous system anatomy; molecular and cellular properties of the nervous system; sensory and motor systems; current methods used in neuroscience; and how the nervous system produces behavior and cognition. This course provides greater breadth and depth of neuroscience topics, as compared to Biopsychology (PSYC 220). Previously offered as PSYC 175 and 315. Honors version available.

courses.title: Special Topics in Neuroscience
courses.description: An undergraduate seminar course that is designed to be a participatory intellectual adventure on an advanced, emergent, and stimulating topic within a selected discipline of neuroscience. This course does not count as credit toward the neuroscience major or minor.

courses.title: Neuropsychopharmacology
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the scientific study of psychopharmacology, with emphasis on drugs of abuse and psychotherapeutic drugs. Previously offered as NSCI/PSYC 320.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and PSYC 220.

courses.title: Learning
courses.description: Topics in Pavlovian and operant (instrumental) conditioning, learning theory, higher order cognitive learning, and application of those principles to mental-health related situations. Previously offered as PSYC 222. Honors version available.

courses.title: Sensation and Perception
courses.description: Topics in vision, audition, and the lower senses. Receptor mechanisms, psychophysical methods, and selected perceptual phenomena will be discussed. Previously offered as PSYC 225. Honors version available.

courses.title: Human Neuroscience through Imaging and Data Science
courses.description: This Course-based Undergraduate Research Experience introduces students to big data approaches in human neuroscience, emphasizing neuroimaging methods such as fMRI, DTI, EEG, and PET, alongside behavioral measures. Throughout the semester, students will engage in original research analysis & visualization, working on a sustained, scaffolded research project and learn fundamental techniques in data preprocessing, statistical modeling, connectivity analysis, and visualization. The course also provides an accessible introduction to advanced approaches, including machine learning and network analysis. Students will work with publicly available neuroscience datasets, gaining practical experience analyzing large-scale data, and completing a project that applies big data methods to neuroscience.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175 and COMP 110 or 116 (C or better required); Students may receive credit for only one NSCI 27X course.

courses.title: Cellular Mechanisms in Addiction Lab
courses.description: Cellular Mechanisms in Addiction is a laboratory and research-based course aimed at investigating the cellular underpinnings of drug addiction. Students will gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge approaches utilized in addiction research. Utilizing rodent brain tissue and immunohistochemistry techniques, students will delve into the cellular and molecular changes associated with addiction. Students may receive credit for only one NSCI 27X course. Majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 (C or better required); Pre- or corequisite, PSYC 210 or STOR 155 or STOR 120.

courses.title: Brain Organoid Electrophysiology Lab
courses.description: This is a hands-on, course-based undergraduate research experience (CURE) in developmental neurobiology. Students learn the principles of early neurodevelopment and activity-dependent plasticity while gaining technical experience in sterile cell culture, brain organoid generation, and electrophysiological recording. Working in research teams, students design and execute an original experiment testing how environmental, pharmacological, or activity-based interventions influence neural activity during development. The course emphasizes experimental design, data collection and analysis, scientific reading, and communication through journal clubs, research manuscripts, and poster presentations. Students with credit for NSCI 270-279 may not enroll.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 (C or better required); Pre- or corequisite, PSYC 210 or STOR 155 or STOR 120.

courses.title: Brainwaves: Human Electroencephalography Lab
courses.description: This research-based course is focused on understanding the neural underpinnings of electroencephalography (EEG) data. By synchronizing EEG recorded on the scalp with experimental events, Event-Related Potentials (ERPs) link human brain activity to specific mental processes. Students will gain technical skills, through hands-on experience, in processing, analyzing, and interpreting electrophysiological data. Majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 (C or better); Pre- or Co-requisite, PSYC 210 or STOR 155 or STOR 120; Students may receive credit for only one NSCI 27X course.

courses.title: Neurophysiology Data Science Lab
courses.description: In this research-based course, students will design novel experiments to examine sex differences in large neurophysiology datasets. Students will use Python to access and analyze data. Students will also learn research literature analysis, experimental design, data analysis, collaboration, and presentation skills by developing a research proposal, paper, and poster. Students may receive credit for only one NSCI 27X course. Restricted to Neuroscience Majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175 (C or better required) and either COMP 110 or COMP 116.

courses.title: Neural Circuits & Behavior
courses.description: This hands-on laboratory course introduces students to neuroscience research through a Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) using Drosophila melanogaster. Students will investigate how neural circuits shape behavior by designing and conducting original experiments with behavioral assays and neural manipulation techniques (genetic, pharmacological, optogenetic). Emphasis is placed on collaboration, iteration, and scientific communication. Alongside their projects, students will analyze primary literature, develop hypotheses, troubleshoot challenges, and interpret novel data. The semester culminates in both a written research paper and a poster presentation, showcasing student-designed discoveries. Students may only receive credit for one NSCI 27X Lab CURE course.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 (C or better required); Pre- or corequisite, PSYC 210 or STOR 155 or STOR 120.

courses.title: Obesity in the Brain - Neuroscience qPCR Laboratory
courses.description: Obesity in the Brain - Neuroscience qPCR Laboratory is a laboratory and research-based course that will expose students to the fundamental and emerging approaches used in RT-qPCR neuroscience research. Students will have the opportunity to delve into the effect of obesity and/or diabetes on the brain. In this course students will learn to handle rodent brains, perform cryostat sectioning, conduct reverse transcription, create a cDNA library, and utilize R programming to analyze qPCR results by studying genes of interest. Students with credit for NSCI 270-279 may not enroll. Majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 (C or better required); Pre- or corequisite, PSYC 210 or STOR 155 or STOR 120.

courses.title: Molecular Brain Imaging Lab
courses.description: Students will design novel experiments to examine and visualize sex differences in the nervous system. Students will learn how to handle brain slices, neuroanatomy, microscopy, immunohistochemistry and imaging analysis techniques by studying neuronal diversity in the norepinephrine system of mice. Students will have the opportunity to develop and test hypotheses, write a research proposal, and present their work in poster form. Students may receive credit for only one NSCI 27X course. Majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 (C or better required); Pre- or corequisite, PSYC 210 or STOR 155 or STOR 120.

courses.title: Microglia Laboratory
courses.description: In this laboratory course, students will utilize molecular biology techniques (e.g., immunohistochemistry and immunoassays) while developing and testing hypotheses regarding how environmental or experimental conditions alter microglia. Students will work in teams to design an experiment, and then collect, analyze, and report data. Students may receive credit for only one NSCI 27X course. Neuroscience majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 (C or better required); Pre- or corequisite, PSYC 210 or STOR 155 or STOR 120.

courses.title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
courses.description: Various special areas of neuroscientific study, offered as needed. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Service Learning in Neuroscience: APPLES
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Service learning component for students enrolled in Neuroscience APPLES courses. May not count toward the major or minor.

courses.title: Neuroscience Career Development, Networking & Applications in the Working World
courses.description: This course provides students interested in the neuroscience field an opportunity to gain valuable networking, job application and interviewing skills. Over the course of the semester students will meet with neuroscience professionals and create application packages. Students will learn from individuals in neuroscience related jobs about the diverse careers options available and strategies for navigating the job market successfully. Students will explore advances in neuroscience research and how they relate to industry, research, etc. Majors only.

courses.title: Current Topics In Neuroscience
courses.description: Various special areas of neuroscience study, offered as needed.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Pedagogy Course for Psychology and Neuroscience Undergraduate Learning Assistants
courses.description: This course gives an overview of teaching methods that facilitate the acquisition of knowledge and understanding as well as entails hands-on experience in the classroom. Common misconceptions of learning as well as legal and ethical considerations related to working closely with an undergraduate population will also be covered. Departmental application and approval required.

courses.title: Psychology and Neuroscience Undergraduate Learning Assistant
courses.description: This course is for students that have already served as a ULA and completed an associated pedagogy course. Students will gain additional hands-on experience supporting learning in the classroom and preparing supplemental learning materials. Departmental application and approval required.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Supervised research resulting in a written report for declared NSCI majors. May be repeated for credit up to six hours. Up to three hours may count as a neuroscience methods elective. Permission of the instructor.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175 and two additional STEM courses one of which must be at the 200 level or above; a minimum of a 3.0 cumulative grade point average.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Molecular Neuropharmacology
courses.description: This course will examine the molecular basis of drug action in the brain. Students will learn about ligand-receptor interactions and modulation of receptor number, structure, and function by drugs. Detailed examples will examine the molecular details of both ligand-gated ion channels and G-protein coupled receptors. The course will use analysis of primary literature and a semester-long makerspace project to delve into research where central themes will include developing critical thinking, design thinking, and communication skills.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175 or both PSYC 101 and PSYC 220; and NSCI 221.

courses.title: History of Neuroscience
courses.description: In this class, we will consider how neuroscience emerged as a multidisciplinary field. The class will cover key research findings that propelled the field forward. We will also delve into the autobiographies of some of the pioneering researchers who made these important discoveries. Previously offered as PSYC 415.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and 220.

courses.title: Glial Neuroscience
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide an in-depth investigation into glia cells in the brain, and their roles in health and disease. We will focus particularly on astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocytes, but we will also cover and discuss other glial cell types as well. A general overview will be provided for each topic, followed by study and discussion of primary literature.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and 220.

courses.title: Behavioral Endocrinology
courses.description: The endocrine and nervous systems interact with each other in complex ways to influence behavioral processes. In this course, we will discuss the ways by which hormones regulate homeostatic and social behaviors, learning, stress responses, and affective disorders, among others. Additionally, we will read scientific articles to learn about advances in the field of neuroendocrinology.

courses.title: Functional Neuroanatomy
courses.description: For advanced undergraduate and graduate students. An introduction to human neuroanatomy, covering function of the neuroanatomy of each major system and relation to neurobehavioral disorders associated with damage to the neuroanatomy of the system. Previously offered as PSYC 420.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175, or PSYC 101 and 220; recommended preparation, EXSS 175.

courses.title: Principles of Brain Circuits
courses.description: This course is designed for upper-level undergraduates who are interested in how brain circuits control behavior. A major focus will be the new technique of optogenetics that is revolutionizing our approach to systems neuroscience. Circuits that control movement, sensation, sleep, memory, and fear will be explored in detail. Points of emphasis will be circuits mediating pain as related to actions of opiates and circuits mediating feeding behavior as related to obesity.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and PSYC 220; BIOL 101 recommended.

courses.title: Genetics of Brain Diseases
courses.description: This course will explore the manifestations and causes of important neurological and psychiatric diseases. A particular focus will be the impact of advances in genetics on our understanding of these disorders. Disorders that affect large numbers of patients including Alzheimer's disease, autism, and schizophrenia will be studied in detail.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and PSYC 220.

courses.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurotechnology
courses.description: This course addresses fundamental challenges inherent in studying the brain and explores the theory, applications, and limitations of new and traditional neurotechnology. The unique ethical issues and significance of interdisciplinary approaches in neuroscience will also be highlighted. Students will analyze research literature and focus on cellular, molecular, and genetic techniques that are essential staples in the neuroscientist's toolkit. Students will also design experiments, utilize publicly available resources, and analyze big data generated by high-throughput approaches.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and PSYC 220.

courses.title: Neural Connections: Hands on Neuroscience
courses.description: This class will explore links between the brain and behavior through neuroscience outreach activities. Students will also reflect on the meaning of community engagement. By the end of the semester, each student must complete a minimum of 30 hours of service within the community. Previously offered as PSYC 424.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and 220.

courses.title: Animal Perception
courses.description: The course will focus on discussing and identifying how animals' "Umwelt" (perceptual experience of their environment) may differ from ours and how differences in their sensory receptors, sense organs, etc. lead to this difference in experience.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, PSYC 101 or NSCI 175; NSCI 225 recommended.

courses.title: Computational Methods in Neuroscience Using Python
courses.description: This course teaches Python fundamentals through the lens of computational neuroscience, using real examples and data. Students build practical coding skills and learn how computational tools help answer key questions about the brain, with no coding experience needed.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisite, NSCI 175 or PSYC 220.

courses.title: Neurobiology of Aging
courses.description: This course will survey clinical and experimental literature regarding the neurobiology of aging, considering different theories of aging, how aging is studied in the laboratory, and recent findings. Biochemical, molecular, physiological, and behavioral changes associated with both "normal" and pathological aging will be considered. Previously offered as PSYC 427.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and 220.

courses.title: Neuroscience, Society, and the Media
courses.description: Neuroscience is a "hot" topic in popular media. We will consider media coverage of neuroscientific research by reading the popular press versions of studies alongside the findings from primary sources and what kinds of topics are most often covered by the media and why. Previously offered as PSYC 428.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NSCI 175, or both PSYC 101 and 220.

courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to cognitive neuroscience. Higher mental processes including attention, memory, language, and consciousness will be covered, with an emphasis on the neural mechanisms that form the substrates of human cognition. Previously offered as PSYC 434.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, One of the following: NSCI 175, NSCI 222, NSCI 225, PSYC 220, or PSYC 230.

courses.title: Neuroimmunology
courses.description: The nervous and immune systems interact with each other in complex ways to influence behavior, health and well-being. In this course, we will examine the mechanisms by which these two systems interact. Further, we will cover how the nervous and immune systems function together to serve homeostasis, behavior and disease.

courses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience and Experimental Methods in Rodents
courses.description: This is to survey the wide variety of experimental methods used in rodent studies to assess behavioral outcomes, including memory, anxiety, depression, and drug seeking. This will be combined with readings on how changes in brain circuitry can affect behavioral outcomes, such as drugs of abuse or other disease states.

courses.title: Current Topics in Neuroscience
courses.description: Various special areas of neuroscience study, offered as needed. Honors version available.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Internship in Neuroscience
courses.description: Designed for highly motivated neuroscience majors interested in exploring professional opportunities in neuroscience-related areas. Students complete hands-on internships at community sites for approximately 120 hours across the semester and attend a weekly one-hour class or regular meetings with the instructor of record.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NSCI 175 and two additional NSCI courses.

courses.title: Autism
courses.description: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is characterized by difficulty in communication and social interaction. This course will examine scientific advancements in diagnosis, causes, and interventions for ASD. Additional topics include neurodiversity and inclusion.

courses.title: Emotion
courses.description: This course will provide a comprehensive overview of the scientific study of emotion. Topics will include theoretical models of emotion process and structure. A range of perspectives, including social, cultural, developmental, clinical, and cognitive psychology, as well as behavioral neuroscience, will be considered. Previously offered as PSYC 568.

courses.title: Neuropsychobiology of Stress
courses.description: Stress is a common experience in modern life that impacts psychological and physical health. In this course, we will delve into the scientific literature in psychology and neuroscience that explores how the brain and the body respond to stress, and how we can intervene to prevent stress from negatively impacting physical and mental health.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, PSYC 210 and 270, and NSCI 175 or both PSYC 101 and PSYC 220.

courses.title: Honors in Neuroscience I
courses.description: This course comprises the first semester in the two-semester sequence of Senior Honors in Psychology/Neuroscience. There are two components to the course: research that you will conduct under the direction of your faculty thesis advisor, and this class, which you will attend with the other senior honors students to learn about research-related topics and receive consultations with the instructor and your classmates.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, A cumulative GPA of 3.3, at least one semester of PSYC/NSCI 395 or the approved equivalent, and acceptance into the Psychology or Neuroscience Senior Honors Program; PSYC/NSCI 693H must be taken in the first semester of the last year of studies.

courses.title: Honors in Neuroscience II
courses.description: This course comprises the second semester in the two-semester sequence of Senior Honors in Psychology/Neuroscience. There are two components to the course: research that you will conduct under the direction of your faculty thesis advisor, and this class, which you will attend with the other senior honors students to learn about research-related topics and receive consultations with the instructor and your classmates. Admission to the neuroscience honors program required.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, A cumulative GPA of 3.3, completion of PSYC/NSCI 693H, at least one semester of PSYC/NSCI 395 or the approved equivalent, and acceptance into the Psychology or Neuroscience Senior Honors Program; PSYC/NSCI 694H must be taken in the second semester of the last year of studies.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Navigating and Advocating for your Wellness
courses.description: In a time when healthcare is more complex than ever, we often focus on training healthcare providers to communicate effectively for patient safety. However, a crucial piece of the puzzle is missing: who is teaching the patients how to communicate effectively to ensure they receive the highest quality and safest care? Navigating and Advocating for Your Wellness is designed to fill this gap by empowering students with the skills and knowledge they need to successfully navigate the healthcare system and advocate for themselves and their loved ones. The course utilizes TeamSTEPPS strategies, widely recognized in healthcare for enhancing teamwork.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.title: Building Effective Relationships in Healthcare: Carolina Core I
courses.description: This course provides socialization into relationship-centered nursing practice. All Carolina Core tenets are introduced; however, diversity and inclusion, relationship-centered care, and scholarly communication are a central emphasis. Students will obtain a beginning ability to act as a therapeutic agent. Majors Only.

courses.title: Research, Ethics, and Innovation: Carolina Core II
courses.description: This course focuses on research, ethics, and health innovations as a basis for scientific inquiry to address problems that require solutions. All Carolina Core tenets are examined; however, nursing inquiry, evidence-based nursing practice, and ethical conduct in research are central foci. Majors Only.

courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment I: On Campus Clinical I
courses.description: The first in a series of four on campus clinical courses, this course introduces foundational clinical nursing skills and integrates knowledge and skills of comprehensive health assessment for the adult and older adult. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills. Majors Only.

courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment II: On Campus Clinical II
courses.description: This is the second in a series of four on-campus clinical courses with application of advanced clinical nursing skills and comprehensive health assessment to specialized populations. This course emphasizes application of mental health and reproductive health concepts. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills. Majors only.

courses.title: The Intersections of Nursing and the Military I
courses.description: This is the first in a series of 3 courses that introduces the discipline, profession, and practice of nursing with a lens on the experiences of nurses and nursing students who have served in the military. History, values, culture, and critical thinking are critical in the discipline of nursing and is explored within this course. Admission to the UNC School of Nursing Military Pathway Program

courses.title: The Intersections of Nursing and the Military II
courses.description: This is the second in a series of 3 courses that discusses the discipline, profession, and practice of nursing with a lens on the experiences of nurses and nursing students who have served in the military. History, values, culture, and critical thinking are critical in the discipline of nursing and is explored within this course.

courses.title: The Intersections of Nursing and the Military III
courses.description: This is the last in a series of 3 courses that integrates the discipline, profession, and practice of nursing with a lens on the experiences of nurses and nursing students who have served in the military. History, values, culture, and critical thinking are critical in the discipline of nursing and is explored within this course.

courses.title: Culture and Nursing Care
courses.description: Relationship of culture to health and health care practices. Role of culture in structure and delivery of health care in selected countries, and with selected indigenous and minority populations. Majors only.

courses.title: Applied Global Health Nursing
courses.description: This faculty-led immersion provides students with the opportunity to observe and participate in culturally responsive nursing practice within a global setting or a "local as global" context. Learning experiences may occur internationally or within under-resourced communities of need in the United States. Students will apply nursing knowledge and skills to address the health needs of individuals, families and communities while developing a deeper understanding of global health perspectives.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 4 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Nursing Care of Adults I
courses.description: This course considers how nursing influences the health and healing capacities of adults. Students will attain the knowledge necessary to complete a comprehensive assessment of the older adult's physical, functional, psychosocial, and cognitive capacities. Clinical experiences in post-acute care settings provide opportunities for clinical reasoning, clinical care, and knowledge integration. Majors only.

courses.title: Pathophysiology/Pharmacology Across the Lifespan I
courses.description: Part one of a two-part course series focusing on the physiologic changes that occur as a result of select disease processes. Additionally, the clinical manifestations of altered health and related pharmacotherapy are addressed. Majors only.

courses.title: Pathophysiology/Pharmacology Across the Lifespan II
courses.description: Part two of a two-part course series focusing on the physiologic changes, the clinical manifestations of altered health, and the pharmacotherapy used to treat complex disease processes. Safe and effective medication administration by the Registered Nurse will be explored. Majors only.

courses.title: Evidence-Based Care of Older Adults
courses.description: This course emphasizes evidence-based care of the older adult across the care continuum and examines resources available for caregivers of this population.

courses.title: Family Focused Genomic Health Care
courses.description: This course focuses on the essential competencies in genetics and genomics for all registered nurses. A family perspective is used to help students relate advances in genomics to nursing care. Majors Only.
