courses.title: Integrating Principles of Leadership, Quality and Safety, and Informatics into Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on systems thinking and complexity, development of leadership roles and skills, and interprofessional communication and teamwork. All Carolina Core tenets are examined; however, leadership, quality and safety, and informatics are central foci. Majors Only.

courses.title: Foundations of Population Health and Global Health: Carolina Core IV
courses.description: In this course, all Carolina Core tenets are explored; however, there is a focus on population health and global health as essential components of nursing. Students will examine global health challenges as well as policy strategies of promoting health for all. Majors Only.

courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment III: On Campus Clinical III
courses.description: The third in a series of four on campus clinical courses with application of advanced clinical nursing skills and comprehensive health assessment to specialized populations. This course emphasizes application of leadership, pediatric and community health concepts. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills. Majors Only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 310, 311, and 352; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 484.

courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment IV: On Campus Clinical IV
courses.description: Fourth in a series of four on-campus clinical courses with application of advanced clinical nursing skills to specialized populations with a focus on transition to practice. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills.

courses.title: Global and Interprofessional Approaches to Solve Complex Cases
courses.description: This course uses a case-based approach to assist students to identify and critically examine challenging issues in health care, develop presentation skills as well as critical thinking from an interprofessional perspective. Students will work in interprofessional teams on a global complex case. Using this approach, students will attain the knowledge necessary to analyze and present results for a comprehensive case at the individual, organizational, and community levels. Open to undergraduate students with permission from instructor.

courses.title: Nursing Care of Adults II
courses.description: Centers on management of adults experiencing complex health problems and focuses on application of evidence based practice and skill acquisition needed to care for acutely ill patients through transitions in an illness experience. Clinical experience in acute care settings provide application for clinical reasoning, clinical care, and knowledge integration. Majors Only.

courses.title: Exploring Social Determinants of Health Across Populations
courses.description: This seminar allows students to explore how social determinants of health affect the health of populations.

courses.title: Mental Health Promotion and Psychiatric Care Across Populations and Settings
courses.description: Using selected theories of human psychosocial development, psychopathology, and psychotherapy, this course requires students to advance their use of therapeutic communication skills, examine the range and complexities of human emotional suffering, and apply methods of effective intervention. Majors Only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 330 and 351; Pre- or corequisites, NURS 311 and 352.

courses.title: Reproductive Health and Nursing Care of the Childbearing Family
courses.description: The course emphasizes development of caring and critical thinking skills in providing evidence-based nursing care focused on reproductive health and care of childbearing families. Majors Only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 351 and 330; Pre- or corequisites, NURS 311 and 352.

courses.title: Family-Centered Nursing Care from Birth through Adolescence
courses.description: This course emphasizes development of caring and critical thinking skills in providing evidence-based, family centered, culturally responsive nursing care to infants, children, and adolescents throughout the care continuum. Majors Only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 311, 330, and 352; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 430.

courses.title: Public Health Nursing in Community Settings
courses.description: Students apply evidence-based public health concepts to community practice to improve health and reduce disparities across the life span, emphasizing interventions using partnership strategies at individual, family, organizational, and policy levels. Majors only.

courses.title: Advanced Practicum in Nursing
courses.description: Majors only. The focus of this course is the development of knowledge and experience related to research or service learning and its application to the practice of nursing and health care.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Preparation for Professional Practice
courses.description: This course will assist students in preparation for the NCLEX-RN examination through a strategic and systematic individualized plan of study that utilizes testing programs and other relevant resources.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Management of the Critically Ill Adult
courses.description: This course focuses on collaborative management of critically ill adult patients. Students will gain advanced skills and demonstrate critical thinking to apply evidence based practice to care for critically ill patients across the continuum of care.

courses.title: Care of Individuals with Cancer and their Families
courses.description: This course focuses on the cancer experience of individuals and families across the lifespan (pediatric to older adults). The cancer control continuum framework will guide content focused discussions on prevention and risk reduction, screening, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and end-of-life care.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 301 and 330; pre- or corequisite, NURS 352.

courses.title: Pediatric Emergency and Critical Care Fundamentals
courses.description: This course, offered in collaboration with UNC Hospitals, focuses on the collaborative care of pediatric patients in the emergency department and in critical care units (NICU, PICU). Students will be introduced to advanced assessments and interventions utilized in these environments. Students will also discuss interdisciplinary challenges specific to pediatric emergency and critical care and investigate evidence-based solutions to some of these challenges. Majors only.

courses.title: SHAC: Student Health Action Coalition
courses.description: This course provides service-learning opportunities to apply nursing practice within the context of interprofessional care for vulnerable populations by participating with Student Health Action Coalition (SHAC) activities.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 0 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.title: Experiential Learning in Nursing
courses.description: This course provides experiential educational opportunities to apply nursing practice through volunteer participation in select communities. Majors only.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 0 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.title: Interprofessional Team Work and Communication - Key to Patient Safety
courses.description: Majors only. This interprofessional course focuses on understanding roles, teamwork, and communication to improve patient safety within the health care environment. National standards and initiatives will be the foundation of the course. Pass/Fail only.

courses.title: Health Care in the Global Context
courses.description: A faculty-led experiential learning opportunity focusing on development and knowledge related to research, health care systems, or service learning and its application to nursing and health care. Majors only or permission of the instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 8 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.title: Introductory Spanish for Health Professionals
courses.description: This course is intended for students who know no Spanish or so little that they feel the need to start over. Students with more than two semesters of college Spanish are not eligible. The course covers the curriculum of first-semester Spanish taught within a health context, with a focus on speaking.

courses.title: Supporting the Childbearing Family
courses.description: Application required. An interprofessional, service-learning approach to studying maternity care. Students will receive professional doula training and volunteer as birth doulas within the Volunteer Doula Service Program at North Carolina Women's Hospital.

courses.title: Interprofessional Perspectives on Diabetes Mellitus Management
courses.description: This elective course examines the current issues involved in managing diabetes mellitus in persons over their lifespan with an interprofessional lens. Contributions from all members of the healthcare team are an important theme throughout this course. This course integrates the pathophysiology of disease, therapeutics, and psychosocial modalities into the management of patients with diabetes. Previously offered as NURS 516. Majors only.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: This intermediate course is the equivalent of the third semester of college Spanish. Students will hone their listening and speaking skills in class primarily through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a health clinic in rural North Carolina.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: Required preparation, third semester Spanish or equivalent. This advanced course reviews the grammar of the third and fourth semester of college Spanish. Students hone their listening and speaking skills through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a Latino-run health clinic.

courses.title: Experiential Learning in Nursing: A Collaboration with UNC Health Center for Nursing Excellence
courses.description: This course provides experiential educational opportunities to apply nursing practice through volunteer participation in select communities associated with UNC Health. Admission to the undergraduate nursing program required.

courses.title: Experiencing Health Professions: A Service-Learning Partnership for Pre-Health Students
courses.description: This course provides experiential service opportunities for career exploration with select communities and populations associated with UNC Health. Students will be assigned to a role within the health system and will complete service hours within their assigned role. Class sessions will include topics related to healthcare and will develop skills in reflection, communication, and teamwork for career development. Does not count as an elective in the BIOL major or minor. It is recommended that students complete BIOL 117 before enrolling in BIOL 119. Permission of instructor.

courses.title: Mindfulness and Self-Compassion for Caring Professionals
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to rationale, research, and practices of mindfulness and self-compassion. Upon course completion, students will exhibit knowledge and skills related to mindfulness/contemplative practice/training, research evidence on mindfulness for enhancing provider self-care, patient/client engagement, and wellness (e.g., reducing stress, burnout, and fatigue; increasing resilience). Majors only; permission of the instructor for non-majors.

courses.title: Nursing Inquiry and Evidence-Based Practice for Advanced Scholarship
courses.description: Introduction to scientific inquiry, evidence-based practice, and nursing/healthcare innovations. Emphasis on: theory; ethics; problem identification; question development; design selection; data analysis and interpretation; statistical applications; and appraisal of research reports. Admission to an undergraduate BSN program and eligible to take required undergraduate nursing research course; the Hillman Scholars program; or PhD in Nursing Program required.

courses.title: Hillman Scholars in Nursing Innovation: Integrative Seminar
courses.description: Cultivates students' development as nurse scientists, scholars, and leaders to improve health care quality, safety, and delivery, and to influence policies that promote health and strengthen health systems outcomes. Admission to the Hillman Scholars Program in Nursing Innovation is required.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Experimental Courses
courses.description: Pilot test for new courses in the nursing program.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Care of the Dying and Bereaved throughout the Life Span
courses.description: Students from a variety of health sciences-related disciplines gain an understanding of issues in working with dying and bereaved individuals of all ages and their families.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Honors in Nursing, Part I
courses.description: Permission of the program director. Majors only. Preparation of a two-semester honors project under the direction of department advisors.

courses.title: Honors in Nursing, Part II
courses.description: Permission of the program director. Majors only. Preparation of a two-semester honors project under the direction of department advisors.

courses.title: Capstone: Transitions in Care and Practice
courses.description: Students will incorporate previously learned leadership concepts, clinical skills, therapeutic communication, and critical thinking to deliver quality nursing care, using evidence based practice, in varied settings with faculty and RN guidance. Preparing for the NCLEX-RN examination and strategies for successful transition from student nurse to registered nurse will be explored. Majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 330, 430, 481, 482, and 483; Corequisites, NURS 402 and 411.

courses.title: Scientific Writing
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and practice of scientific writing, with emphasis on research proposals, theses, research reports, dissertations, and articles for publication.

courses.title: Developmental Physiology and Pathophysiology
courses.description: This course explores developmental changes in morphological processes and normal and pathologic physiology in humans from conception through adolescence. Physiological differences between infants and children and adults are emphasized.

courses.title: Pathophysiology for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course explores the physiologic functions in humans throughout the lifespan. The broad-based content integrates pathophysiological concepts with emphasis on advanced practice nursing. Must be enrolled in School of Nursing Graduate Program.

courses.title: Pharmacotherapeutics for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course will examine the principles of pharmacotherapeutic decision-making in advanced nursing practice, with application to the clinical management of common health problems specific to all age groups, encompassing a life span approach. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Pediatric Pharmacology
courses.description: The course will examine the principles of pharmacotherapeutic decision making in advanced nursing practice, with application to the clinical management of common health problems specific to pediatrics.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 715 and 720; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Psychopharmacology in Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing
courses.description: Examines the principles of psychopharmacology and neurobiology for safe and effective psychotherapeutic management of individuals with psychiatric and mental health problems across the lifespan.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 715, 726, and 727; co-requisite, NURS 720; permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- and corequisites.

courses.title: Psychopharmacology for Advanced Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing
courses.description: This course introduces evidence-based psychopharmacological principles for the management of psychiatric-mental health conditions.

courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment and Diagnostic Reasoning in Pediatric Nursing
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare the advanced practice nurse to comprehensively assess pediatric clients using a diagnostic reasoning process.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 8 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment and Diagnostic Reasoning in Primary Care Nursing
courses.description: This course examines the process of diagnostic reasoning as a framework to synthesize comprehensive assessment of patients throughout the lifespan.

courses.title: Advanced Diagnostic Process in Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing
courses.description: The course introduces you to the psychiatric-mental health specialty of nurse practitioners. It evaluates and enhances competencies in gathering information to conduct a comprehensive psychiatric assessment and synthesize diagnoses. Through the course, students learn the clinical and theoretical reasoning processes for developing and validating psychiatric diagnoses and using models for assessing individuals.

courses.title: Foundations in Clinical Informatics: Data, Information, and Knowledge
courses.description: Required preparation, graduate nursing program admission or instructor permission. This foundational course provides an overview of computer and information science concepts as applied to health care.

courses.title: Evidence-Based Practice and Research
courses.description: This course provides the essential concepts and strategies for research and quality improvement, and the impact of these methodologies on patient populations and care systems.

courses.title: Health Care Policy and Leadership
courses.description: This course examines the role of nursing in health care leadership and policy. Students will gain competencies in the application of micro and meso level leadership tools. Students will apply these skills to the health policy development and advocacy as a means of impacting the health of populations at the local, state, and national and/or international level. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course is an advanced, comprehensive assessment of an individual's health across their developmental lifespan that examines the interactions of developmental, biopsychosocial, and socio-cultural contexts of health.

courses.title: Advanced Diagnostic Reasoning
courses.description: This course examines the process of diagnostic reasoning as a framework to synthesize comprehensive assessment and disease prevention using lifespan concepts. Nursing majors only.
courses.requisites: Corequisite, NURS 750; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 715.

courses.title: Research for Advanced Clinical Practice
courses.description: Graduate standing and successful completion of an undergraduate statistics course required. This course explores approaches to research problems in advanced practice nursing. Theories, methods, designs, measurement, ethical conduct, and skills in critical appraisal are emphasized.

courses.title: Intermediate Statistical Applications in Health Care
courses.description: Graduate standing required. This course provides an introduction to probability, statistical concepts, and analytical techniques useful in health care research and for interpreting the literature.

courses.title: Interpreting Research Reports
courses.description: For Nursing students admitted to the Graduate School. Focuses on approaches for critical reading of research reports to evaluate the evidence base for practice.

courses.title: Synthesis and Translation of Evidence
courses.description: Focuses on the translation of research evidence to support improved models of care delivery.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 778; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Multidisciplinary Perspectives on Managing Diabetes Mellitus
courses.description: This course examines the current issues involved in managing diabetes mellitus in persons over their life span. Contributions of the multidisciplinary team are an important theme throughout this course.

courses.title: Genomics and Society
courses.description: This multidisciplinary course offers students the opportunity to gain a basic understanding of human genetics and explore the ethical, legal, and social implications of recent advances in genetics.

courses.title: Advanced Concepts in the Clinical Care of Older Adults
courses.description: Graduate students only. Focuses on advanced concepts for nursing management of older adults and their families with an emphasis on interdisciplinary care.

courses.title: Cancer Care for Advanced Practice Providers
courses.description: This course for MSN, DNP, and PhD students provides an understanding of management of adults across the cancer continuum (prevention, early detection, treatment, and beyond [survivorship, palliative care, end-of-life care]) for advanced practice providers regardless of practice setting.

courses.title: Advanced Pharmacology in Oncology
courses.description: Focuses on the pharmacologic management of drugs used for therapeutic management and supportive care in adult oncology.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 715 and 720; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Advanced Concepts in Oncology Nursing
courses.description: Admission to Adult-Gerontology Nurse Practitioner program or permission of the instructor required. This course focuses on an evidence-based approach for the advanced practice nurse, incorporating pathophysiology; prevention/detection; medical treatment; nursing management; and socioeconomic, ethical, and legal issues related to adult cancer care.

courses.title: Population Health: Interprofessional Management in a Changing Healthcare System
courses.description: This interprofessional education course focuses on preparing healthcare professionals with the foundational skills needed to work in teams to effectively collaborate and coordinate care in population health. Admission to the School of Nursing graduate program or graduate students in any of the Health Affairs Schools with permission of instructor required.

courses.title: Special Problems
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 99 total completions.

courses.title: Primary Care of Adolescents and Adults
courses.description: This course will focus on advanced assessment, diagnosis and management of adolescents and adults seen in primary care settings.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 715, NURS 720, NURS 750, & NURS 752; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 720.

courses.title: Selected Issues in Adult Health
courses.description: Provides the opportunity for an in-depth examination of management strategies with selected health problems in adults. Also examines issues inherent in the management of women and elderly populations.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 715, 720, 726, and 810; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Care of Adults with Complex Health Problems
courses.description: This course focuses on care of adults with complex health problems. Students will develop skills to assist with the successful transition into the role of an AGPCNP into health care systems.

courses.title: Advanced Practice Nursing Role
courses.description: Examines current advanced practice nursing roles issues, within the context of contemporary healthcare delivery, legal, and sociopolitical systems.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 810, 840, or 860; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Practicum in Primary Care Management of Adults
courses.description: A clinical practicum in an ambulatory care setting that provides experience in the delivery of healthcare from age 13 through end-of-life, to individuals and their families.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum in Advanced Oncology Nursing
courses.description: Focuses on the evidence-based management of common acute, episodic, and chronic health problems in adult cancer patients for the oncology nurse practitioner.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 788 and 789; Corequisites, NURS 821; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- and co-requisites.

courses.title: Seminar in Advanced Oncology Nursing
courses.description: Focuses on evidence-based nursing and medical management issues relevant to the care of patients and their families across the cancer continuum and practice settings.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 788 and 789; co-requisite, NURS 820; permission of instructor for students lacking the co-requisite.

courses.title: Advanced Practicum in Primary Care Management of Adults
courses.description: This clinical capstone course prepares Adult Gerontology primary care nurse practitioner students to synthesize and apply concepts and knowledge critical for professional primary care advanced practice nursing with individuals, families and communities. Students' independent practice skills are refined in precepted clinical experiences.

courses.title: Advanced Concepts in the Clinical Care of Older Adults
courses.description: This course focuses on the clinical management of older adults and their families emphasizing interdisciplinary care. Content includes physiologic, pathological, psychosocial and functional changes associated with aging; including social gerontological issues. Nursing majors only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 715, NURS 720, NURS 750, NURS 752, NURS 810, NURS 819, NURS 825.

courses.title: Sexual and Reproductive Health for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: Uses a life span approach to examine principles of primary care management of childbearing couples and sexual reproductive health in women and men. Application is in community-based settings. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Introduction to Population Health and Community-Based Practice
courses.description: This course introduces fundamental concepts and models of population-oriented nursing practice and the central issues affecting that practice. Focuses on health disparities and underserved populations.

courses.title: Primary Care of Infants, Children and Adolescents
courses.description: This course will focus on developmentally appropriate advanced assessment, diagnosis and family-centered management of infants, children and adolescents seen in primary care settings.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 715, NURS 720, NURS 750, NURS 752, and NURS 810.

courses.title: Primary Care Across the Lifespan with Advanced Clinical Practicum
courses.description: This capstone course emphasizes the comprehensive, whole-person approach to the clinical management of primary health care needs across the lifespan in the context of the individual, the family and/or the community.

courses.title: Advanced Practicum in Sexual and Reproductive Health: Clinical & Simulation for Advanced Nursing Pra
courses.description: This course provides nurse practitioner students with applied clinical and laboratory experiences in sexual and reproductive health across the lifespan, with emphasis on prenatal and postpartum care. Students will integrate family-centered and culturally responsive approaches while developing advanced assessment, diagnostic reasoning, and management skills for sexual and reproductive health conditions. Through supervised clinical practice (90 hours) and simulation/laboratory learning (22.5 hours), students demonstrate competency in patient care, interprofessional collaboration, and evidence-based decision-making.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 715, NURS 720, NURS 750, NURS 752, NURS 810; Corequisite, NURS 825.

courses.title: Acute Care Advanced Nursing Practice for the Adult-Gerontology Population I
courses.description: Students will begin to explore the professional role of the Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner. The program begins with a developmentally focused examination of how to assess and manage common challenges in complex patient care, including the older adult and those with chronic conditions.

courses.title: Pharmacology in the Acute Care Setting with the Adult-Gerontology Population
courses.description: Focusing on unique aspects of prescribing in the acute care setting, this course will help the AG-ACNP student to understand specific knowledge related to prescribing for more complex and unstable patients, and establish a systematic approach to prescriptive stewardship.

courses.title: Acute Care Advanced Nursing Practice for the Adult-Gerontology Population II
courses.description: This course will focus on content and clinical applications for more complex and critical conditions managed within the scope of Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner practice.

courses.title: Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Practicum
courses.description: This final clinical course is intended to promote increasing independence in clinical decision making, risk stratification, and overall management of adult-gerontological patients with complex illness or injury in the acute care setting.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 830, NURS 831, NURS 832 ; Corequisite, NURS 834.

courses.title: Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Seminar
courses.description: This final seminar course is designed to support the nurse practitioner in the transition from primary to acute care clinician. Students will explore the professional role of the Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner as a pivotal member of interdisciplinary teams. Unique aspects of this transition will be examined, including collaborative relationships, the credentialing process, billing and coding, ethical challenges, and professional advocacy.

courses.title: Population Health and Epidemiology
courses.description: Admission to Nursing graduate program. Focuses on epidemiologic approaches for studying the impact of social, economic, and cultural inequalities on health and illness patterns at population and clinical levels.

courses.title: Health Care of Women Practicum
courses.description: The women's health care advanced practicum focuses on the synthesis and clinical management of primary health care and specialty health care problems of women.

courses.title: Primary Care of Children I
courses.description: This course concentrates on clinical management of pediatric primary care patients and their families with a continuing focus on advanced diagnostic reasoning.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 715, NURS 720, NURS 750, & NURS 752; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Primary Care of Children II
courses.description: The course focuses on advanced clinical management of pediatric primary care patients, emphasizing concepts of family-centered health care in selected child and adolescent health problems. Students function in an advanced practice role working with children, adolescents, and their families in primary care, or outpatient pediatric specialty settings.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, NURS 715, 720, 750, 752, 840 and 849; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- or co-requisites.

courses.title: Care of Children with Complex Health Conditions
courses.description: This course prepares the advanced practice nurse to design, implement, and evaluate a coordinated system of interventions that aim to promote optimal health and development for infants, children and adolescents with complex conditions. Students will develop skills to assist with the successful transition into the role of a Pediatric Nurse Practitioner into health care systems.

courses.title: Pediatric Behavioral and Developmental Assessment and Management
courses.description: This course prepares the advanced practice nurse to assess, design, implement, and evaluate a coordinated system of interventions that aim to promote optimal behavioral and developmental health for infants, children, and adolescents. It meets the didactic requirement for completing the Pediatric Mental Health Specialist certification exam.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum in Advanced Pediatric Nursing
courses.description: Supervised practicum in an advanced practice role in a selected health care setting that provides primary care to infants, children, or adolescents.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 715, 720, 750, 752, 840, or permission of instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Practicum in Primary Care of Children
courses.description: This course is the capstone practicum for pediatric nurse practitioner students. It emphasizes the comprehensive clinical management of primary health care needs of children in the context of the family.

courses.title: Advanced Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing Interventions in Adulthood
courses.description: This course is designed to build on the PMHNP diagnostic reasoning skills for assessment and management of psychiatric-mental health conditions in adulthood.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 715, NURS 720, NURS 727, NURS 750; Corequisite, NURS 723.

courses.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing for Underserved Populations
courses.description: Utilizing epidemiology, psychoeducation, case management, and health policy, students examine the scope of mental health problems and services for underserved populations.

courses.title: Advanced Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing Interventions in the Context of Relational Dynamics
courses.description: This course focuses on the PMHNP delivering care within relationships and larger systems. This course focuses on the influences of relational dynamics in the development of psychiatric-mental health conditions and the PMHNP's role in management.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 865; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 715, 720, 727, 750, 723, 860.

courses.title: Advanced Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing Interventions in Pediatrics
courses.description: This course focuses on the assessment of psychiatric-mental health conditions seen in pediatrics. It emphasizes the management and evaluation of evidenced-based, developmentally appropriate pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions.

courses.title: Advanced Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing Interventions for Complex Conditions
courses.description: This capstone course builds on and synthesizes PMHNP competencies in identifying and managing complex psychiatric-mental health conditions for diverse patients across the lifespan.

courses.title: Practicum in Psychiatric Mental Health Care for Advanced Practice Nurses
courses.description: This is the final advanced clinical course for students to apply knowledge and skills in selected domains of the advanced practice of psychiatric-mental health nursing. Supervision, peer evaluation, seminar, and independent readings will enhance the experience.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 727, 860, 863 and 864; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Applied Health Informatics in Complex Health Care Systems
courses.description: The course focuses on the concepts relevant to health care informatics, the use of computerized information systems, and the use of computer applications to support clinical and administrative decision-making.

courses.title: Leadership and Advanced Practice Roles in Health Care Organizations
courses.description: This course examines health care and nursing practice organizations, and the influence of the external and internal environment on these organizations. Roles and functions of nurses at different levels and in different types of health care settings are explored.

courses.title: Managing Human Resources in Complex Health Care Systems
courses.description: This course explores the knowledge and skills required for effective human resource management with emphasis on behaviors that promote and sustain an interprofessional health care practice environment. Nursing majors only. Admission to the Graduate School or permission of instructor required.

courses.title: Financing for Value-Based Health Services and Systems
courses.description: This course focuses on fundamental financial management concepts in health services organizations. Emphasis is placed on the financial environment and application of financial and managerial accounting and budgeting principles and methods to prepare nurse leaders and entrepreneurs for decision-making in simple to complex health services organizations. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Improving Quality, Safety and Outcomes in Complex Health Care Systems
courses.description: Explores theories and methods for improving the quality, safety, and outcomes of care at patient and organizational levels, emphasizing the quality and patient safety movement, improvement science, and evidence based practice. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Teaching Principles and Practices for the Nurse Educator
courses.description: This course will prepare students for teaching in diverse healthcare and educational settings. Emphasis will be placed on the development of skills for teaching in nursing and healthcare to promote ethical, safe, and quality care. Must be a professional nurse enrolled in a graduate program at UNC-CH.

courses.title: Curriculum Development in Nursing and Healthcare Education
courses.description: This course will examine curriculum development and evaluation in healthcare education for academic and clinical settings. Emphasis is placed on current contextual influences that facilitate curriculum development, implementation, and evaluation in diverse healthcare educational settings. Must be a professional nurse enrolled in a graduate program at UNC-CH.

courses.title: Organization Theory for Managing Complex Health Care Systems
courses.description: This course explores complex health care systems' distinctive structures, processes, and outcomes and how internal and external environmental factors influence health care and nursing practice. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Health Care Leadership and Administration Residency and Integrative Seminar
courses.description: This course is designed to examine evidence-based strategies within health care systems, related to the management of resources, information systems, policies, and delivery of quality, relationship-centered care. Nursing majors only and permission from instructor required.

courses.title: User-Centered Analysis and Design of Health Care Information Systems and Interfaces
courses.description: This course combines user-centered design theories, the science of systems analysis and design, and usability in health care, supported by real-world exercises in a simulated environment.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 730 and 870; permission of instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Advanced Assessment for Nursing Leadership
courses.description: This course focuses on advanced assessment for identifying evidence-based interventions across a variety of healthcare settings. Emphasis is on the application of tools to implement changes related to care delivery and coordination at the client, unit, and organizational levels.

courses.title: Evidence Based Care for Clinical Nurse Leaders
courses.description: Advanced clinical nurse leadership course emphasizing collaboration with key stakeholders to implement evidence-based interventions and improve care delivery in clinical systems.

courses.title: Clinical Teaching and Evaluation in Nursing Education
courses.description: Prepares students for clinical teaching in diverse nursing education settings. Emphasis will be placed on the development of evidence-based clinical teaching skills designed to facilitate student learning and evaluation as well as safe, ethical, relationship-centered clinical practice of students. Must be a professional nurse enrolled in a graduate program at UNC-CH.

courses.title: Special Topics in Nursing
courses.description: Special topics with an authority in the field.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Scientific Reasoning I: Defining and Articulating a Researchable Nursing Problem
courses.description: Introduces scientific reasoning, methods and ethical principles guiding scientific inquiry. Includes an introductory review of the literature and formulation of a researchable problem and purpose statement within a focused area of nursing inquiry.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, Enrollment in the SON PhD Program; Corequisite, NURS 913.

courses.title: Crafting Effective Health Research Grant Proposals
courses.description: In this course students will apply their foundational knowledge of scientific theory, methods and analysis to design a research proposal. They will generate ideas and drafts of the Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, and Methods sections of the proposal. While students are encouraged to search and apply for NIH and non-NIH grants, the course will focus on the NIH research proposal since it is the major funding source for health-related biomedical research. The final product will include a full draft of the research plan for an NIH F31 grant proposal or equivalent (e.g., foundation grant, K99).
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 912, NURS 913, NURS 916, NURS 917, NURS 926 or permission of instructor.

courses.title: Carolina PhD Seminar I: Introduction to Nursing Science and Syndemics
courses.description: Introduces the ontological and epistemological basis of nursing science and the application of syndemic thinking as a lens for conducting nursing science.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, Enrollment in the SON PhD Program.

courses.title: Multilevel Approaches to Health Equity
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to scientific inquiry using a multilevel approach. Fundamental principles around conceptual, theoretical, study design, and analytic perspectives for why and how multilevel approaches are useful for addressing determinants of health and health equity are at the core of covered content.
courses.requisites: Corequisite, NURS 912 or permission of instructor.

courses.title: Carolina PhD Seminar III: Social Determinants of Health
courses.description: Examines social determinants of health at multiple levels, and their interactions, and characteristics that differentiate structural from non-structural social determinants. Enrollment in the SON PhD Program.

courses.title: Carolina PhD Seminar IV: Synthesizing Determinants of Health, Syndemics and Nursing Science
courses.description: Evaluates the interplay among biological, physiological, psychological, behavioral, and social determinants, whether the relationships are consistent with a syndemics framework, and the potential for novel relationships across determinants in these areas to advance nursing science. Enrollment in the SON PhD Program.

courses.title: Theoretical Foundations of Nursing Inquiry
courses.description: Students develop competence in analyzing and applying philosophical and theoretical orientations as well as in the conduct and critique of scientific and scholarly work. Majors only.

courses.title: Knowledge Synthesis: Organizing, Evaluating, and Summarizing Evidence
courses.description: Student develops competence in identifying, organizing, critiquing, and synthesizing the evidence in a focused area. Includes writing a review of the synthesized evidence that serves as a foundation for a publication.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 912 or permission of instructor.

courses.title: Transforming Health Systems: Innovation, Implementation Science, and Policy
courses.description: This course introduces students to the principles and concepts of innovation, implementation science, and policy, to transform clinical practice, health systems, and societal health. Students will critically evaluate multi-level contexts, identify strategies to catalyze change, and evaluate impact using relevant theories and frameworks. Applications and skills development will be used to engage students in translating innovations into real-world impact.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NURS 909, 912, 913 and 934, or permission of instructor.

courses.title: Qualitative Approaches to Scientific Inquiry
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive examination of qualitative research methodologies, including qualitative description, grounded theory, ethnography, and narrative inquiry. Students will critically examine the philosophical underpinnings of these approaches and their application to scientific inquiry. Emphasis is placed on designing qualitative studies, with a focus on sampling strategies, data collection techniques, data analysis processes, and the representation of findings. The course also addresses essential considerations for ensuring validity and rigor, ethical research practices, and strategies for managing challenges in qualitative research.

courses.title: Quantitative Approaches to Scientific Inquiry
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth introduction to quantitative research methods. It focuses on designing studies, including descriptive, associational, explanatory, and predictive designs, as well as sampling, measurement, data collection, analysis, and result interpretation. Students will explore the philosophical foundations of these methods and their application in scientific inquiry. The course also covers key aspects of validity, rigor, ethical practices, and strategies for overcoming challenges in quantitative research.

courses.title: Intermediate Statistics: Regression Analysis
courses.description: Focuses on the use of advanced regression techniques to analyze various types of response variables with multiple predictors, interaction terms, or longitudinal data. Permission of Instructor.

courses.title: Theoretical Foundations of Advanced Practice
courses.description: This course provides a foundation philosophy of science, examines the elements and utility of theory, and explores key theories of practice, including theories from nursing and other disciplines. Admission to Nursing graduate program required.

courses.title: Theoretical Principles of Evidence-Based Practice
courses.description: This course is an analysis of the theoretical principles of translating, disseminating, and implementing evidence into healthcare practice. Students will evaluate major theoretical and conceptual models in the fields of translational science, dissemination and implementation, organizational change, and quality improvement. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Critical Appraisal of Evidence
courses.description: This foundational course is focused on identification of a practice problem and systematically searching, appraising, and synthesizing a body of evidence to support practice change. Nursing Majors Only.

courses.title: Implementation and Evaluation of Evidence-Based Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on evidence-based implementation and evaluation strategies for development of methodologies for planning, implementing and evaluating a sustainable practice change project that emphasizes quality and safety principles. Nursing Majors Only.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 922; Pre- or corequisites, NURS 921 and 969.

courses.title: Experiential Learning I: Statistical Analysis
courses.description: This course will introduce and prepare students for biostatistical computing of quantitative data using mainly SAS statistical software. It builds on the knowledge obtained in NURS 916: Design Measurement and Analysis: Descriptive & Associational Research by reinforcing the material and focusing on application within the SAS framework. Course prepares students for future SAS programming and analysis needs in NURS 917: Design Measurement and Analysis: Explanatory and Predictive Research and NURS 918: Intermediate Statistics: Regression Analysis.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, Enrollment in the SON PhD Program; Corequisite, NURS 916.

courses.title: Foundations of Statistical Analysis
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to statistical analysis for quantitative data, combining theoretical concepts with practical applications through various software programs (e.g., SAS, G*Power, and nQuery). Students will learn core methods such as descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square tests, and correlation, along with an introduction to advanced topics like regression, moderation, mediation, sample size calculation, and handling missing data. Emphasis is placed on interpreting statistical results, data visualization, and communicating APA-style results.

courses.title: Clinical Scholarship and Professional Communication
courses.description: This course provides students with a foundation in professional communication of scholarly and clinical work through a variety of strategies. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Leading Organizational and Systems Change
courses.description: This course provides a foundation for the application of core leadership principles to lead organizational change within complex and dynamic healthcare systems. Students will gain competencies in the application of macro-level leadership tools (e.g., organizational assessment, systems thinking, strategic planning, workforce management, and organizational policy development and analysis) to address service delivery challenges and drive organizational change, with a particular focus on quality improvement and patient safety initiatives. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Informatics for Safe and Effective Health Care
courses.description: This course prepares health care leaders to effectively select, implement and utilize health information systems for effective delivery of health care services and promote quality, safety and patient engagement.

courses.title: Public Policy and Advocacy in Health Care
courses.description: This course examines the intersection of health policy development, advocacy and nursing as a means of impacting the health of populations at the local, state, national and/or international level. Emerging issues in health policy will be explored with an emphasis placed on transformational leadership principles as a means of influencing change. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Advanced Leadership I: Operational Effectiveness
courses.description: This course allows the learner to examine personal values, strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats as they relate to successful leadership practices and behaviors in complex health care organizations. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Advanced Leadership II: Strategic Effectiveness
courses.description: This course builds upon foundational leadership knowledge to incorporate executive practices essential to successfully leading larger health care delivery systems and health professions organizations into the future. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Practice Inquiry I
courses.description: Course and project hours focused on identifying an evidence-based clinical practice question and resources necessary to support the DNP Project.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisite, NURS 778; permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- or corequisite.

courses.title: Practice Inquiry II
courses.description: Course and project hours focused on methodologies for planning and implementing the DNP Project.
courses.requisites: Pre- or co-requisites, NURS 778, 779, 941; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites or co-requisites.

courses.title: Practice Inquiry III
courses.description: Course and project hours focused on issues related to the implementation, evaluation, and dissemination findings of the DNP Project.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, NURS 778, 779, 941, 942, and 994; permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- or corequisites.

courses.title: Population Health in a Global Context
courses.description: This course analyzes the complexities that contribute to the health of populations in a local to global context. This course will prepare leaders to integrate evidence-based approaches that impact the health of populations, building upon skills and knowledge developed throughout the program. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Analysis of the Academic Role in Nursing Education
courses.description: Knowledge, theories, and skills necessary for transition into an academic teaching role in university schools of nursing. Particular emphasis on the teaching-learning process as used in higher education.

courses.title: Mentored Teaching Practicum
courses.description: Admission to the PhD program in nursing and successful completion of qualifying examination. Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. Application of educational theory and methods in teaching activities with mentor. Provides opportunities to analyze course design, implement objectives, evaluate student competencies, and practice in teaching methods.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: From Theory to Intervention and Implementation
courses.description: Required preparation, NURS 912 or graduate level theory course. In-depth exploration of selected programmatic research in nursing and related fields on prevention and management of chronic conditions in order to generate and evaluate treatment theory and intervention protocol.

courses.title: Designing Intervention Studies
courses.description: Examines methodological, ethical, and practical issues in the design and implementation of theory-based intervention studies.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NURS 957; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Proseminar in Nursing
courses.description: Proseminars are offered for one, two, or three credits. Topics differ each semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Writing for Publication
courses.description: In this course, students apply principles and practices of writing to the preparation of manuscripts for publication.

courses.title: Issues in Gerontological and Geriatric Research
courses.description: This course is designed to enhance the student's knowledge of relevant issues researchers face when planning, designing, and implementing research with an older adult population.

courses.title: Implementing Health System Innovations in Complex Organizations
courses.description: Explores the application of implementation science and other relevant theory, focusing on the role of the executive nurse in integrating innovations into complex systems.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisite, NURS 779, 871, 873, 874; permission of the instructor for students lacking the pre- or corequisites.

courses.title: Economics and Financing of Health Care Systems
courses.description: This course examines economic and finance principles in health care from various perspectives including small to large healthcare organizations. Students will gain an understanding of the perspective of economics in the allocation of resources in the healthcare sector. Nursing majors only.

courses.title: Writing the Pre-/Post-Doctoral Training Plan for a Research Intensive Career
courses.description: Explore components of and rationale for a pre-/post-doctoral training plan and its relevance for planning a research intensive career. Students will write a personalized training plan following grant criteria.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, Graduate status or permission of the instructor; NURS 959 or equivalent (including postdoctoral status); permission of primary mentor.

courses.title: Applied Data Analysis
courses.description: This course focuses on the application of statistical concepts to the analysis of health care data and includes evaluation and presentation of the results.

courses.title: Measurement and Data Quality in Health Research
courses.description: This course will examine the links between measurement theory and practice, emphasizing study design, data collection methods, and data quality. Students will critically evaluate concepts underlying measurement reliability and validity and explore the construction of measurement tools and their use in quantitative research. The course will incorporate a combination of theory, methods, and practical skill development, including training in statistical software (e.g., SAS, SPSS, or Stata) for factor analysis and computation of reliability measures. Students will be prepared to critically evaluate methodological issues in quantitative measurement and develop measurement approaches for research proposals. Permission of the instructor for students lacking the required preparation.

courses.title: Qualitative Analysis
courses.description: Required preparation, doctoral level qualitative methods course or NURS 977. Emphasizes the work of analysis and interpretation. Students apply relevant qualitative techniques to their own data.

courses.title: Research Seminar and Practicum: Guided Individual Research Experience
courses.description: Directs students to develop research skills related to the dissertation and to their future research.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Elective Doctor of Nursing Practice Residency
courses.description: This course focuses on the synthesis of knowledge related to advanced practice, practice leadership, and practice inquiry and is composed of a residency related to the DNP project.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: PhD Dissertation/DNP Project
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Food, Fitness, and Health
courses.description: This course introduces undergraduates to evidence-based nutrition and exercise science, empowering them to critically evaluate media claims, explore diverse professional perspectives, and apply practical strategies to promote health in college and beyond.

courses.title: Introduction to Food Studies: From Science to Society
courses.description: Introduction to food studies covering a variety of topics including how food was consumed over history, land use and aquaculture, food in the arts, food and culture in the American South, food politics, and nutrition science. Previously offered as ANTH 175.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Nutrition
courses.description: Relationships of human nutrition to health and disease. Integration of biology, chemistry, and social sciences as related to human function. Nutrient composition of foods and safety of the food supply.

courses.title: Sustainable Local Food Systems: Intersection of Local Foods and Public Health
courses.description: This course examines the health, economic, and environmental impacts of our current food system with a focus on current efforts to build a more local, equitable, and sustainable food system, including looking at systemic racism and its effect on the food system.

courses.title: Global Sustainable Food Systems
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of global food systems drivers, elements, and activities; key players; key problems, and potential solutions. Students will explore these challenges worldwide, gaining insight into the design, implementation, and impact of programs, policies, and interventions aimed at addressing them.

courses.title: Nutrition in Action: Applied Service-Learning and Community Engagement
courses.description: This course provides undergraduate nutrition students with the opportunity to integrate their academic study of nutrition with community-based service. Students would get hands-on experience in the field of nutrition and public health as part of this course working with a community-based food or nutrition organization. Students will apply foundational knowledge of nutrition by engaging with community health centers, community gardens, food pantries, non-profit organizations, schools, and/or public health organizations aligned with students' career interests. Through hands-on projects, reflection, and collaboration, students develop practical skills in nutrition education, communication, and program implementation while fostering civic responsibility and cultural awareness.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research Experience in Nutrition
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. For undergraduates enrolled in the department's baccalaureate degree program. Directed readings or laboratory study on a selected topic. May be taken more than once for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Introduction to Nutritional Biochemistry
courses.description: Function of the human body focusing on chemical properties, function, and metabolism of nutrients. Biochemistry of nutrients with a limited focus on medical aspects of nutrient metabolism. For advanced undergraduates and graduate students needing to enhance background prior to NUTR 600.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, BIOL 101, CHEM 101 and 102, and NUTR 240; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Food and Nutrition Policy in Public Health
courses.description: This course focuses on food and nutrition policy on a federal, state, and local level. Topics covered include policy formation, interest/consumer advocacy groups, key legislation, how research informs policy, equity and diversity, global food policy issues, sustainability and health, advocacy, and current public health nutrition policy hot topics and examples.

courses.title: Foundations of Nutrition Interventions
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to clinical trials in nutrition, including experimental designs, nutrition intervention methods, and skills necessary to critically analyze, describe, and evaluate feeding and behavioral nutrition interventions. The course covers concepts, skills and methods related to nutrition interventions, with an emphasis on theory-based interventions at the individual, community, or environmental levels to improve health and nutrition outcomes.

courses.title: Human Metabolism: Macronutrients
courses.description: Cell biochemistry and physiology emphasizing integration of proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids in whole-body metabolism; regulation of energy expenditure, food intake, metabolic adaptations, and gene expression; and macronutrient-related diseases (atherosclerosis, obesity).
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NUTR 400; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Food And Your Life Stages
courses.description: This course covers nutrition during the life cycle. Units include women during preconception, pregnancy, and lactation; infancy; childhood; adolescence; and older adults (65+). Nutrient and energy needs, assessment of nutritional status, and cultural and socioeconomic barriers are discussed for each phase.

courses.title: Human Metabolism: Micronutrients
courses.description: Cell biochemistry and physiology emphasizing metabolism of vitamins and minerals including antioxidant protection, immune function, nutrient control of gene expression, and disease states induced by deficiencies (e.g., iron-deficient anemia).
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, NUTR 400 and 600; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.title: Nutrition Research Seminar
courses.description: The changing landscape of nutritional science research has increased the demand for early-career researchers to be more transdisciplinary, perform highly rigorous research, and be prepared for less-traditional research positions. This course is designed to introduce first-year undergraduate BSPH nutrition students to the foundations of nutrition research. It provides an introduction to nutrition research topics, research methods, study design, research ethics, and the generation and development of research questions within the context of nutrition science. This course also covers aspects of professionalism in public health.

courses.title: Navigating Culture, Technology, and Communication in Nutrition
courses.description: In the course, students will explore cultural foodways and regional food practices. Students will examine the influence of technology and social media on effective communication and nutrition messaging. Emphasis will be placed on cultural awareness and leveraging digital platforms in nutrition practice. Students will learn how to frame messages for individuals, groups, and broader public audiences.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, NUTR 240; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Mouse Models of Human Disease
courses.description: This course will focus on the laboratory mouse as a model organism to learn fundamental genetic concepts and understand how state-of-the-art experimental approaches are being used to elucidate gene function and the genetic architecture of biological traits.

courses.title: Food Service Systems Management Experience
courses.description: This is a food service management practicum that applies the basic concepts of institutional food service systems. Two laboratory hours per week.

courses.title: Honors Research in Nutrition
courses.description: This is an honors course for research for the first semester of senior year, to be followed by NUTR 692H in the second semester. NUTR 691H/692H is a two-course sequence. Enrollment is only for students approved to conduct a senior honors thesis project.

courses.title: Honors Research in Nutrition
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Directed readings or laboratory study of a selected topic. Requires a written proposal to be submitted to and approved by the B.S.P.H. Committee and faculty research director. A written report is required. May be taken more than once for credit. Six laboratory hours per week.

courses.title: Nutrition Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Individual arrangements with faculty for bachelor and master students to participate in ongoing research.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.title: Readings in Nutrition
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Reading and tutorial guidance in special areas of nutrition.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.title: Nutrition Practicum Preparation
courses.description: This course provides support for the practicum process and trains students on how to ethically, meaningfully, and professionally engage and prepare for practicum placements. Students will learn how to work within their organization and their stakeholders through building skills in leadership and interprofessional practice. Additionally, students will sharpen their clinical skills in preparation for their hospital-based experience and include mandatory on-boarding requirements.

courses.title: Human Nutrition
courses.description: Fundamental scientific premises of human nutrition. This course covers the basic concepts of macro and micronutrients, food sources, and the evidence-based requirements for a healthy diet. This course integrates nutritional needs of populations, with an emphasis on nutrition-related diseases, including over and undernutrition.

courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy 1
courses.description: A lecture and skills course where students practice skills used in nutrition therapy and the Nutrition Care Process (such as calculating caloric intake, modifying intake, calculating sodium content of intakes, carbohydrate counting, exchanges, etc.) under the supervision of a Registered Dietitian. This course covers nutrition during the life cycle. Units include women during preconception, pregnancy, and lactation; infancy; childhood; adolescence; and older adults (65+). Nutrient and energy needs, assessment of nutritional status, and cultural and socioeconomic barriers are discussed for each phase.

courses.title: Nutrition Across the Lifecycle
courses.description: This course covers global perspectives on nutrition across the life cycle including US and international food-based recommendations for the following life phases: Adults, Pregnancy and Lactation, Infants and Toddlers, Children and Adolescents, and Older Adults. Heavy emphasis is placed on understanding diet-disease relationships across each life phase as well as opportunities and strategies for intervention using life course and ecological perspectives.

courses.title: Nutrition Communication, Counseling and Culture
courses.description: This course teaches the future nutrition professional the art and science of communicating with individuals, groups, and the public. Students will enhance cultural awareness, practice counseling individuals and facilitating groups, and frame nutrition messages for mass media including social media.

courses.title: Nutrition Communication, Culture and Equity
courses.description: This course teaches the future nutrition professional the art and science of communicating with individuals, groups, and the public. Students will explore the role of nutrition in different cultures and how to frame nutrition messages for mass media including social media. The course will also focus on nutrition justice and nutritional health equity.

courses.title: Nutritional Biochemistry, Metabolism and Health
courses.description: Introduction to biochemistry and functions of macro- and micro-nutrients with a limited focus on medical aspects of nutrient deficiencies and metabolism. Focus on chemical structures, chemical properties, metabolism, and functions of macro- and micro-nutrients.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, BIOL 252 and 252L, BIOL 422 and 422L, NUTR 240, CHEM 261 and CHEM 430, or permission from the instructor.

courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy 2
courses.description: A lecture and skills course where students practice skills used in nutrition therapy and the Nutrition Care Process (such as calculating caloric intake and modifying intake, calculating diabetic diets, calculating sodium content of intakes, etc.) under the supervision of a Registered Dietitian.

courses.title: Community Nutrition
courses.description: This course provides graduate students with competencies to assess factors that influence the nutritional status of the population; identify community resources to promote and support nutrition and health; conduct community assets and needs assessments; and design, implement, and evaluate public health nutrition programs.

courses.title: International Nutrition
courses.description: Provides a broad overview of international nutrition research issues, programs, and policies. Topics will include micronutrient deficiencies, child feeding and growth, determinants of under- and over-nutrition, chronic disease and nutrition, food fortification and supplementation, and nutrition intervention programs and policy.

courses.title: Taxes, Bans & Burgers: Directed Readings in Global Food Policy
courses.description: Course will explore the social, historical, and political context of how individuals make decisions about what to eat; how this context shapes food policy; and how these policies in turn shape individual behavior, by employing a comparative framework over three countries (China, Mexico, and the U.S.).

courses.title: Global Food and Nutrition Security
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles of food and nutrition security from a global lens; addresses nutrition in emergencies and humanitarian contexts; and the role that nutrition security plays in improving the health and well being of populations. Aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills required to conduct population and community-based nutrition research, to assess the food and nutrition security status of vulnerable population groups. Will cover key aspects related to food security interventions, taking into consideration cultural, social, geo-political and environmental dimensions in conflict- affected settings and humanitarian contexts, with a focus on the Middle East and North Africa.

courses.title: mHealth for Behavior Change
courses.description: This special topics seminar examines the impact and potential of mobile health interventions and apps for health behavior change. The overall course objective is to understand state of the science and future potential to leverage mobile phones and wearable technologies in innovative and powerful behavior change interventions to improve health. The course considers adaptation of eHealth interventions for mobile delivery, unique opportunities with mHealth, data collection via mobile devices and sensors, and using the data.

courses.title: Global Healthy And Sustainable Food Systems
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of global food systems drivers, elements, and activities; key players; key problems, and potential solutions. Students will explore these challenges worldwide, gaining insight into the design, implementation, and impact of programs, policies, and interventions aimed at addressing them.

courses.title: Local Food Systems, Health, and the Environment
courses.description: This course addresses how our current food system impacts the health of people, communities, and the environment. Students will hear from experts across these domains and review the current literature about evidence-based approaches to address the major challenges. Students will learn how to assist local food system partners on how to promote a healthier and sustainable food system. Students may enroll in a 3 credit or 1 credit option.

courses.title: Nutrition and Cancer: Insights for Prevention and Treatment
courses.description: This course covers emerging research on the interplay of nutrition, physical activity and cancer from a multidisciplinary perspective. Students will gain a solid scientific basis to better weigh and interpret the information available on nutrition and cancer while further developing skills in presenting and discussing emerging research focused on the links between cancer and a range of diet-related exposures (including obesity, micronutrients, dietary patterns, meat intake, coffee consumption, dietary supplements, and alcohol) and physical activity in relation to the development, progression, treatment and survivorship of the most common types of cancer.

courses.title: Food Science
courses.description: Introduction to foods, chemical and physical properties, nutritional composition, food safety, production, and regulation.

courses.title: Food Science Laboratory
courses.description: Basic culinary techniques. Classes illustrate biochemical processes and food properties covered in lecture. Introduction to new foods and food ideas. Critical evaluation of recipes. Laboratory fee required. Three laboratory hours per week.

courses.title: Food Science Laboratory
courses.description: Basic culinary techniques. Classes illustrate biochemical processes and food properties covered in lecture. Introduction to new foods and food ideas. Critical evaluation of recipes. Laboratory fee required. Three laboratory hours per week.

courses.title: Foundations in Nutrition Epidemiology
courses.description: This course introduces basic methods of dietary assessment, reviews various topics in nutrition epidemiology, and teaches the skills needed for critical evaluation of the nutritional epidemiologic literature.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPHG 711, SPHG 712, SPHG 713, SPHG 721, SPHG 722 (MPH Core Courses) or PhD Student Status.

courses.title: Clinical Trials in Nutrition
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to nutrition interventions and help students develop knowledge and skills necessary to critically analyze, describe, and evaluate behavioral nutrition interventions. The course covers concepts, skills and methods related to nutrition interventions, with an emphasis on theory-based interventions at the individual, community, or environmental levels to improve health and nutrition outcomes.

courses.title: Nutrition Policy
courses.description: This course focuses on food and nutrition policy on federal, state, local, and organizational levels. Topics covered include legislative and regulatory processes, policy evaluation, advocacy, agencies/organizations involved with food and nutrition policy/advocacy, how research informs policy, and ways to engage with food and nutrition policy/advocacy efforts. Key food and nutrition-related legislation and current public health nutrition policy examples from the US and globally will be discussed. Permission of the instructor for undergraduates.

courses.title: Global Cardiometabolic Disease Seminar
courses.description: This core seminar addresses biology, genetics, epidemiology, intervention and policy strategies relevant for addressing global cardiometabolic disease, as well as, professional development and responsible conduct of research in global settings.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Physical Activity Epidemiology and Public Health
courses.description: This course provides an overview of major issues in physical activity measurements, population distribution, correlates, impacts (physically and economically), and public health recommendations. Interventions, including relevant theories, will be reviewed. Three lecture hours per week.

courses.title: Introduction to Obesity: Cell to Society
courses.description: Provides a broad survey of obesity research including measurement issues, biological, social and economic etiologies, health and economic consequences, and prevention and treatment of obesity.

courses.title: Introduction to Epidemiology for Nutrition Applications
