courses.description: Explores key sociological concepts through the lens of food: labor, power, social status, political economy, social inequalities, social movements, globalization, and social justice. Additionally, this course examines the emergence of food related social movements, food policy, and food related social problems, including famine, obesity, food deserts, food insecurity, GMOs (genetically modified organisms), CAFOs (concentrated animal feeding operations), industrial agriculture, environmental degradation, and poor health.

courses.title: Aging
courses.description: The process of aging from birth to death, with a concentration on the later years of life, examined from a broad perspective. Topics include individual change over the life-course, the social context of aging, and the aging of American society.

courses.title: Immigration in Contemporary America
courses.description: Why do people leave their homes for unfamiliar places? This course examines migration as a defining force shaping modern America. Through documentary films, news analysis, scholarly writings and family migration stories, students explore the economic and political realities and experiences behind immigration statistics. We'll investigate refugee, border policies, and how communities adapt to newcomers. Students will develop skills in interviewing, policy and media analysis, and understanding how personal stories connect to broader social patterns.

courses.title: Race, Class, and Gender
courses.description: Conceptualizations of gender, race, and class and how, separately and in combination, they are interpreted by the wider society. Emphasis on how black and working-class women make sense of their experiences at work and within the family.

courses.title: Sociology of Emotions
courses.description: The course examines how emotions are organized within social groupings and institutions. Differences in socialization by gender, ethnicity, social class, and age will be explored.

courses.title: Contemporary Social Theory
courses.description: Analysis of current problems in general social theory; action and structure, justice and equity, social change and reproduction. Contrast and evaluation of leading approaches to solutions.

courses.title: United States Poverty and Public Policy
courses.description: This course explores U.S. poverty and public policy through a sociological lens. It examines key aspects of poverty (e.g., measurement, trends, causes, consequences), the U.S. welfare system (e.g., social assistance program, welfare reform, international comparisons), and other substantive policy areas (e.g. food/housing insecurity, employment, healthcare, education). This course encourages critical reflection and assessment of poverty and the motivations and implications of anti-poverty policies and other policies that impact Americans.

courses.title: Health and Society
courses.description: Health is not simply an individual-level characteristic affected by genes, behavior, and healthcare. Indeed, individual-level health is profoundly affected by social resources like education, money, and friendships; institutions like churches and schools; and larger contexts such as neighborhoods and states. This course broadens the study of health far beyond the individual to think deeply about the social forces, including inequalities, that are important for the health of individuals and populations.

courses.title: Negotiating Organizations
courses.description: This course examines how organizations negotiate with one another in economic, political, and social settings. Students analyze conflicts among corporations, governments, labor unions, nonprofits, and advocacy groups through case studies and negotiation simulations.

courses.title: Senior Honors Research and Seminar
courses.description: Permission of the department. SOCI 691H is required of senior honors candidates. Individual student research (under supervision of an advisor). Weekly seminar to discuss work on honors thesis, as well as special topics in sociology.

courses.title: Senior Honors Research and Seminar
courses.description: Permission of the department. Individual student research under supervision of an advisor. Weekly seminar to discuss work on honors thesis as well as special topics in sociology.

courses.title: Undergraduate/Graduate Study in Sociology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Graduate study in sociology for undergraduate students. Undergraduate students taking a 700- or 800-level course in sociology register via this course and complete all requirements for the associated graduate course.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: History of Social Thought
courses.description: Graduate standing in sociology or permission of the instructor. Historic social ideas of Western culture are considered against a background of general cultural analysis in terms of systematic theory. Required of all graduate degree candidates in sociology.

courses.title: Measurement and Data Collection
courses.description: Provides an introduction to measurement theory and a review of various methods of data-gathering. Gaining experience with a variety of techniques of measurement and preparing a pretested research proposal are required for all students.

courses.title: Statistics for Sociologists
courses.description: Provides an introduction to probability theory, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, and the algebra of expectations. Emphasis is on elements useful to research sociologists, including bivariate regression and correlation.

courses.title: Linear Regression Models
courses.description: The course presents regression analysis and related techniques. The major topics are the assumptions of the regression model, dummy variables and interaction terms, outlier diagnostics, multicollinearity, specification error, heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation. The final section introduces path analysis, recursive models, and nonrecursive systems.

courses.title: Qualitative Inquiry
courses.description: This course is required for graduate study in Sociology at UNC. The main goal is for students to develop basic literacy and proficiency in the methodological approaches commonly known as "qualitative methods," including semi-structured interviewing, participant observation, case studies, and content analysis.

courses.title: Analysis of Categorical Data
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Introduction to techniques and programs for analyzing categorical variables and nonlinear models. Special attention is given to decomposition of complex contingency tables, discriminant function analysis, Markov chains, and nonmetric multidimensional scaling.

courses.title: Seminar on Social Networks
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Theoretical and substantive issues in social network analysis. Focus is on models of social structure.

courses.title: Structural Equations with Latent Variables
courses.description: This course examines models sometimes referred to as LISREL models. Topics include path analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, measurement error, model identification, nonrecursive models, and multiple indicators.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SOCI 708; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Longitudinal and Multilevel Data Analysis
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to event history analysis or survival analysis, random effects and fixed effects models for longitudinal data, multilevel models for linear and discrete multilevel data, and growth curve models.

courses.title: Participant Observation and In-Depth Interviewing
courses.description: Students will learn the methods of participant observation and in-depth interviewing. Each student will collect data (provide detailed fieldnotes and transcriptions of interviews) in one group or setting for the duration of the course. Such topics as gaining access, ethics of research, and analysis of data will be covered.

courses.title: Experimental Design in Sociology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Statistical aspects of experimental designs, with emphasis on applied problems involved in executing a statistically sound design.

courses.title: Survey Sampling
courses.description: The different sampling techniques are discussed. Major emphasis on planning of large-scale sample surveys rather than on statistical theory.

courses.title: Data Collection Methods
courses.description: Reviews alternative data collection techniques used in surveys, concentrating on the impact these techniques have on the quality of survey data. Topics covered include errors associated with nonresponse, interviewing, and data processing.

courses.title: Questionnaire Design
courses.description: Examines the stages of questionnaire design including developmental interviewing, question writing, question evaluation, pretesting, questionnaire ordering, and formatting. Reviews the literature on questionnaire construction. Provides hands-on experience in developing questionnaires.

courses.title: Case Studies in Surveys
courses.description: A number of external speakers from government and industry will describe various problems they encounter in surveys. Students will be challenged to develop proposals for addressing the problems, citing the literature as appropriate.

courses.title: Survey Computing
courses.description: Introduces basic statistical concepts and practices emphasizing the analysis of real data. Provides training in the use of the SAS statistical analysis system and the practical problems of stratification, clustering, and weighting in survey analysis.

courses.title: Social Movements
courses.description: The structure and dynamics of social movements and their societal environment, with special reference to sociopolitical movements of minority and low status groups in industrialized and third world societies.

courses.title: Seminar in Political Sociology
courses.description: The relationships between social structure and political decisions. Regimes and social structure; bureaucracies, political associations, and professions; science and politics; closed and open politics; political movements and change.

courses.title: Comparative Welfare States
courses.description: This course examines the development, achievements, present crisis, and future of welfare states in advanced industrial democracies.

courses.title: Comparative and Historical Analysis Exploration
courses.description: Exploration and use of techniques for the comparative study of social processes and historical events. Special attention is devoted to methodologies that facilitate the collection, analysis, and interpretation of historical and/or comparative phenomena.

courses.title: Race and Ethnicity
courses.description: This course reviews the historical and contemporary sociological literature on race and ethnicity. Students will gain an advanced state-of-the-art understanding of how racial and ethnic groups emerge and evolve, how these constructs shape societies, how they influence intergroup relations, and their role in identity formation.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.title: Seminar in Family Sociology
courses.description: Introduces students to a wide range of studies to develop familiarity with the empirical, theoretical, and methodological foundations of family research in sociology. Examines demographic trends; relationship formation, dissolution, and dynamics; childbearing, childrearing, and parenthood; family structure/transitions; work/family issues; health and caregiving; gender, race/ethnicity/nativity, and social class; intergenerational and interhousehold families; and policies affecting families.

courses.title: The Life Course
courses.description: Provides an intense introduction to the life course as a theoretical orientation and methodology (logic of inquiry).

courses.title: Integrating Social and Biological Perspectives on Human Health
courses.description: Student will learn key theories and methodological approaches for how social processes, socio-spatial organization, and social inequality are associated with health patterns, changes, and disparities; theories/approaches for studying human health from a biological perspective; and strategies using integrated social and biological research perspectives and address advantages and challenges.

courses.title: The Life Course and Aging: Theory and Methods in Social and Epidemiologic Research
courses.description: This seminar surveys the major theoretical paradigms, methodological tools and empirical studies of aging and cohort analysis that are of enduring importance to the understanding of social change, epidemiologic trends, and related population and life course processes and dynamics. It aims to provide a sweeping review of the theoretical models in recent life course and aging research and introduce useful guidelines on how to conduct empirical analysis.

courses.title: Health and Developmental Trajectories From Adolescence into Adulthood
courses.description: Graduate seminar that integrates theory and research on health and developmental trajectories across the early life course using the design and data from the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health). Within the social and epidemiology life course frameworks, this course facilitates student research using Add Health.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.title: Demography: Theory, Substance, Techniques, Part I
courses.description: A basic introduction to the discipline of demography. Materials covered include population history, data sources, mortality and fertility trends, and differentials and techniques of analysis.

courses.title: Demography: Theory, Substance, Techniques, Part II
courses.description: A continuation of SOCI 830. Materials covered include population growth and stable population theory, migration and distribution, population policy, and population estimates and projections.

courses.title: Migration and Population Distribution
courses.description: Treats migration trends, patterns, and differentials and their effects on population distribution in continental and regional areas. Attention is given to theoretical and methodological problems in the study of population movement.

courses.title: Socioeconomic Factors in Fertility
courses.description: Study of fertility differentials by social and economic factors, changes over time, the manner in which these factors affect fertility, and the implications thereof for fertility-control programs.

courses.title: Mortality: Social Demographic Perspectives
courses.description: This advanced seminar covers mortality date and measurement, the inequality of death, trends in morbidity and mortality, and explanations of mortality decline. Social demographic perspectives receive primary emphasis.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SOCI 830; Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Social Stratification
courses.description: Analysis of major theories of and approaches to the study of social inequality, with attention to how the various theories and approaches are operationalized. Focus on recent research in labor markets and worldwide inequality.

courses.title: Sociology of Gender
courses.description: Reviews theory on variation in men's and women's gender roles, with emphasis on industrialized societies and women's roles.

courses.title: Seminar in Urban Sociology
courses.description: Theory and research in the study of the location and growth of urban areas, the effect urban areas have upon behavior, and the study of social behavior in different urban subareas. Each member of the seminar completes a project interrelating theory and research.

courses.title: Poverty in America
courses.description: This graduate seminar will study trends, causes, and consequences of poverty in America, covering the topics of single-mother families, child poverty, low-wage work, immigrant families, and welfare reform and social policy.

courses.title: Black Feminist Theory
courses.description: Black Feminist Theory centers praxis, justice, and liberation in the production of knowledge. This graduate level course engages writings in black feminist theory to critically interrogate social inequality at the intersections of racism, capitalism, and heteropatriarchy. In this course, we will focus on the histories of these systems in a global context and how black feminist theory challenges traditional modes of knowledge production and hegemonic claims that reproduce these structures. Specifically, we will explore themes of epistemic violence, colonialism and racial capitalism, social movements, reproductive justice, and carcerality from diverse black feminist perspectives in sociology and beyond.

courses.title: Sociology of Organizations
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Structural features of organizations. Behavior in organizations. Organizational career patterns. Comparative analysis of structure, behavior, and careers in different types of organizations. Interorganization and organization-environment relations.

courses.title: Occupations and Work
courses.description: The changing occupational system. Structural types of labor markets. Occupational organization, role sets, power relations, careers, and satisfaction in different types of labor markets and occupations.

courses.title: Sociology of Health, Illness, and Healing
courses.description: This seminar provides a broad introduction to the sociology of health and illness. Classic and contemporary perspectives, as well as empirical evidence, are covered. Questions such as, "how (and why) are health and illness socially constructed and socially distributed?" and "what can be done to address these phenomena?" are examined.

courses.title: Sociology of Culture
courses.description: Focuses on substantive and theoretical issues in this field and their intellectual origins. Topics include organizations, art, religion, science, class, and politics. Quantitative and qualitative approaches are examined.

courses.title: Sociology of Religion
courses.description: An introductory, graduate-level survey of the sociology of religion as a field of study, reviewing literature on important theoretical approaches and key problems and issues in the field.

courses.title: The Sociology of Science: Science as a Social and Cultural Activity
courses.description: This course examines the production of scientific knowledge. The focus is on the processes by which scientific knowledge and technological artifacts are constructed through cultural practices and the organizational of scientific work.

courses.title: Field Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Survey Practicum
courses.description: Applied workshop in sample survey design and implementation. The student works in a data collection center under the guidance of the instructor. Course focuses on real world problems in data collection and their practical, cost-effective solutions.

courses.title: Seminar in Selected Topics
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. The course description for a particular semester is available in the departmental office.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Training Program Seminars
courses.description: Continuing seminars in selected topics.

courses.title: Reading and Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Reading
courses.description: Library research or field research on a selected topic under guidance of the instructor.

courses.title: Reading and Research in Methodology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Special work on selected problems of research methodology.

courses.title: Reading and Research in Methodology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Special work on selected problems of research methodology.

courses.title: Publishing in Sociology
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This seminar exposes students to a variety of issues related to journal publication in sociology, such as types of journals and collaboration, the experience of writing an article for submission to a journal, reviewing articles for journals, and responding to editorial decisions.

courses.title: Seminar on the Teaching of Sociology
courses.description: Doctoral candidacy in sociology or permission of the instructor. Examines the teacher's role and the teaching process, planning a course and constructing syllabi, testing for teaching or grading, evaluating teacher performance and the needs of different student populations.

courses.title: Writing Academic Research for Sociology
courses.description: Course material will cover how to write an introduction, literature review, methods section, results section, and discussion. It will also include overviews on the style of academic writing, citation practices, and how to think about situating a research paper within a body of scholarly literature. Readings will stem from published resources on academic writing. Assignments include submissions of student writing (e.g., drafts of a literature review) and peer review of other students' written work. The final course requirement is a defended MA thesis or a thesis draft with a scheduled defense.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.description: Individual research in a selected field under the direction of a member of the department.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.description: Individual research in a selected field under the direction of a member of the department.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.title: Strategies for Social Good: From Analysis to Action
courses.description: This course focuses on social, economic, and structural factors that create and contribute to problems in daily living and explores solutions to foster positive social change. Using social work perspectives, students will engage in reflective assignments, social issue analysis, and solution-identification related to urgent human needs, strengthening communities, and promoting well-being.

courses.title: Families in Focus: Navigating Challenges, Inspiring Change
courses.description: This course examines the social, economic, and policy issues shaping the lives of children and families in North Carolina and beyond. Using a Person-in-Environment framework, students will explore interventions at the micro, mezzo, and macro levels to address social complexities and promote family well-being. Through reflective assignments, case studies, group projects, and policy discussions, students will gain an in-depth look at the intersection of policy, practice, and advocacy while connecting students to contemporary issues affecting families.

courses.title: Human Development in Context I: Infancy to Adolescence
courses.description: This course provides an overview of child and adolescent development in an environmental context, using a social work lens to analyze major theoretical frameworks.

courses.title: Social Work and Systems of Change
courses.description: Through personal reflexivity and historical/systemic analysis, this course examines dynamics of institutional barriers through a critical theory lens. Students explore implications for social work practice, including professional complicity and resistance.

courses.title: Human Development in Context II: Adulthood
courses.description: This course provides an overview of adult development in environmental and systemic contexts, using social work approaches to the analysis of major developmental frameworks.

courses.title: Foundations For Evidence-Based Practice & Program Evaluation I
courses.description: This course introduces students to the foundational principles of social work research and evidence-based practice. Through critical engagement with research literature, students will learn how to identify, evaluate, and apply empirical evidence to inform ethical and effective social work interventions. Emphasis is placed on research design, community-engaged methods, and the role of data in advancing social work practice. Students will develop core skills in literature review, peer collaboration, and research communication, preparing them for evidence-informed social work practice.

courses.title: Foundational Aspects of Engagement and Interviewing
courses.description: This course explores foundational theories, concepts, and skills related to engagement with individuals, groups, communities, and organizations. Emphasis will be placed on building rapport, reflexivity, critical discourse and dialogue, demonstrating cultural humility, and establishing professional helping relationships across micro, mezzo, and macro levels.

courses.title: Social Welfare Systems and Policies
courses.description: Explores the US social welfare system and its implications for social work practice. Social welfare policies are analyzed, yielding implications for advocacy and action.

courses.title: From Classroom to Community: Developing Competencies for Practicum Education
courses.description: This course prepares students for successful social work practicum experiences by integrating theory and practice through reflection, skill-building, and community-engaged learning.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SOWO 300, SOWO 301, SOWO 315, and SOWO 330.

courses.title: Social Work Study Abroad
courses.description: Variable content. Course examines international social issues, programs, and policies and their impact on client populations and cultures in a particular country or global region.

courses.title: Social Work Study Abroad: Africa
courses.description: Course examines social issues, development strategies, health/mental health programs. Explores how country's fledgling democracy and people are redesigning organizations and interventions to respond to the needs of South Africans.

courses.title: Foundations for Evidence-Based Practice & Program Evaluation II
courses.description: This course introduces students to the key components of evaluating interventions, which is necessary for evidence-based practice. These concepts include the scientific method, human ethics, development of research questions, measurement, and quantitative and qualitative analysis. Students will apply the concepts learned in this course to design their own evaluation project of a social work intervention.

courses.title: Undergraduate Social Work Practicum
courses.description: In the undergraduate social work practicum, students practice social work knowledge, values, skills, and cognitive and affective processes within a variety of human service settings.

courses.title: Undergraduate Social Work Practicum Seminar
courses.description: This course assists students in integrating and applying classroom learning with their undergraduate practicum. Opportunities are provided for self-reflection, case presentation, discussion of social work values and ethics in practice, and peer consultation in alignment with standards of our professional accrediting body.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SOWO 300, SOWO 301, SOWO 305, SOWO 310, SOWO 315, SOWO 330, SOWO 350; Corequisite, SOWO 420.

courses.title: Social Work Practice with Individuals, Families, and Groups
courses.description: This course provides the foundation for social work practice with individuals, families, and groups. It emphasizes basic knowledge, analytic and practice skills, and values necessary for practice.

courses.title: Social Work Practice with Organizations and Communities
courses.description: This course introduces students to macro-level social work practice with communities and organizations. Students will build on knowledge and skills gained in SOWO 101 and SOWO 315 to focus on assessment, design, and implementation of interventions with communities, organizations, and broader systems. The course will emphasize the use of evidenced-based, evidence-informed, and participatory approaches to change.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SOWO 101, SOWO 300, SOWO 301, SOWO 305, SOWO 315, SOWO 330.

courses.title: Public Service and Social Change
courses.description: Course examines the role of volunteer involvement and citizen participation in community development, grassroots organizing, advocacy, and other efforts to create a more just and democratic society. Includes a service-learning requirement.

courses.title: Preprofessional Special Topic
courses.description: Focuses on current professional social work issues. The focus will be specified each time the course is offered.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Community Organizing for Social Change
courses.description: Course examines different types of advocacy strategies and their use in efforts both to enhance the delivery of services to disadvantaged populations and to promote social change in communities.

courses.title: Seminar in Service Learning
courses.description: Participants explore frameworks, values, and skills around the democratic principles of service, citizenship, and social justice. Accompanies an intensive, paid internship in a local nonprofit agency.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Social Work
courses.description: Research under the supervision of a selected instructor. Approved learning contract required. Permission of the instructor and school required.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.title: Human Development in Context I: Infancy to Adolescence
courses.description: This course provides an overview of child and adolescent development in an environmental context, using an anti-oppressive lens to analyze major theoretical frameworks.

courses.title: Oppression and Resistance in Social Work
courses.description: Through personal reflexivity and historical/systemic analysis, this course examines dynamics of institutional oppression through a critical theory lens. Students explore implications for social work practice, including professional complicity and resistance.

courses.title: Human Development in Context II: Adulthood
courses.description: This course provides an overview of adult development in environmental and systemic contexts, using critical and anti-oppressive approaches to the analysis of major developmental frameworks.

courses.title: Foundations for Evidence-Based Practice and Program Evaluation
courses.description: Develop knowledge of evidence-based practice, including skills needed to identify, acquire, and assess appropriate interventions for practice and skills required to evaluate their own social work practice.

courses.title: Social Work Generalist Practicum I
courses.description: Students learn generalist competencies and behaviors by demonstrating core knowledge, skills, and values through direct (individuals, families, small groups) and macro (organizations, communities) practice in an agency setting (Field Fee: $300).

courses.title: Social Work Generalist Practicum II
courses.description: A continuation of SOWO 520, students demonstrate an increased knowledge of generalist competencies and behaviors through direct (individuals, families, small groups) and macro (organizations, communities) practice in an agency setting. (Field fee: $300.)

courses.title: Pre-Specialization Practicum for Advanced Standing Students
courses.description: Introduces advanced standing students to specialization competencies and behaviors by demonstrating knowledge, skills, and values in direct (individuals, families, small groups) or macro (organizations, communities) practice in an agency setting. (Field fee: $300.)

courses.title: Generalist Practicum Seminar I
courses.description: Assist students in integrating and applying classroom learning with the generalist practicum. Opportunities are provided for self-reflection, case presentation, discussion of social work values and ethics in practice, and peer consultation in alignment with standards of our professional accrediting body.

courses.title: Generalist Practicum Seminar II
courses.description: Assist students in integrating and applying classroom learning with the generalist practicum. Opportunities are provided for self-reflection, case presentation, discussion of social work values and ethics in practice, and peer consultation in alignment with standards of our professional accrediting body.

courses.title: Social Welfare Systems and Policies
courses.description: Explores the US social welfare system and its implications for social work practice. Social welfare policies are analyzed, yielding implications for advocacy and action.

courses.title: Social Work Practice with Families, Individuals, and Groups
courses.description: Provides the foundation for social work practice with individuals, families, and groups. It emphasizes basic knowledge, analytic and practice skills, and values necessary for practice.

courses.title: Social Work Practice with Organizations and Communities
courses.description: This course focuses on developing knowledge and skills in engagement, assessment, and intervention design and implementation within the context of communities, organizations, and broader systems.

courses.title: Introductory Spanish for Health Professionals
courses.description: This course is intended for students who know no Spanish or so little that they feel the need to start over. Students with more than two semesters of college Spanish are not eligible. The course covers the curriculum of first-semester Spanish taught within a health context, with a focus on speaking.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: This intermediate course is the equivalent of the third semester of college Spanish. Students will hone their listening and speaking skills in class primarily through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a health clinic in rural North Carolina.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: Required preparation, third semester Spanish or equivalent. This advanced course reviews the grammar of the third and fourth semester of college Spanish. Students hone their listening and speaking skills through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a Latino-run health clinic.

courses.title: Treatment Foundation for Problematic Substance Use and Process Addictions
courses.description: Introduces students to the field of problematic substance use and process addiction. Explores historic and current theories of addiction, the key domains of addiction counseling, and applicable ethical and legal considerations.

courses.title: Human Development in Context
courses.description: This course provides an overview of human development in an environmental context, surveying major theoretical frameworks and highlighting the impact of different systems on the development, functioning and health of individuals, families and communities. Course frameworks will include definitions, structural variations, theories, strengths, stressors, and changes that affect functioning needed to carry out practice with clients.

courses.title: Mental Health Recovery and Psychiatric Rehabilitation
courses.description: The concept of mental health recovery is introduced, exploring theoretical foundations and lived experiences of consumers. Psychiatric rehabilitation is discussed as a framework and set of interventions supporting recovery.

courses.title: Special Topics in Human Behavior and Social Environment
courses.description: Permission of the Instructor. Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Foundations for Evidence-based Practice and Program Evaluation
courses.description: Students will develop knowledge of evidence-based practice, including skills needed to identify, acquire and assess appropriate interventions for practice and basic skills required to evaluate their own social work practice.

courses.title: Special Topics in Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Individualized Field Practicum
courses.description: (Field fee: $300.)
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Social Work and the Law
courses.description: Course provides familiarity with legal processes, legal research, and legal analysis within the context of socio-legal issues important to social work practice.

courses.title: Advanced Standing Bridge Course: Social Welfare Policy & Institutional Oppression
courses.description: This course addresses foundational understandings of social welfare policies and the institutional oppression of marginalized groups, focusing on core theoretical frameworks and policy analysis skills.

courses.title: Special Topics in Policy
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Implementing Evidence-Informed Practice w/ Individuals, Families Groups
courses.description: Using a multi-cultural lens, this course introduces students to core evidence-based interventions common to most theoretical approaches. Focus is on building effective direct practice skills applicable across settings and populations.

courses.title: Integrated Behavioral Health Care with Underserved Populations
courses.description: This course teaches practical skills for behavioral health care delivered in primary care settings. In this course you will develop expertise in providing brief interventions as part of an interprofessional care team.

courses.title: The Satir Growth Model: Enhancing Individual, Couple, Family and Organizational Health
courses.description: This practice course will apply Satir Growth Model interventions to help students facilitate the healthy functioning of individuals, couples, families, and organizations.

courses.title: SW at the Interface of the MH & Criminal Justice Systems: Practice, Policy, and Research
courses.description: This course explores social work practice, policy, and research for justice-involved people with mental health and/or substance use disorders.

courses.title: Community Organizing
courses.description: In this course, students will learn and apply the universal skills of community change and broad-based community organizing. Students will learn and practice the skills needed to effectively organize communities.

courses.title: Facilitation Skills Within the Organizational and Community Context
courses.description: Building from group relations theory, this course develops facilitation skills (e.g., agenda setting, process checking, participatory planning, navigating conflict) to engage culturally diverse task group members to achieve identified objectives.

courses.title: Autism and Neurodiversity-Affirming Practice
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the core vulnerabilities faced by autistic and neurodivergent individuals. Selected neurodiversity-affirming evidence-based interventions will be reviewed with ASD across contexts. Disability and social justice issues faced by this population will be discussed throughout the course.

courses.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
courses.description: This course will use the cognitive behavioral therapy CBT framework to teach students how to move from an assessment to intervention using the CBT model.

courses.title: Behavioral Intervention with Children
courses.description: This course teaches basic principles of behavior theory and intervention, current applications, and how to assess, design and implement behavior plans for children.

courses.title: Interpersonal Psychotherapy
courses.description: This practice course focuses on interpersonal psychotherapy, an empirically supported intervention for depression in adolescents and adults. Adaptations for other mental health disorders are discussed.

courses.title: Differential Diagnosis of Mental Health Disorders
courses.description: This course focuses on the process of conducting a differential diagnosis of mental health and substance use disorders using the current Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.

courses.title: Clinical Practice with Addictive Disorders
courses.description: Students develop knowledge, skills, and attitudes specific to clinical practice with clients experiencing Addictive Disorders. This will include effective interventions in a variety of clinical settings utilizing evidence-based and evolving best-practice methodologies.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, SOWO 540 and 700; permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisites.

courses.title: Practice with Diverse Populations Affected by Addiction
courses.description: This advanced practice course provides an overview of the unique problems and needs of diverse populations living with addictive disorders and focuses on the application of culturally sensitive intervention strategies.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, SOWO 540 and 700; permission of the instructor for students lacking the requisites.

courses.title: Motivational Interviewing for the Treatment of Addictive and Mental Health Disorders
courses.description: This course presents the theoretical basis of motivational interviewing (MI), the principles of this counseling approach, and the key strategies for facilitating effective discussions about behavior change with a particular focus on addictive disorders.

courses.title: Social Work Practice with Groups
courses.description: The course is designed to enable students to become more knowledgeable and skillful as direct practice group workers.

courses.title: Dialectical Behavioral Therapy: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), exploring both its theoretical underpinnings as well as its practical application.

courses.title: Differential Diagnosis and Case Formulation
courses.description: This course prepares students to take psychiatric histories, conduct mental status examinations, engage in differential diagnosis decision-making using the DSM-5, write mental health reports, and begin case formulation for treatment planning.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SOWO 540; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740.

courses.title: Special Topics in Direct Practice
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Implementing Evidence-Informed Practice with Organizations and Communities
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to evidence-informed and best practices for program management. Focus is on building effective organizational and community practice skills in implementing new programs and interventions.

courses.title: Integrative Bridge Course: Practice Overview
courses.description: Course is a brief overview of direct and macro practice social work. First half will focus on fundamentals of direct practice with individuals, families and groups and review assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning and intervention selection. Second half will review the fundamentals of macro social work practice. Including exposure to methods that groups, organizations and communities utilize to assess communities and address needs of individuals and families, and the impact of interagency functioning on service delivery.

courses.title: Population Health: Interprofessional Management in a Changing Healthcare System
courses.description: This interprofessional education course focuses on preparing healthcare professionals with the foundational skills needed to work in teams to effectively collaborate and coordinate care in population health. Admission to the School of Nursing graduate program or graduate students in any of the Health Affairs Schools with permission of instructor required.

courses.title: Program Development and Proposal Preparation
courses.description: In this skills-oriented course, students will learn to apply three approaches to program development and prepare a proposal draft suitable for submission to a foundation or governmental organization.

courses.title: Asset Development Practice
courses.description: This course explores community-based efforts and social policies to help lower-income individuals and families build wealth through increased access to financial services and asset-building opportunities.

courses.title: Special Topics in Macro Practice
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Social Work Study Abroad: Global Immersion
courses.description: Examines social issues, development strategies, health problems, and delivery of social services in Ghana and the influence of world view in the conceptualization of and approaches to social problems. Students who partake in this course will gain skills and knowledge relevant to addressing real-world challenges at the direct, mezzo, and macro scopes.

courses.title: Evaluation of Social Work Interventions
courses.description: Students apply knowledge of research methods and evidence-based practice to evaluation of social work interventions, by developing and conducting a detailed evaluation of specific social work intervention.

courses.title: Social Work Specialization Practicum I
courses.description: Students learn specialization competencies and behaviors by demonstrating advanced knowledge, skills and values through direct (individuals, families, small groups) OR macro (organizations, communities) practice in an agency setting. (Field fee: $300.)

courses.title: Social Work Specialization Practicum II
courses.description: A continuation of SOWO 820, students demonstrate mastery of specialization competencies and behaviors through direct (individuals, families, small groups) or macro (organizations, communities) practice in an agency setting. (Field fee: $300.)

courses.title: Online MSW Program Specialization Practicum I
courses.description: Online MSW Students learn specialization competencies and behaviors by demonstrating advanced knowledge, skills and values through direct (individuals, families, small groups) or macro (organizations, communities) practice in an agency setting. (Field Fee: $300)

courses.title: Online MSW Program Specialization Practicum II
courses.description: A continuation of SOWO 822, students demonstrate an increased knowledge of specialization competencies and behaviors by demonstrating advanced knowledge, skills, and values through direct or macro practice in an agency. (Field Fee: $300.)

courses.title: Online MSW Program Specialization Practicum III
courses.description: A continuation of SOWO 823, students demonstrate mastery of specialization competencies and behaviors through direct or macro practice in an agency setting. (Field Fee: $300.)

courses.title: Addiction and Public Policy: Implications for Practice
courses.description: The course will examine alcohol and drug policies, particularly as they relate to the exacerbation and resolution of health and social inequities for those with substance use disorders.

courses.title: Child Welfare Policy Practice and Advocacy
courses.description: This course engages students in the process of child welfare policy practice and advocacy to formulate, analyze, implement, evaluate, and disseminate evidence-informed policies and interventions at all system levels.

courses.title: Social Work and Policy Practice: Theory, Analysis and Advocacy
courses.description: This policy practice course prepares students to become skilled in analyzing, formulating, implementing, and evaluating social welfare policies. The course equips students with the knowledge, values, and skills necessary to navigate the complex landscape of social welfare services and advocate for social change through policymaking.

courses.title: Advanced Policy Practice
courses.description: This class will explore decision-making and strategy models that will engage students in the development of practical knowledge and skills in the areas of policy analysis and advocacy.

courses.title: Poverty Policy
courses.description: Course provides students with a framework for advanced policy analysis and strategies for policy change, focusing on national and state poverty policy, focusing on legal, socio-political, and economic factors influencing financing, access, service delivery. Course explores skills and strategies for policy analysis and change.

courses.title: Health Access and Health Disparities
courses.description: Examines disparities in health outcomes as a function of access to and quality of care for persons disadvantages by income, ethnicity, sexual orientation and other factors. Critically evaluates health and social policies related to exacerbation and resolution of health inequalities.

courses.title: Disability Policy
courses.description: Using an advanced policy analysis framework, this course focuses on strategies for policy change, national and state policy, and legal and socio-political factors influencing financing, access, and service delivery.

courses.title: Policy Analysis, Development, and Change: Examining Military Families
courses.description: This course will provide students with a framework for advanced policy analysis and strategies for policy change, with a focus on military families.

courses.title: Adult Mental Health: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on mental health social work practice with adults, covering assessment and several theoretically based interventions with an emphasis on gaining practice skills.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SOWO 500, 505, and 540; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740 or SOWO 770.

courses.title: Child and Adolescent Mental Health: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course presents knowledge and practice theories to understand mental health and well-being in children, adolescents and their families. It emphasizes practice skills and theories relevant to assessment and evidenced-based interventions.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SOWO 500, 505, and 540; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740 or SOWO 770.

courses.title: Families: Theory and Practice
courses.description: A review and synthesis of explanatory and practice theories for understanding and intervening with family systems.

courses.title: Older Adults: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course fosters understanding of normal aging, illness, and common challenges associated with aging, and also practice skills to treat older adults and their families.

courses.title: Health: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on social work practice in healthcare covering the social context of health problems, and the theories and interventions that facilitate prevention of and coping with health problems.

courses.title: School Social Work Practice
courses.description: This course examines public school social work policy and practice emphasizing an ecological approach within the school-family-community context.

courses.title: Core Components and Skills for Trauma-informed Practice
courses.description: This course facilitates students' acquisition of the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to effectively use 12 common trauma-informed practice elements in interventions for and the treatment of traumatized children and their families. The course highlights consideration of the impact of trauma, intervention objectives, and the practice elements needed to accomplish the intervention objectives. This course is taught using an inquiry-based learning (IBL) pedagogy to enhance students' engagement and learning using full-length cases that exemplify the diverse clients a clinician might encounter in practice.

courses.title: Approaches to Brief Treatment
courses.description: This advanced practice elective course covers theories and application of three models of brief psychotherapy. Skill building, critical thinking, and utilization of empirical support are emphasized.

courses.title: Treatment of Trauma and Violence
courses.description: This course focuses on the assessment and treatment of trauma and the impact of violence within the biopsychosocial context. You will learn foundation skills for intervening in direct practice settings with diverse client populations.

courses.title: Care of the Dying and Bereaved
courses.description: This interdisciplinary clinical course addresses issues and practice models relating to terminal illness and bereavement faced throughout the life span.

courses.title: Community Organizing
courses.description: This comprehensive course explores the fundamentals and advanced strategies of community organizing, blending theoretical knowledge with practical application. Students will learn to analyze power dynamics and engage in effective community-led public action. The curriculum covers relational power, strategic planning, policy advocacy, and ethical considerations, preparing students with skills to engage in sustained grassroots change.

courses.title: Child Welfare Perspectives and Practices
courses.description: Focus on the knowledge, skills, and critical thinking necessary for effective practice in child welfare. Students examine their own perspectives regarding pertinent research, current events, and initiatives in the state.

courses.title: Cognitive Behavior Therapy and Dialectical Behavior Therapy: Essential Practices
courses.description: This course offers an introductory exploration of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), delving into their theoretical foundations and practical implementation within each model.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SOWO 540; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740.

courses.title: Administrative and Management: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course explores contemporary theories, models, and practices for managing human service organizations, emphasizing skills in human resources, leadership, fund management, program implementation, partnerships, equity, organizational change, stakeholder engagement and cultural humility.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SOWO 500, 505, and 570; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740 or SOWO 770.

courses.title: Interorganizational and Community-Level Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on social planning, intervention design, and implementation within a complex inter-organizational environment. Theoretical frameworks and historical, sociopolitical and economic contexts of human service delivery systems are discussed.

courses.title: Sustainable Development
courses.description: Examines perspectives and models of sustainable development. Students will analyze a project and present a participatory plan for engaging in sustainable development work.

courses.title: Development Theory and Practice in Global Settings
courses.description: This course is designed to assist students to learn skills, methods, theory, and research in development practice in global settings. Focus is on competent practice with marginalized populations globally.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SOWO 500, 505, and 570; Pre- or corequisite, SOWO 740 or 770.

courses.title: Marketing and Fundraising for Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: This course helps students to develop skills and practices associated with marketing and fundraising strategies for nonprofit organizations at the macro level.

courses.title: Leadership in Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of the executive role in nonprofit organizations, particularly in leadership transitions, strategic planning, board development, policy administration, governance, employee relations, and resource planning and acquisition.

courses.title: Financial Management of Nonprofit Organizations
courses.description: Provides basic financial skills for leaders of nonprofits, including bookkeeping fundamentals, interpreting financial statements, budgeting, cash management and investment, and legal compliance.

courses.title: Program Design and Proposal Development and Pre-implementation Planning
courses.description: Students will learn to develop proposals to fund programs and interventions that address an organizational or social problem or condition and build skills in problem theory, program theory, proposal development, and pre-implementation assessment and planning.

courses.title: Conceptualizing Social Problems to Inform Interventions
courses.description: An application and critical analysis of behavioral and social science theories and theory- driven research for understanding the etiology of social problems for purposes of social intervention.

courses.title: Research Methods in Social Intervention
courses.description: An introduction to the basic principles of research for planning and evaluating social interventions. Topics include problem formulation, design, measurement, analysis, and the application of findings to theory and practice.

courses.title: Introduction to Social Statistics and Data Analysis
courses.description: Designed to explore basic principles and to provide advanced instruction in data analysis, including the construction and analysis of tables, statistical tests, and an introduction to the use of computer programs.

courses.title: Research Practicum I
courses.description: Students develop independent research competence through work on a research project under the direction of an experienced researcher.

courses.title: Advanced Research Methods in Social Intervention
courses.description: Students build advanced competence in research design, data collection, data analysis, and statistics by analyzing exemplary social work research and presenting independent learning projects within specialized areas of study.

courses.title: Measurement in Intervention Research
courses.description: This course focuses on the development of knowledge and skills in measuring social, psychological, environmental, and other factors related to intervention with individuals, families, groups, and organizations.

courses.title: Research Practicum II
courses.description: Continuation of Research Practicum I.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Structural Equation Modeling
courses.description: SEM is a general statistical method that can be employed to test theoretically derived models. In this course, students will learn fundamental concepts and skills to conduct SEM, and how to apply these techniques to social work and related areas of research.

courses.title: Longitudinal and Multilevel Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces the context and intuition for longitudinal and multilevel models, and the statistical frameworks, analytical tools, and social behavioral applications of multilevel modeling (MLM) and longitudinal analysis.

courses.title: Applied Regression Analysis and Generalized Linear Models
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course introduces statistical frameworks, analytical tools, and social behavioral applications of OLS regression model, weighted least-square regression, logistic regression models, and generalized linear models.

courses.title: Special Topics in Doctoral Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Special Topics in Social Work Doctoral Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topic determined by the instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Qualitative Analysis
courses.description: This course will introduce the application of qualitative research methods for social work research.

courses.title: Causal Inference for Social Work Research
courses.description: This course focuses on topics and methods for causal inference in social work research.

courses.title: Systemic Reviews and Introduction to Meta-Analysis
courses.description: This course focuses on conducing and writing systematic reviews in social work and related behavioral/social sciences, as well as an introduction to meta-analysis.

courses.title: Professional Development Seminar: Navigating Doctoral Studies and Beyond
courses.description: This seminar-style course seeks to bolster the explicit and implicit curriculum of preparing social work scholars. The course focuses on preparing students for a successful doctoral education experience and individual development of their scholarly identities. The course will also introduce students to specialized knowledge and skills that will allow them to develop and implement a program of research in their future careers. This course is required for first year doctoral students in the School of Social Work. Other doctoral students are welcome to attend sessions of interest with permission from the instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Development of Social Intervention Models
courses.description: This PhD-level course focuses on preparing advanced graduate students with the knowledge and skills needed to design and develop interventions that address social needs, problems, and conditions.

courses.title: Teaching Practicum
courses.description: This practicum provides a range of supervised classroom or training opportunities designed to prepare advanced doctoral students for faculty positions in undergraduate- and graduate-level social work education.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.description: Dissertation work.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Elementary Spanish Review
courses.description: Online course that includes essentials of elementary Spanish. Designed for students with previous study who place into first-semester Spanish. Upon successful completion students will enroll in SPAN 102. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 100 and SPAN 101, 111, or 401.

courses.title: Elementary Spanish I
courses.description: Introduces the essential elements of Spanish structure and vocabulary and cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing are stressed. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 101 and SPAN 100, 111, or 401. Note that SPAN 101 is only offered during the fall and summer terms; it is not offered in the spring.

courses.title: Elementary Spanish II
courses.description: Continues the study of the essential elements of Spanish structure, vocabulary, and the cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 102 and SPAN 105, 111, 401, or 404. Honors version available.

courses.title: Spanish for High Beginners
courses.description: Accelerated course that covers SPAN 101 and 102 for students with previous study of Spanish. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 105 and SPAN 102, 111, 401, or 404.

courses.title: Modified Intensive Elementary Spanish I and II
courses.description: Students must meet eligibility criteria. Class meets five days per week (MTWRF) for a total of six hours of instruction. Alternative teaching and learning strategies used to provide in-depth coverage of the material of the SPAN 101 and 102 sequence in a single semester. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 111 and SPAN 100, 101, 102, 105, or 401. Permission of the instructor required.

courses.title: Reading América Now. Fourteen Spanish American Prose Fictions Written While You've Been Around
courses.description: This course studies trends in thought and social practices in the Spanish speaking Americas through the most recent literature of the region. Topics may include colonialism, race, class, ethnicity, modernization, ecology, religion, gender, and popular culture. Texts and class are in English.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I
courses.description: Develops language skills for communication. Review of elementary Spanish. Expands awareness of the Spanish-speaking world through readings and discussion of representative texts. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 203 and SPAN 212, 402, or 405. Honors version available.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II with Creative Project
courses.description: Continued development of language skills for communication. Considers finer points of linguistic structure. Expands awareness of Spanish culture through reading, inquiry, and class discussion. The course includes a semester-long, immersive creative project. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 204 and SPAN 206, 212 or 402. Honors version available.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II for Heritage Learners
courses.description: Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 204, and 205, and SPAN 212, or 402. This course is designed for the further development of language skills of Heritage Learners for better communication at the Intermediate level. Considers finer points of linguistic structure. Expands awareness of Spanish-speaking cultures through reading, inquiry, and class discussion.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 203, or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II
courses.description: Continued development of language skills for communication. Considers finer points of linguistic structure. Expands awareness of Spanish culture through reading, inquiry, and class discussion. Awarded as transfer credit, by-exam credit, and placement credit. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 206 and SPAN 204, 212 or 402.

courses.title: Modified Intensive Intermediate Spanish I
courses.description: A continuation of SPAN 111. Class meets five days per week (MTWRF) for a total of six hours of instruction. In-depth recycling of SPAN 111 material while providing alternative teaching and learning strategies to cover the material of SPAN 203. Additional focus on modified reading and writing strategies, as well as opportunities for further cultural enrichment. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 212 and SPAN 203. Permission of the instructor required.

courses.title: Conversation I
courses.description: Introductory conversation. Builds oral proficiency and awareness of Hispanic culture. Emphasizes vocabulary and grammatical accuracy; writing activities support speaking. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 255 and SPAN 266. Not open to native speakers. Honors version available.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish in Context
courses.description: Fifth semester Spanish course required for all majors and minors that uses literature, film, and culture as a basis for reviewing grammatical concepts, developing writing competency, and improving overall communication skills. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 261 and SPAN 267. Honors version available.

courses.title: Spanish Conversation for Heritage Learners
courses.description: Spanish conversation for native speakers. Develops vocabulary and standard grammar skills, supports research in the history and lives of Hispanics in the United States. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 266 and SPAN 255.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish in Context for Heritage Learners
courses.description: Fifth semester Spanish course, designed specifically for Heritage learners, required for all majors and minors. Uses literature, film, and culture as a basis for reviewing grammatical concepts, developing writing competency, and improving overall communication skills. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 267 and SPAN 261.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 204 or SPAN 205; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Contemporary Spanish American Prose Fiction in Translation
courses.description: Narrative works of Borges, Cortázar, García Márquez, and other contemporary Spanish American writers.

courses.title: Masterpieces of Spanish Literature in Translation
courses.description: Representative Spanish authors from the Middle Ages to the present.

courses.title: Cervantes in English Translation
courses.description: Study and discussion of Don Quijote with consideration of the Exemplary Novels and the background of Renaissance prose.

courses.title: Approaches to Spanish Language Teaching
courses.description: Permission of the program director based on oral proficiency interview. Students must have advanced proficiency in Spanish. Students learn and implement fundamentals of foreign language instruction as peer tutors for elementary Spanish courses. Students may take course twice for credit. May not count toward the major or minor in Spanish.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Course Correspondent Project in Spanish
courses.description: Learning contract required. Students participating in UNC-led study abroad programs develop activities to supplement instruction in on-campus courses. Supervised by the on-campus instructor, students file reports on the sites, language, and culture of the country in which they are studying. Pass/Fail only. Permission of the instructor and the instructor's department.

courses.title: Grammar and Structure of Spanish
courses.description: Advanced grammar designed to improve grammatical analysis, accuracy, and develop writing skills, using process and task-oriented approaches. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 261 or SPAN 267; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Introduction to Literary and Cultural Analysis
courses.description: Prepares students to formulate and communicate critical analyses of literary works in at least three genres chosen from theater, poetry, essay, narrative, and film while situating the readings within a cultural context. Students will improve Spanish language proficiency and appreciation of different world views through literature and culture. Previously offered as SPAN 260. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 301 and SPAN 260 or 302. Honors version available.

courses.title: Literary and Cultural Analysis for Heritage Learners
courses.description: Designed for heritage learners, prepares students to formulate and communicate critical analyses of literary works in at least three genres chosen from theater, poetry, essay, narrative, and film while situating the readings within a cultural context. Students will gain appreciation of different world views through literature and culture. Previously offered as SPAN 262; students may not receive credit for SPAN 302 and 260 or 301.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 261 or 267; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: LAC Recitation
courses.description: A recitation or stand-alone section for LAC courses. May not count toward the major or minor in Spanish. Co-registration required unless a stand-alone LAC course. Contact instructor or view Notes to determine.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 204; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Spanish for Business (First Semester)
courses.description: All-skills course with review of grammar and extensive writing and speaking practice. Vocabulary, readings, and activities geared toward the language of business professions in the context of the United States Hispanic community. Students may receive credit for only one of SPAN 320, 321, or 323.

courses.title: Spanish for the Medical Professions (First Semester)
courses.description: All-skills course with review of grammar, extensive writing and speaking practice. Vocabulary, readings, and activities geared toward the language of health care professions in the context of the United States Hispanic community. Students may receive credit for only one of SPAN 320, 321, or 323. Open only to students in the minor in Spanish for the professions.

courses.title: Spanish for the Legal Professions (First Semester)
courses.description: All-skills course with review of grammar and extensive writing and speaking. Vocabulary, readings, and activities geared toward the language of legal professions within the context of the Hispanic community.Students may receive credit for only one of SPAN 320, 321, or 323. Open only to students in the minor in Spanish for the professions.

courses.title: Spanish for the Legal Professions (Second Semester)
courses.description: Second semester, all-skills course with extensive writing and speaking practice, and grammar review. Vocabulary, readings, and activities geared toward the language of law professions in the context of the United States Hispanic community.

courses.title: Spanish for Business (Second Semester)
courses.description: Second semester, all-skills course with extensive writing and speaking practice, including grammar review. Vocabulary, readings, and activities geared toward the language of business professions in the context of the United States Hispanic community.

courses.title: Spanish for the Medical Professions (Second Semester)
courses.description: Second semester, all-skills course with extensive writing and speaking practice, including grammar review. Vocabulary, readings, and activities geared toward the language of health care professions in the context of the United States Hispanic community.

courses.title: Spanish for Professional and Community Engagement
courses.description: Eighth-semester capstone course applying skills in Spanish language and cultures to professional and community contexts. Assignments include writing and reviewing professional documents and a research project. Students may undertake a community service project in conjunction with this course, registering for ROML 194 as well, which satisfies HI-SERVICE. Open only to students in the minor in Spanish for the professions.

courses.title: Spanish for Mental Health Professionals
courses.description: This course is designed for students completing the Spanish Minor in the Medical Professions Track. It will focus on mental health, including how mental health well-being has been affected by contemporary events (COVID-19, social media, etc.). Topics include eating disorders, addiction, and domestic violence. Students will learn about these topics and how to discuss them with Spanish-speaking clients and patients.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 261; Pre- or corequisite, SPAN 321.

courses.title: Trans-Atlantic Cultural Topics
courses.description: Cultural history of Spain and Spanish America from the 16th century to the 21st century. Explores trans-Atlantic dimensions of Spanish and Spanish American cultures and the elements that have shaped those societies and their cultural traditions during the periods studied. Formerly offered as SPAN 331.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Podcasting: New Narratives of the Hispanic World
courses.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of the most influential non-fiction narrative podcasts produced in Latin America and Spain. Through these audio narratives, students engage with the cultural, historical, and societal landscapes of the Hispanic world. They learn the language of podcasting, master narrative structures, and understand the production process. They also conceptualize and produce their own narrative podcast episodes, using audio storytelling as a medium to share meaningful perspectives on Hispanic experiences, particularly within the context of the United States.

courses.title: Topics in the Cultural History of Iberia
courses.description: This course studies trends in thought, art, film, music, and social practices in the Iberian context, and includes the study of Spain's historical nationalities. Topics may include nationalism, ethnicity, race, class, gender, migration, and popular culture.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Latin American Cultural Topics
courses.description: This course studies trends in thought, art, film, music, social practices, in the Spanish speaking Americas, including the United States. Topics may include colonialism, race, class, ethnicity, modernization, ecology, religion, gender, and popular culture.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Latin American Maternal Health: Theory, Culture, and Practice
courses.description: This course explores Latin American maternal health through the lenses of theory, culture, and practice, emphasizing how beliefs and social norms shape experiences of pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum care. Focusing on cultural variability and its impact on healthcare, the course is especially relevant to North Carolina, where the Latin American population has grown significantly. Students engage with texts, films, legal documents, and guest lectures to examine how maternal health is influenced by cultural and structural factors. By connecting global issues to local realities, the course equips students to critically analyze the social, political, and ethical dimensions of maternal care.

courses.title: Spanish Interpretation I
courses.description: Introduces the profession of interpreter: main interpretation models, history and theory, use of cognitive processes in developing skills, ethical standards, and best practices. Emphasis on expanding communicative and cultural competency while applying strategies in business, conference interpretation, education, health care, law, and law enforcement.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SPAN 261 or 267, and SPAN 300 or 301 or 302.

courses.title: Spanish Interpretation II
