courses.description: Refines interpretation skills through continued study of theory and best practices in varied professional contexts. Focuses on enhancing linguistic competence, sight-translation, and mnemonic strategies. Increases cultural sensitivity to issues interpreters face in business, conference interpretation, education, health care, the hospitality industry, law, and social services.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish Oral Communication
courses.description: SPAN 355 is an advanced conversation course for students of Spanish. Through different communicative and interactive activities, students will build oral fluency and develop effective communication skills while discussing topics of interest and debate in the contemporary Hispanic world. The class will explore different modes and strategies for successful interactions with Spanish speakers in a variety of contexts: professional, personal, and public.

courses.title: Introduction to Hispanic Linguistics
courses.description: Introduction to the linguistic study of sound, meaning, grammatical form, dialectal and sociolinguistic variation, with a particular focus on modern Spanish and the languages of Spain and Latin America. Previously offered as SPAN/LING 377.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 300 or SPAN 301; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Hispanic Film
courses.description: Study of contemporary cultural, historical, and aesthetic issues through narrative film, documentary, and other media from Latin America and Spain.

courses.title: Experiences of Disease and Health through Hispanic Literature and Culture
courses.description: This courseseeks new perspectives on disease, literature, and culture in the Hispanic milieu. We will examine texts that present disease as theme, as aesthetic approach, as self-representation, or as metaphor in the Spanish-speaking world.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 301 or 302; or permission from the instructor.

courses.title: Multiethnic Cultures of Contemporary Spain
courses.description: This course examines multiethnic cultural production from Spain since 1975. Considers the histories and literatures of religious, ethnic, and racial minorities including but not limited to Jewish, Moroccan, Afro-descendent, and East Asian identities.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 301 or 302, or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Introduction to Translation
courses.description: Theory and practice of translation through a dual approach of conceptual readings and classroom discussion and workshops in interdisciplinary fields. Emphasizes cultural role of the translator as mediator.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SPAN 261 or 267, and 300 or SPAN 301 or SPAN 302.

courses.title: Spanish Translation II
courses.description: This course introduces students to literary translation: close reading and creative re-writing. Students work with memoir/essay, poetry/songs, theater/film, science-fiction, la novela rosa, true crime, graphic novels and comics, young adult, and children's literature by a diverse representation of artists. They learn marketplace skills: how to contact authors and assemble a submission ''package'' for publication. They also practice solving unique problems in determining priorities and compensating for translation loss, transferring figurative speech, cultural practices, and regionalisms.

courses.title: Studies in Spanish Literature
courses.description: Study of the literatures of Spain centering on representative authors and texts from various literary movements, situated within their sociohistorical contexts.

courses.title: Studies in Latin American Literature
courses.description: The literature of Spanish America from pre-Colombian times to the present. Representative authors and texts from various literary movements will be studied in their sociohistorical contexts.

courses.title: Spanish of the United States
courses.description: Study of the Spanish found today in the United States, its history and characteristics, and the socioeconomic repercussions of its presence in contact with English.

courses.title: Spanish Phonetics and Phonology
courses.description: Introduction to the description of sound systems with a focus on Spanish. Includes the study of the historical development of Spanish and its areal and social variation in Spain, Latin America, and the United States.

courses.title: Afro-Hispanic Language Contacts
courses.description: Introduction to the study of Spanish in contact with African languages in the Iberian Peninsula and Latin America since the beginning of the slave trade. Linguistic analysis of literary texts from a variety of eras will assess how contact with the African diaspora has had a permanent impact on contemporary Spanish.

courses.title: Aesthetics of Violence in Latina/o American Fiction
courses.description: The course explores the aesthetics of violence in contemporary Latina/o American fiction, paying attention to historical memory, rewritings of history, and the formation of otherness and marginality. Selections from Junot Díaz, Graciela Limón, Daniel Alarcón, Santiago Roncagliolo, Horacio Castellanos Moya, Roberto Bolaño, and Orfa Alarcón, among others.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SPAN 301 or 302, and SPAN 371 or 373.

courses.title: Studies in Spanish Drama
courses.description: Spanish-language theater. Specific topics to be announced in advance by the instructor.

courses.title: Studies in Spanish and Spanish American Poetry
courses.description: Specific topics to be announced in advance by the instructor.

courses.title: Studies in Spanish Prose
courses.description: Selected works of prose from the Spanish canon organized by topic or theme.

courses.title: Medieval Spanish Literature
courses.description: A survey of lyric poetry, drama, prose, and genres peculiar to the literature before 1500.

courses.title: Spanish Renaissance
courses.description: A survey of poetry, drama, and prose of the 16th century.

courses.title: Contemporary Spanish American Prose Fiction
courses.description: A study of the cultural, political, and aesthetic dimensions of the novels and short stories of selected contemporary Spanish American writers such as Borges, Cortázar, García Márquez, Puig, etc.

courses.title: Literature and Politics in Central America
courses.description: The course will explore the most prominent authors of Central America (Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and the United States) since the 1950s. Critical analysis of their poetry, short stories, novels, testimonial narratives, and films.

courses.title: Eroticism in Contemporary Latin American Literature
courses.description: Literary manifestations of love, sexuality, and eroticism as social and political metaphors of contemporary Latin America. Selections from Sor Juana, Agustini, Darío, López Velarde, and Neruda with more emphasis on 20th-century works by writers like Donoso, Vargas Llosa, García Márquez, Poniatowska, Rivera Garza, and Montero.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SPAN 301 or 302, and SPAN 371 or 373.

courses.title: Narratives of the Mexican Revolution
courses.description: Analysis of historical and literary writing, cinematic productions, and popular corridos produced in response to the Mexican Revolution. In addition to exposure to significant milestones in the development of Mexican literature, students will strengthen their Spanish reading ability and sharpen critical skills.

courses.title: International Internship in Seville
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare students for an increasingly interconnected global labor market. Students will learn how to observe, interact with co-workers, recognize cultural differences, compare teamwork and interpersonal interactions in different cultures, apply academic knowledge in a professional setting, identify opportunities to create value within the school/healthcare company/business, and to research, propose and present their report at the end of the semester.

courses.title: Creative Writing in Spanish
courses.description: This fiction workshop allows students to engage in individual and collaborative creative expression, exploration, and production. Throughout the semester, students analyze literary works to acquire the necessary tools to create their own short stories in Spanish, while mastering certain techniques and methods related to fiction. The course also integrates cultural events outside of the classroom such as guest lectures, book presentations, or literary workshops as part of class participation.

courses.title: Research for Advanced Students
courses.description: Required preparation, two major-level courses or permission of the instructor. Research project for advanced students on a topic agreed upon by the student and faculty member.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Language and Linguistics
courses.description: Seminar on a previously announced topic.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Literature and Culture
courses.description: Variable topics seminar.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SPAN 371 and 373; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Special Topics in Spanish, FC-AESTH
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary by each semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Beginning Accelerated Spanish
courses.description: Covers levels one and two of the basic language sequence in one semester. Designed for highly motivated undergraduate/graduate language learners, especially those who have experienced success with learning another language. Intensive approach to developing all skills but with an emphasis on speaking. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 401 and SPAN 101, 102, 105 or 111.

courses.title: Intermediate Accelerated Spanish
courses.description: A continuation of SPAN 401, covers levels three and four in one semester. Develops all skills, with increasing emphasis on reading, writing, and cultural analysis. Designed for highly motivated undergraduate/graduate language learners, especially those who have experienced success with learning another language. Prepares students for advanced courses. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 402 and SPAN 203, SPAN 204 or SPAN 212.

courses.title: Elementary Spanish for Health Professionals
courses.description: Distance course requiring access to the Internet. Focuses on communication within the context of Latino/a immigrant culture in health care settings. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 404 and SPAN 102 or 105.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish for Health Care Professionals
courses.description: Distance course requiring access to the Internet. Focuses on improving communication within the context of Latino/a immigrant culture in health care settings. This course is equivalent to SPAN 203 (Intermediate Spanish I) and therefore fulfills the foreign language requirement. Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 405 and SPAN 203.

courses.title: Languages of Spain I
courses.description: Study of the language and culture of one of the languages of Spain other than Spanish. Selection will vary according to term: Catalan, Euskera (Basque), Galician.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Languages of Spain II
courses.description: Continuation of the study of the language and culture of one of the languages of Spain other than Spanish. Selection will vary according to term: Catalan, Euskera, Galician.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Languages of the Americas I
courses.description: Study of the language and culture of one of the languages of Spanish America other than Spanish. Selection will vary according to term: Mayan, Nahuatl, Quechua, Guarani.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Languages of the Americas II
courses.description: Continuation of the study of the language and culture of one of the languages of Spanish America other than Spanish. Selection will vary according to term: Mayan, Nahuatl, Quechua, Guarani.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Hispanic Linguistics
courses.description: Seminar on a previously announced topic. For graduate and advanced undergraduate students.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Spanish for Reading
courses.description: For students with no background in Spanish or those needing a review of grammatical structures and vocabulary in preparation for the reading knowledge exam for graduate students (FLPA).

courses.title: Colonial and 19th-Century Spanish American Literature
courses.description: Advanced survey of literary works from 16th- through 19th-century Spanish America, with emphasis on their rhetorical foundations and historical, political, and aesthetic connections.

courses.title: Modernist and Contemporary Spanish American Literature
courses.description: Advanced survey of Spanish American works from the 1880s through the present, with emphasis on their rhetorical foundations and historical, cultural, political, and aesthetic connections.

courses.title: Cervantes and the Quijote
courses.description: Close reading of Cervantes' Quijote and selected Novelas ejemplares, with consideration of the background of Renaissance prose (romance of chivalry, pastoral, and sentimental novel) in relation to 16th-century historiography.

courses.title: Women in Hispanic Literature
courses.description: The image of woman in 16th- and 17th-century Hispanic literature. A study of texts by Spanish and Spanish American authors. Readings in Spanish or in English translation. Lectures in English.

courses.title: Literary and Cultural History of the Spanish Language
courses.description: A historical study of the cultural and societal factors that influence the evolution of the Spanish language and its literature, from its first written documents in the ninth century to literatures written in Spanglish today.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 300; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Indigenous Literatures and Cultures of the Américas
courses.description: Panoramic view of indigenous literatures in the Américas through a study of a variety of indigenous textual production including chronicles, manifestos, novels, testimonial narratives, short stories, poetry, artistic production, and film.

courses.title: Literature and the Visual Arts in Spain
courses.description: Study of the literature of the Iberian Peninsula and developments in the visual arts from the Middle Ages to the early 20th century.

courses.title: Iberian Literary and Cultural Studies
courses.description: Advanced study of Iberian literary and cultural history from the Middle Ages to the present. Emphasis on situating cultural production in historical, political, and aesthetic contexts. Specific topic and time period studied will vary by instructor.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 371 or 373; permission from the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite; or graduate standing.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Topics in Hispanic Jewish Studies
courses.description: This seminar examines selected topics in modern Hispanic Jewish culture, focusing on literature and film. Possible thematic approaches include identity, diaspora, migration, memory, statehood, life writing, and interreligious relations.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, SPAN 371 and 373; permission from the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: The Spanish Comedia of the Golden Age
courses.description: A comprehensive study of the Golden Age Spanish theater from its Renaissance beginnings through the 17th century.

courses.title: Film Studies: Iberia and the Americas
courses.description: Advanced study of the history and theory of film produced in the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking worlds for beginning graduate students and advanced undergraduates. Readings in film history and theory will build students' knowledge in cultural, political, and aesthetic issues. Class discussions emphasize critical and analytical thought.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 361; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Advanced Spanish Phonology
courses.description: Topics in Spanish phonology from a range of theoretical perspectives. Autosegmental theory, optimality theory (OT), syllable structure, stress and accent, and the interaction of phonology and morphology.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 376; OR graduate standing; OR permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Spanish Syntax
courses.description: Why do we say in Spanish "me gusta" ("to me pleases") for "I like it"? Syntax studies how words associate in larger structures. This class provides the tools to understand the forms of different varieties of Spanish.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 360; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: History of the Spanish Language
courses.description: SPAN 376 desirable. A theoretical study of the evolution of Spanish from classical and spoken Latin, focusing on phonological, morphological, and syntactic phenomena. Intended for linguistics majors.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 360; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Spanish Pragmatics
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the study of meaning and language use, with a focus on Spanish. Includes discussion of the classical texts in the field as well as analysis of a variety of data (corpora, fieldwork, and experimental materials).

courses.title: First- and Second-Language Acquisition of Spanish
courses.description: Why and how do children learn language so easily, and why is it so difficult for adults to learn a second language? This course examines these and related questions in the light of current theories of first and second language acquisition, with a focus on Spanish.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 360; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Spanish Semantics
courses.description: This course is an upper undergraduate/graduate-level introduction to the study of the meaning of words and sentences, with a focus on Spanish. It covers the following topics: truth-conditional theories of meaning, modality, quantification, reference, tense and aspect, Aktionsart. The course also addresses cross-linguistic data collection, e.g., field work and experimental methods.

courses.title: Spanish Sociolinguistics
courses.description: Interdisciplinary approach to studying the Spanish language as a social and cultural phenomenon. Explores the relationship between language and culture, communicative competence and pragmatics, social and linguistic factors in language variation and change, attitudes toward language and language choice, linguistic prejudice and language myths, and language and identity.

courses.title: Guaraní Linguistics
courses.description: Guaraní, an official language of Paraguay, is the only indigenous language in the Americas (and possibly in the world) that is spoken natively by a nonindigenous majority. This seminar explores the linguistics of Guaraní: its typology, history, grammar, and sociolinguistics.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 360; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Spanish Dialectology and Variation
courses.description: Linguistic analysis of variation within the Spanish-speaking world. Special attention paid to contact situations between Spanish and other languages.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPAN 360; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: Required of students reading for honors. Preparation of an essay under the direction of a faculty member. Topic to be approved by thesis director in consultation with honors advisor.

courses.title: Honors Thesis in Spanish
courses.description: Restricted to senior honors candidates. Second semester of senior honors thesis. Thesis preparation under the direction of a departmental faculty member.

courses.title: Beginnings of Castilian Hegemony to 1369
courses.description: Early medieval romance period (11th century to 1369). The establishment of Castilian hegemony studied through a variety of texts (chronicles, miracles, collections of law and exempla, fueros, epic and lyric poems).

courses.title: The Trastamara Dynasty: 1369 to 1504/1516
courses.description: The final shaping of Castile, the beginning of nationhood, and American expansion studied through a variety of texts (chronicles, books of chivalry, lyric and narrative poems, sentimental novels, and travel narratives).

courses.title: Nonfiction Prose of the 16th and 17th Centuries
courses.description: An examination of the histories, chronicles, and other documents written in Spain and Spanish American, with special emphasis on the literature of exploration.

courses.title: 19th-Century Spanish Novel
courses.description: A study of the development of romanticism, costumbrismo, realism, and naturalism, principally through the novels of Gil y Carrasco, Pereda, Valera, Pérez Galdós, Pardo Bazán, Clarín, and Blasco Ibañez. .

courses.title: The Modern Spanish Novel
courses.description: Trends in modern Spanish narrative fiction from 1898 to 1975. Modernism, Civil War, and dictatorship.

courses.title: The Contemporary Spanish Novel
courses.description: Trends in contemporary Spanish narrative from 1975 to the present. Post-totalitarian fiction, postmodernism, and minority literatures.

courses.title: War, History, and Society in Iberian Narrative and Film
courses.description: Focuses on the narrative production of Iberian literature in Castilian, Catalan, Basque, and Galician since 1936, with their corresponding film adaptations when available. Begins with the end of the Spanish Civil War, continuing with the years of the Francoist dictatorship and the transition to democracy, and concludes with Spain today.

courses.title: Golden Age Poetry
courses.description: Selected poetic works from Garcilaso through Quevedo.

courses.title: Modern and Contemporary Spanish Poetry
courses.description: Study of Spanish poetry from the 19th to the 21st centuries in terms of aesthetics and literary movements including romanticism, modernism, and postmodernism.

courses.title: Contemporary Lyric Poetry
courses.description: Major poets from the Generation of 1927 to the present.

courses.title: Golden Age Prose
courses.description: The major prose works of the Golden Age, excluding those of Cervantes.

courses.title: Topics in Contemporary Literary and Cultural Theory
courses.description: Study of major topics in modern theory such as identities, time, space, history, nation, language, text, and image, from modernity to post-modernity and beyond.

courses.title: Topics in the Intellectual History of Spain
courses.description: Historical concepts such as power, ideology, class, culture, identity, attitude, race, perception, and methods as they developed among elite and nonelite groups of the 16th and 17th century Spanish society. Focuses on evolution of ideas, sciences, arts, techniques, and cultural expression of social movements - nationalism, colonialism, racism - and historical reflection.

courses.title: The Essay and Short Story
courses.description: Theory and practice of the essay and short story. Topics include masters of the Spanish American and international essay and short story, the evolution of both genres, gender, cultural studies.

courses.title: Poiesis in Spanish America
courses.description: Theories and practices of literary creation across genres and periods.

courses.title: Topics in Spanish American Performance Studies
courses.description: A thorough grounding in contemporary plays in the Spanish-speaking Americas. Topics include performing class, ethnicity, and gender; parody; staging nations; politics of metatheatre; postmodern agency; and the performance of everyday life.

courses.title: The Aesthetics of the Baroque in Spanish American Literature
courses.description: The origin, development, and persistence of a baroque aesthetic in Spanish American literature through an examination of diverse theories of baroque and close readings of representative texts.

courses.title: The Vanguards
courses.description: The theory and practice of innovative writing, especially since the 19th century. Topics include the historical Spanish American and Anglo-European vanguards, experimental literature, modernismo's literary rebellion, gender, and cultural studies.

courses.title: The Novel in Spanish America
courses.description: The novel to 1960. The course examines romanticism, realism, naturalism, modernism, and the new national literatures through such authors as Avellaneda, Blest Gana, Silva, Asturias, Carpentier, Rulfo, Bombal, and Vargas Llosa.

courses.title: The Contemporary Spanish American Novel
courses.description: The theory and practice of the novel since the 1960s. Topics include the Spanish American "Boom" of the 60s and 70s, major international trends and writers, gender, cultural studies.

courses.title: Enlightenment and Romanticism in Spain
courses.description: Readings from 18th and 19th-century Spanish authors in various genres.

courses.title: Seminar in Peninsular Spanish Literature and Culture
courses.description: Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Seminar in Spanish American Literature
courses.description: Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Seminar Spanish/Spanish American Transatlantic Topics
courses.description: Topic determined by instructor and announced in advance.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Special Readings
courses.description: Doctoral students only.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with the instructor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: C-Start
courses.description: A one-credit hour seminar designed and taught by students under the guidance of a faculty mentor. Pass/fail only.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Undergraduate Internships
courses.description: Undergraduate internships available through University Career Services with the approval of the Office of Undergraduate Curricula. For students whose employers require them to receive academic credit for their internship. Arrangements must be made in advance of beginning the internship. Credit does not count toward graduation.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 8 total credits. 8 total completions.
courses.gradingStatus: Pass/Fail; credit hours may not be used toward degree.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Public health topics will vary with the instructor and semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: This introductory course will describe the history of public health, the key terms and concepts, and how the core areas of public health are integrated to promote health at a population level. The class will engage the students in active learning through the use of media, innovative technology, discussion groups, and field experiences.

courses.title: Foundations of Public Health
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce you to public health and help you develop the knowledge and skills necessary to identify and describe public health problems. Restricted to matriculated BSPH majors in BIOS, CGPH, HPM, EHS, and NUTR.

courses.title: Public Health Systems and Solutions
courses.description: The course is designed to help you understand and analyze complex health systems and develop the knowledge and skills necessary to develop, implement, and evaluate solutions to public health problems. Restricted to matriculated BSPH majors in BIOS, CGPH, HPM, EHS, and NUTR.

courses.title: Public Health Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Basic concept underlying commercial and social entrepreneurship applied to public health, including guest lectures by individuals with proven success in these areas. Honors version available.

courses.title: Global Social Entrepreneurship in Public Health
courses.description: This study abroad course will introduce students to basic concepts and case studies of commercial and social entrepreneurship as applied to the pursuit of public health through both for-profit and non-profit entities. This course features guest speakers with successful experience in public health entrepreneurship in diverse arenas as well as those who have experienced challenges or venture failures. Honors version available.

courses.title: Foundations of Public Health
courses.description: By applying crosscutting themes of health equity, history, community engagement and the Gillings's mantra of "Global is Local. Local is Global," students develop foundational knowledge of how public health has evolved, its frameworks, the determinants of health and health disparities through research and practice applications. With this knowledge, students work individually and in teams to apply their learning to a public health problem and propose innovative solutions.

courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Topic will vary with the instructor and semester.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.title: Leading from the Inside-Out
courses.description: This course prepares students for public health practice by introducing fundamental leadership skills necessary to advance health equity and recognize and address challenges in organizational settings. Restricted to MPH students only.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisites, SPHG 711, SPHG 712, SPHG 713, SPHG 721, and SPHG 722.

courses.title: Practicum Assignments & Interprofessional Practice Activities
courses.description: This course awards credit to required practicum assignments and includes a series of interprofessional practice activities designed to provide healthcare professionals with the foundational skills needed to work in teams to effectively collaborate and coordinate care in population health. Restricted to MPH students only.

courses.title: MPH Pre-Practicum Assignments
courses.description: This course provides structures and supports for students as they search, select, and plan for the practicum. It awards credit to required pre-practicum assignments.
courses.requisites: Pre- or corequisite, SPHG 711, SPHG 712, SPHG 713, SPHG 701, SPHG 721, SPHG 722.

courses.title: MPH Pre and Post Practicum Assignments
courses.description: This course provides structures and supports for the practicum search, selection, planning, implementation, and evaluation process. It awards credit to practicum hours and assignments.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, PUBH 706, PUBH 746, PUBH 749, PUBH 750, PUBH 751, PUBH 760, PUBH 890, and BIOS 641.

courses.title: MPH Post-Practicum Assignments
courses.description: This course facilitates reflection on the practicum and awards credit to required post-practicum assignments.

courses.title: Data Analysis for Public Health
courses.description: This introductory course is part of the MPH core curriculum and focuses on the biostatistics and analysis methods commonly found in public health. Students will learn to produce, interpret, and use straight-forward data analyses.

courses.title: Methods and Measures for Public Health Practice
courses.description: This course is part of the MPH core curriculum, and introduces epidemiologic concepts and how to describe population patterns of health, health inequities, and their determinants.

courses.title: Systems Approaches to Understanding Public Health Issues
courses.description: This course is part of the MPH core curriculum and introduces students to systems thinking approaches to understanding the complex and interconnecting factors that underpin current public health issues.

courses.title: Public Health Solutions: Systems, Policy and Advocacy
courses.description: This course introduces students to the health systems and the US health system in particular. It provides an introduction to the role of health policy in addressing public health problems and advancing health equity, and how evidence, law and ethics play a role in policy-making. It provides students with the skills to communicate information about public health problems and solutions to various audiences and introduces them to concepts of public health advocacy.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPHG 711 or BIOS 600, SPHG 712 or EPID 600, SPHG 713.

courses.title: Developing, Implementing, and Evaluating Public Health Solutions
courses.description: Students will identify, analyze and prioritize potential public health solutions. In addition, students will learn to adapt evidence-based solutions, engage with community partners, and disseminate solutions. Builds on first semester MPH core courses.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPHG 711 or BIOS 600, SPHG 712 or EPID 600, SPHG 713; Pre- or corequisite, SPHG 721.

courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.description: This course serves as the Master's Thesis substitute course for the MPH program.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research Experience
courses.description: Supervised undergraduate directed research on communication science topics of mutual interest to the student and a faculty member.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.title: Autism in Our Communities: An Interdisciplinary Perspective
courses.description: Students have 30 hours of service-learning with individuals with autism at community partner sites. Class discussions introduce students to diverse topics related to autism spectrum disorder. This is an APPLES course.

courses.title: American Sign Language I
courses.description: This American Sign Language (ASL) course includes topics on linguistic features, cultural protocols, and core vocabulary for students to function in basic ASL conversations on a variety of topics. All instructions and discussions in the classroom will be conducted in ASL. Students minoring in Speech and Hearing Sciences have priority in registering.

courses.title: American Sign Language II
courses.description: Students in the Speech and Hearing Minor have priority in registering. The American Sign Language (ASL) course focuses on developing conversational skills on a variety of topics. All instructions and discussions in the classroom will be conducted in ASL.

courses.title: Introduction to Communication Disorders
courses.description: Introductory overview of communication disorders, including the nature of communication across the lifespan; cultural and linguistic issues that impact communication; communication modalities; speech disorders; language disorders; hearing disorders; swallowing disorders.

courses.title: Human Communication Across the Lifespan
courses.description: Development of human communication processes across the lifespan, including linguistic and cultural bases of communication.

courses.title: Human Communication Across the Lifespan (EE)
courses.description: Development of human communication processes across the lifespan, including linguistic and cultural bases of communication. Includes a minimum of 30 service hours related to human communication. 12 spaces reserved for Juniors in Speech and Hearing Sciences Minor.

courses.title: Introduction to Phonetics
courses.description: A detailed study of the International Phonetic Alphabet with emphasis on the sound system of American English. Application of phonetics to problems of pronunciation and articulation. Includes broad and narrow phonetic transcription.

courses.title: Speech Science
courses.description: Introduction to the science of speech, including production, acoustics, and perception.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech, Language, and Hearing Mechanisms
courses.description: Anatomy and physiology of the speech producing and aural mechanisms.

courses.title: Introductory Audiology I
courses.description: Theory and practice of the measurement of hearing, causative factors in hearing loss, evaluation of audiometric results, and demonstration of clinical procedures.

courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Practice in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
courses.description: Introduction to diagnosis and treatment of communication disorders, including articulation, fluency, voice, and language, and those resulting from autism and hearing loss.

courses.title: Introduction to Research in Speech and Hearing
courses.description: Required preparation, statistics course. Experimental and descriptive research designs in speech and hearing sciences, including both group and single subject.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum in Audiology
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Audiology which covers the breadth of the scope of practice. This course is taken multiple semesters throughout the AuD program.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Cochlear Implants: Foundations & Clinical Applications
courses.description: Examines fundamentals of cochlear implants, candidacy, evaluation, equipment, programming, and performance outcomes.

courses.title: Audiologic Assessment
courses.description: Clinical Audiology assessment including pure-tone audiometry, immittance measures, and other measures commonly employed in the standard diagnostic battery.

courses.title: Audiologic Assessment Lab
courses.description: Laboratory exercises in threshold determination, clinical masking and speech recognition testing, all concepts introduced in SPHS 710, Audiologic Assessment.

courses.title: Characteristics of Amplification Systems
courses.description: Amplification options for the hearing-impaired; specifically, hearing aid, electroacoustics, and earmold technologies. Additionally, hearing aid selection procedures are presented.

courses.title: Characteristics of Amplification Lab
courses.description: Laboratory activities related to earmolds, hearing aids, and ANSI electroacoustic verification.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Hearing
courses.description: This course will cover anatomy and physiology of the peripheral hearing system (outer, middle, and inner ear) as well as relevant central pathways.

courses.title: Professional Considerations in Speech and Hearing
courses.description: To provide the student with information about current issues facing professionals. Issues include changing delivery systems, leadership, treatment efficacy and quality, reimbursement, and ethics.

courses.title: Auditory Perception
courses.description: This course provides an overview of psychoacoustics - the psychology of hearing. Content includes introductory acoustics, normal sound perception, and the perceptual consequences of impaired hearing.

courses.title: Hearing Disorders
courses.description: Diseases and disorders of the auditory system and their management.

courses.title: Clinical Issues and Experiences in Audiology
courses.description: Online course in Year One, In-Person Course Years Two and Three, this course covers universal precautions, privacy regulations, report writing, clinical practice with diverse cultural groups, ethical considerations, coding and billing, and other aspects of audiology practice.

courses.title: Instrumentation and Calibration
courses.description: Principles of instrumentation relevant to clinical practice including study of electronics, filters, and analog and digital processing.

courses.title: Auditory Strategies for Spoken Language in Deaf Children
courses.description: Instruction and application of a variety of topics demonstrating the use of auditory techniques, and strategies to promote the use of spoken language in children with hearing loss.

courses.title: Principles of Prevention, Assessment, and Intervention in Speech-Pathology
courses.description: Principles and methods of prevention, assessment, and intervention for people with communication and swallowing disorders, including consideration of anatomical/physiological, psychological, developmental, and linguistic and cultural correlates of the disorders.

courses.title: Neuroanatomy
courses.description: A survey of neurological anatomy in relation to clinical speech-pathology and audiology. Topics include organization of the CNS, neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, and neurochemistry.

courses.title: Aphasia
courses.description: Discussion of adult aphasia and its clinical management, including assessment, diagnosis, prognosis, counseling, and treatment. Combined lectures and laboratories.

courses.title: Pediatric Speech Disorders
courses.description: Identification and differential diagnosis of delayed and disordered speech development; associated body structures and functions; intervention approaches focused on improving speech intelligibility, fluency, and participation in communication activities.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, SPHS 530; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Motor Speech Disorders
courses.description: Assessment and treatment of adults with disorders of motor speech control (i.e. dysarthria, anarthria, fluency, and apraxia of speech).

courses.title: Cognitive Communication Disorders Across the Lifespan
courses.description: An advanced course on cognitive bases of human communication and cognitive-communication disorders. Topics covered include theoretical models of cognitive communication across the lifespan, cognitive processes thought to underlie communication, and common clinical presentations of cognitive communication disorders associated with traumatic brain injury, right hemisphere injury, left hemisphere stroke and dementia. The goal of this course is to improve students abilities to apply theoretical models of communication and current research literature to assessment and practice. Restricted to: Speech-Language Pathology Graduate students in the MS-SLP program.

courses.title: Voice Disorders
courses.description: Assessment and management of a range of laryngeal and aerodigestive disorders across the lifespan. Students admitted to the Master of Science in Speech and Hearing Sciences/Speech-language pathology program only.

courses.title: Evaluation and Clinical Management of Persons with Oral-Facial Anomalies
courses.description: In-depth analysis of the embryologic and physiologic bases of oral-facial anomalies and the team approach to assessment and habilitation. Particular emphasis placed upon the following specialties: genetics, plastic surgery, prosthodontics, orthodontics, otolaryngology, and speech-language pathology.

courses.title: Global Issues and Practices in Communication Disorders
courses.description: Examination and discussion of issues related to international practices in communication sciences and disorders, including effective global engagement. Restricted to: MS/SLP Graduate students and advanced undergraduates in the Minor with permission of instructor.

courses.title: Seminar in Medical Speech Language Pathology
courses.description: Discussion of normal aging and language. Assessment and treatment of cognitive and linguistic problems in persons with dementing conditions, right hemisphere dysfunction, and traumatic brain injury.

courses.title: Dysphagia
courses.description: Discussion of the development of the normal swallow, anatomy and physiology of the swallowing mechanism, and assessment and team management of swallowing disorders.

courses.title: Neurologic Communication Disorders in Adults
courses.description: Overview of communication disorders commonly seen in adult populations. These include disorders of language, cognition, speech and motor control, voice, and fluency.

courses.title: Child Communication Disorders
courses.description: Disorders of child speech and language development, as a prerequisite for advanced specialized coursework and supervised clinical practicum.

courses.title: Language Impairments in School Age Children
courses.description: Assessment and intervention methods for receptive and expressive language (phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, prelinguistic communication, and paralinguistic communication) in speaking, listening, reading, and writing.

courses.title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication
courses.description: Introduction to Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) systems for individuals with complex communication impairments; processes involved in selecting, representing, and organizing vocabulary; strategies to support development of communicative competence in AAC.

courses.title: Supervised Clincal Experience in Speech-Language Pathology I
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology II
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology III
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology IV
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.

courses.title: Supervised Clinical Experience in Speech-Language Pathology V
courses.description: Supervised clinical experience in Speech-Language Pathology scope of practice.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Ethical Practice Policies and Guidelines
courses.description: Academic program accreditation standards; standards of ethical conduct; practice policies and guidelines; prevention of communication disorders; role of the speech-language pathologist.

courses.title: Contemporary Professional Issues in Education
courses.description: Principles and rules of the current ASHA Code of Ethics; technical reports, diagnostic and treatment reports; treatment plans, and professional correspondence.

courses.title: Professional Development In Person-Centered Care
courses.description: Program coordinator may give permission for students to take this course. Tenets of person- and family-centered care, consistent with recognized standards of ethical practice and in accordance with applicable state and federal laws. Includes discussion of barriers and facilitators that impact access to and utilization of speech-language pathology services in education and health care settings.

courses.title: Professional Practice Issues in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.description: Cultural competence; conflict management; effective clinical and professional interaction with clients/patients and relevant others.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Pediatric Dysphagia
courses.description: This course will cover content on the specialty area of pediatric dysphagia assessment and intervention. The course will cover normal development of feeding skills, explore underlying etiologies of feeding disorders, current methods and philosophies of providing evaluation and intervention, existing and ongoing research in these areas, and special populations such as infants with craniofacial anomalies.

courses.title: Problems in Speech and Hearing Sciences
courses.description: May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Audiologic Rehabilitation for Children
courses.description: Covers speech perception and the effects of hearing loss on perception and production of speech as background for understanding assessment and treatment, with an auditory-verbal emphasis. Pediatric assessment and amplification are reviewed.

courses.title: Audiologic Rehabilitation for Adults
courses.description: Theoretical bases and history of audiologic rehabilitation of adults. Also, practical approaches to assessment and therapeutic intervention are presented. The roles of assistive technology and family-based counseling are included.

courses.title: Seminar in Early Intervention
courses.description: Stages of communication development of children from birth to five years old; clinical issues related to the assessment tools and intervention and planning for children with disabilities and their families.

courses.title: Seminar in Audiologic Rehabilitation
courses.description: Audiologic rehabilitation including counseling, visual speech perception, auditory training, special needs of older adults and psychosocial aspects of hearing loss will be addressed. Review of technology to enhance communication included.

courses.title: Introduction to Cochlear Implants
courses.description: Introductory information regarding cochlear implant candidacy, an overview of implant components, the evaluation process, surgery, device programming, and initiation of post implantation therapy. Class meets three hours for five weeks.

courses.title: Pediatric Audiology
courses.description: Clinical procedures used in the identification and management of hearing loss in young children.

courses.title: Pediatric Amplification and Assistive Listening Devices
courses.description: This course covers prescriptive formulas, verification and fitting of hearing aids and FM systems, and suggested monitoring of progress when working with young children with hearing loss and their families.

courses.title: Fitting and Dispensing of Amplification Systems
courses.description: Theoretical and practical approaches to fitting amplification systems and the procedures for dispensing amplification systems to the hearing-impaired.

courses.title: Fitting and Dispensing of Amplification Lab
courses.description: Laboratory experiences related to the selection, programming, and fitting of amplification devices to hearing impaired individuals.

courses.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials I
courses.description: This course explores the field of auditory evoked responses. The primary focus is on responses from the auditory periphery including otoacoustic emissions (OAEs), electrocochleography (ECochG), and the auditory brainstem response (ABR).

courses.title: The Auditory Evoked Potentials I Lab
courses.description: Elecrophysiologic laboratory exercises to accompany Auditory Evoked Potentials I course.

courses.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials II
courses.description: The primary focus of this course is to cover auditory evoked potentials (Auditory Steady State Responses [ASSR] and Cortical Auditory Evoked Potentials [CAEP]) in addition to the ABR.

courses.title: Occupational and Community Audiology
courses.description: Military and industrial audiology and hearing conservation, including physiological and psychological factors.

courses.title: Balance Assessment and Rehabilitation
courses.description: Principles of vestibular function and dysfunction, clinical assessment, and management.

courses.title: Balance Assessment Lab
courses.description: Laboratory exercises to accompany Balance Assessment course. To include case history, bedside examination, and objective measurements.

courses.title: Educational Audiology
courses.description: Examines the provision of services to school-age children, with special focus on eligibility determination and assessment of central auditory perception.

courses.title: Business Management and Professional Issues
courses.description: Examine healthcare and business models that impact audiology practice. Personnel management, marketing, quality assurance, and service reimbursement for audiology practices will be covered.

courses.title: Audiology Grand Rounds
courses.description: Examines clinical cases from the perspective of presenting symptoms, test results, and clinical outcomes.

courses.title: Embryology and Genetics of Hearing and Deafness
courses.description: Genetics related to developing hearing and balance structures as well as syndromic and nonsyndromic hearing loss and deafness.

courses.title: Pharmacology & Tinnitus in Audiology Practice
courses.description: Advanced audiology course that provides fundamental knowledge about pharmacological mechanisms and their impact on hearing and balance, as well as evaluation and management of patients with persistent tinnitus.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: This course gives enrolled graduate students in the curriculum an opportunity to pursue research supervised by one or more faculty members, culminating in a written document or special project.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.title: Advanced Signal Processing
courses.description: This course will provide information regarding advanced signal processing utilized in digital amplification and cochlear implants.

courses.title: Speech Acoustics
courses.description: This course provides information on the fundamentals of speech production, including the acoustic characteristics of normal and disordered speech.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This is the foundation course in a series related to providing services to children with hearing loss. Six units focus on working with families, speech acoustics, audiological interpretation, instrumentation, foundations of speech and language, and early literacy.

courses.title: Counseling and Communication Disorders
courses.description: This course provides a broad overview of contemporary counseling issues in communication disorders. The impact of subject age, life course, and cultural background on interviewing and counseling is included.

courses.title: Audiology Interpretation and Hearing Technologies
courses.description: This course focuses on behavioral and physiologic assessment of hearing in children and how these measures are used in aural habilitation. Fundamentals of hearing instrument technology including the selection and fitting of hearing aids and cochlear implants are addressed.

courses.title: Aging and Communication Disorders
courses.description: This course focuses on medical, psychological, and social theories and aspects of aging as they relate to communication processes and disorders.

courses.title: Seminar in Speech-Language Pathology
courses.description: Special topics and significant literature in the field of speech pathology.

courses.title: Fluency Disorders
courses.description: Course participants will develop an understanding of evaluation and treatment of acquired and developmental fluency disorders in children and adults through lecture and hands-on practice.

courses.title: Language Disorders Encountered in Audiology
courses.description: Students will learn about four areas of language disorders affecting children and adults (receptive and expressive language disorders, communication modalities, social aspects of communication, and cognitive aspects of communication) through readings, posted videos, and online quizzes. This is an asynchronous online course.

courses.title: Speech Disorders Encountered in Audiology
courses.description: Students will learn about speech disorders (fluency, voice, articulation, and craniofacial anomalies) through readings, posted videos, and online quizzes. This is an online asynchronous course.

courses.title: Speech and Language Disorders Encountered in Audiology
courses.description: Students will select two topics from speech disorders (fluency, voice, articulation, and craniofacial anomalies) and two topics from language disorders (receptive and expressive language disorders, communication modalities, social aspects of communication, and cognitive aspects of communication). This is an online asynchronous course with readings, videos, and quizzes.

courses.title: Seminar in Language and Language Disorders
courses.description: Special topics and significant literature in the field of language and language disorders. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Listening and Spoken Language Development and Intervention
courses.description: The course focuses on typical development, impact of hearing loss on listening and spoken language acquisition, assessment, strategies/techniques, and intervention for children birth-5 years who are deaf/hard of hearing.

courses.title: Speech and Language Impairments of Children
courses.description: Seminar course exploring categorical classifications of young children and the impact of these categories on assessment and intervention. Common topics include autism, visual impairments, fragile X syndrome, and Down syndrome.

courses.title: Directed Research Experience
courses.description: Individual work by a student (supervised by faculty) to explore an area of interest in a research paper or guided research experience.

courses.title: Teaching and Supervision
courses.description: Course regarding teaching of skills and supervision of individuals conducting screening programs. Introduction to teaching and development of assessment tools provides a background for the teaching lab associated with this course.

courses.title: Autism Seminar
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to develop a familiarity and understanding of topics related to Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD). Issues related to characteristics, etiologies, theories, assessment, and intervention will be discussed.

courses.title: Seminar in Speech Science
courses.description: Advanced special topics and current research in speech science. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Autism and Other Developmental Disabilities in Children Who Are Deaf or Hard of Hearing I
courses.description: Students will acquire knowledge related to screening, diagnosis, and intervention for children who have autism and/or other developmental disabilities in addition to hearing loss.

courses.title: Autism and Other Developmental Disabilities in Children Who Are Deaf or Hard of Hearing II
courses.description: Students and faculty will examine challenges and solutions related to screening, diagnosis, and intervention for children who have autism and/or other developmental disabilities in addition to hearing loss.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: North Carolina Service Learning Trip
courses.description: Interdisciplinary learning experience focused on examining social determinants of health while performing service activities in collaboration with community partners.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.title: Autism Seminar
courses.description: Participants develop knowledge of the major neuropsychological theories of autism and methodological issues in autism research through reading and discussion of literature; participate in developing and presenting autism research projects individually or in groups.

courses.title: Literacy
courses.description: This course provides an overview of literacy development for children birth to eight years old. It will also address the impact of hearing loss on the development of literacy.

courses.title: Research Design
courses.description: Doctoral seminar that introduces the student to principles of quantitative research methodology.

courses.title: Seminar in Single Subject and Survey Research
courses.description: Doctoral student seminar that introduces the student to principles of single subject and survey research methodology.

courses.title: Research in the Context of the Evidence-Based Practice Movement in Early Intervention
courses.description: Overview of the evidence-based practice (EBP) movement in early intervention (EI), definitions of EBP, systems for appraising evidence quality, examination of evidence base for current practices in EI.

courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Decisions, Decisions, Decisions
courses.description: In this course, we will investigate the structure of these decision problems, show how they can be solved (at least in principle), and solve some simple problems.

courses.title: FYS: Networks: Degrees of Separation and Other Phenomena Relating to Connected Systems
courses.description: Networks, mathematical structures that are composed of nodes and a set of lines joining the nodes, are used to model a wide variety of familiar systems.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Adventures in Statistics
courses.description: This seminar aims to show that contrary to common belief, statistics can be exciting and fun. The seminar will consist of three modules: statistics in our lives, randomness, and principles of statistical reasoning.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Risk and Uncertainty in the Real World
courses.description: The aim of this class is to study the role of uncertainty in our daily lives, to explore the cognitive biases that impair us, and to understand how one uses quantitative models to make decisions under uncertainty in a wide array of fields including medicine, law, finance, and the sciences.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Art and Science of Decision Making in War and Peace
courses.description: This seminar will use recently assembled historical material to tell the exciting story of the origins and development of operations research during and after World War II.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Statistical Decision-Making Concepts
courses.description: We will study some basic statistical decision-making procedures and the errors and losses they lead to. We will analyze the effects of randomness on decision making using computer experimentation and physical experiments with real random mechanisms like dice, cards, and so on.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Statistics for Environmental Change
courses.description: Studies the Environmental Protection Agency's Criteria Document, mandated by the Clean Air Act; this document reviews current scientific evidence concerning airborne particulate matter. Students learn some of the statistical methods used to assess the connections between air pollution and mortality, and prepare reports on studies covered in the Criteria Document.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Probability and Paradoxes
courses.description: The theory of probability, which can be used to model the uncertainty and chance that exist in the real world, often leads to surprising conclusions and seeming paradoxes. We survey and study these, along with other paradoxes and puzzling situations arising in logic, mathematics, and human behavior.

courses.title: FYS: Statistics, Biostatistics, and Bioinformatics: An Introduction to the Ongoing Evolution
courses.description: This course is designed to emphasize the motivation, philosophy, and cultivation of statistical reasoning in the interdisciplinary areas of statistical science and bioinformatics.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: A Random Walk down Wall Street
courses.description: Introduces basic concepts in finance and economics, useful tools for collecting and summarizing financial data, and simple probability models for quantification of market uncertainty.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Visualizing Data
courses.description: This seminar looks at a variety of ways in which modern computational tools allow easy and informative viewing of data. Students will also study the kinds of choices that have to be made in data presentation and viewing.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Unlocking the Genetic Code
courses.description: Introduces students to the world of genetics and DNA and to the use of computers to organize and understand the complex systems associated with the structure and dynamics of DNA and heredity.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special Topics Course. Contents will vary each semester.

courses.title: Decision Models for Business and Economics
courses.description: An introduction to multivariable quantitative models in economics. Mathematical techniques for formulating and solving optimization and equilibrium problems will be developed, including elementary models under uncertainty.

courses.title: Reasoning with Data: Navigating a Quantitative World
courses.description: Students will use mathematical and statistical methods to address societal problems, make personal decisions, and reason critically about the world. Authentic contexts may include voting, health and risk, digital humanities, finance, and human behavior. This course does not count as credit towards the psychology or neuroscience majors.

courses.title: Foundations of Statistics and Data Science
courses.description: The course teaches critical concepts and skills in computer programming and statistical inference, in conjunction with hands-on analysis of real-world datasets, including economic data, document collections, geographical data, and social networks. It delves into social issues surrounding data analysis such as privacy and design. Honors version available.

courses.title: Introduction to Data Analysis
courses.description: Elementary introduction to statistical reasoning, including sampling, elementary probability, statistical inference, and data analysis. STOR 151 may not be taken for credit by students who have credit for ECON 400 or PSYC 210.

courses.title: Introduction to Data Models and Inference
courses.description: Data analysis; correlation and regression; sampling and experimental design; basic probability (random variables, expected values, normal and binomial distributions); hypothesis testing and confidence intervals for means, proportions, and regression parameters; use of spreadsheet software. Honors version available.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Examines selected topics from statistics and operations research. Course description is available from the department office.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Special Topics, FC-QUANT
courses.description: Examines selected topics from statistics and operations research.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Foundations of Decision Sciences
courses.description: Introduction to basic concepts and techniques of discrete mathematics with applications to business and social and physical sciences. Topics include logic, sets, functions, combinatorics, discrete probability, graphs, and networks.

courses.title: Mathematics for Data Science
courses.description: This course introduces students to some of the key mathematical tools underlying algorithmic data science. The primary focus of the course is matrix algebra and multivariable calculus. The mathematical topics covered in the course will be motivated and connected by concrete applications in data science, with an emphasis on machine learning and optimization.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Examines selected topics from statistics and operations research. Course description is available from the department office.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Learning Assistantship
courses.description: Experience includes preparations, demonstrations, assistance, and attendance at weekly meetings and lab sections. This course will enable you to deepen your understanding of topics in statistics and data science by learning the material with an eye toward explaining it to other less-experienced students, and; develop pedagogical skills, such as developing a rapport with learners, engaging in clear oral and written communication, and taking the perspective of less experienced students.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, STOR 120 grade of A- or higher.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 7 total credits. 7 total completions.

courses.title: Introduction to Decision Analytics
courses.description: Students cannot enroll in STOR 305 if they have already taken STOR 415. The use of mathematics to describe and analyze large-scale decision problems. Situations involving the allocation of resources, making decisions in a competitive environment, and dealing with uncertainty are modeled and solved using suitable software packages.

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics for Data Science
courses.description: The course gives a solid introduction to rigorous mathematical thinking and problem solving, all of which are fundamental in data science. It covers proofs, mathematical induction, counting, and the basics of graph theory.

courses.title: Methods and Models of Data Science
courses.description: Development of basic skill set for data analysis from obtaining data to data carpentry, exploration, modeling, and communication. Topics covered include regression, clustering, classification, algorithmic thinking, and non-standard data objects (networks and text data). Students may not receive credit for both STOR 320 and STOR 520.

courses.title: Ethics of Machine Learning in Society
courses.description: Modern Statistics and Machine Learning introduces several normative issues. Concerns surrounding algorithmic bias, data privacy, and methodological transparency arise from our methods, but our methods are not capable of fully ameliorating them. A more complete answer must be sought in moral philosophy. This course is positioned at the intersection of these disciplines. It will combine rigorous analysis of modern data sets alongside open-ended philosophical discussion. Students leaving this class will be able to defend when their methods are not only technically sound but morally just.

courses.title: Sample Survey Methodology
courses.description: Fundamental principles and methods of sampling populations, with emphasis on simple, random, stratified, and cluster sampling. Sample weights, nonsampling error, and analysis of data from complex designs are covered. Practical experience through participation in the design, execution, and analysis of a sampling project.
courses.requisites: Prerequisite, BIOS 650; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.title: Special Topics in Statistics and Operations Research
courses.description: Examines selected topics from statistics and operations research. Course description is available from the department office.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Special Topics, FC-VALUES
courses.description: Examines selected topics from statistics and operations research.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Introduction to Optimization
courses.description: Linear, integer, nonlinear, and dynamic programming, classical optimization problems, network theory. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, MATH 347 and STOR 315, 215, COMP 283 or MATH 381.

courses.title: Introduction to Probability
courses.description: Introduction to mathematical theory of probability covering random variables; moments; binomial, Poisson, normal and related distributions; generating functions; sums and sequences of random variables; and statistical applications. Students may not receive credit for both STOR 435 and STOR 535. Honors version available.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, MATH/STOR 235 or MATH 233; and STOR 215 or STOR 315 or MATH 381 or COMP 283.

courses.title: Stochastic Modeling
courses.description: Introduction to Markov chains, Poisson process, continuous-time Markov chains, renewal theory. Applications to queueing systems, inventory, and reliability, with emphasis on systems modeling, design, and control.

courses.title: Methods of Data Analysis
courses.description: Review of basic inference; two-sample comparisons; correlation; introduction to matrices; simple and multiple regression (including significance tests, diagnostics, variable selection); analysis of variance; use of statistical software. Honors version available.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Actuarial Mathematics
courses.description: This course focuses on an intensive study of foundations of short-term and long-term actuarial models, including loss modeling, pricing and reserving, mortality and life contingencies.

courses.title: Long-Term Actuarial Models
courses.description: Probability models for long-term insurance and pension systems that involve future contingent payments and failure-time random variables. Introduction to survival distributions and measures of interest and annuities-certain.

courses.title: Short Term Actuarial Models
courses.description: Short term probability models for potential losses and their applications to both traditional insurance systems and conventional business decisions. Introduction to stochastic process models of solvency requirements.

courses.title: Financial Mathematics for Actuarial Science
courses.description: This course develops the mathematical tools used to evaluate and manage financial transactions over time. Students will study interest theory, annuities, loan repayment schemes, and bond valuation, along with selected topics in risk management and derivative instruments. Emphasis is placed on modeling cash flows, analyzing investment projects, and understanding the principles that underlie pricing and reserving in insurance and finance. The course serves both as preparation for the SOA Exam FM and as a gateway to advanced actuarial coursework in life contingencies, financial economics, and asset-liability management.

courses.title: Healthcare Risk Analytics
courses.description: This course will introduce students to the healthcare industry and provide hands-on experience with key actuarial and analytical concepts that apply across the actuarial field. Using real world situations, the course will focus on how mathematics and the principles of risk management are used to help insurance companies and employers make better decisions regarding employee benefit insurance products and programs.

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Examines selected topics from statistics and operations research. Course description is available from the department office.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.title: Internship in Statistics and Operations Research
courses.description: Requires permission of the department. Statistics and analytics majors only. An opportunity to obtain credit for an internship related to statistics, operations research, or actuarial science. Pass/Fail only. Does not count toward the statistics and analytics major or minor.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Undergraduate Reading and Research in Statistics and Operations Research
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. This course is intended mainly for students working on honors projects. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeatRules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.title: Optimization for Machine Learning and Neural Networks
courses.description: This is an upper-level course focusing on optimization aspects of common and practical problems and topics in statistical learning, machine learning, neural networks, and modern AI. It covers several topics such as optimization perspective of linear regression, nonlinear regression, matrix factorization, stochastic gradient descent, regularization techniques, neural networks, deep learning techniques, and minimax models.
courses.requisites: Prerequisites, STOR 415 or STOR 612; or MATH 233 and MATH 347, or MATH 235, and COMP 110 or COMP 116; or permission of instructor.

courses.title: Statistical Computing for Data Science
courses.description: This course provides hands-on experience working with data sets provided in class and downloaded from certain public websites. Lectures cover basic topics such as R programming, visualization, data wrangling and cleaning, exploratory data analysis, web scraping, data merging, predictive modeling, and elements of machine learning. Programming analyses in more advanced areas of data science. Students may not receive credit for both STOR 320 and STOR 520.

courses.title: Probability for Data Science
courses.description: This course is an advanced undergraduate course in probability with the aim to give students the technical and computational tools for advanced courses in data analysis and machine learning. It covers random variables, moments, binomial, Poisson, normal and related distributions, generating functions, sums and sequences of random variables, statistical applications, Markov chains, multivariate normal and prediction analytics. Students may not receive credit for both STOR 435 and STOR 535.
